abstract: Surface waters, non-migrating rodents, plants, and soils are the most common proxies used for the establishment of strontium isotope isoscapes for archaeological investigations. Recent studies have cast doubt about the accuracy of these methods, notably regarding possible agricultural liming contamination on the 87Sr/86Sr ratio. As the exchangeable fraction of lake sediments emulates the chemical composition of water in which they are deposited, we posit that this fraction should be a better indicator of the evolution of past 87Sr/86Sr than modern proxies like surface waters or non-migrating rodent bones. The results from Holocene sediment cores from 12 Danish lakes show that both trace element concentration and 87Sr/86Sr change over time due to leaching of Ca, Sr, and Rb rich minerals out of the soils into the lakes. This temporal change could lead to inaccurate comparisons of the Sr isotopic compositions of the past to those of the modern day (MD). Well-dated lake sediments offer a unique opportunity for constructing spatiotemporal isoscapes for different time periods that can be used in archaeological studies, without the interference from anthropogenic sources.

title: Precipitation dominance in regulating the carbonate weathering carbon sink flux: Insights from a regionally calibrated GEM-CO 2 model
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 210 Author(s): Yuxia Hou, Fen Huang, Huan Liu, Chencong Li, Tongbin Zhu, Jianhua Cao, Qiong Xiao, Pei Wang, Bill Hu
abstract: Reliance on global parameterization impedes the accurate quantification of carbonate weathering carbon sink flux (CCSF), injecting significant uncertainty into regional carbon budgets. To resolve this, we developed a regionally calibrated GEM-CO2 model (CGEM-CO2 model) for the karst region of Guangxi, China. Constrained by local hydrochemical data, the CGEM-CO2 model yielded a calibrated parameter of 1.6313, achieving a robust fit with observations (R2 = 0.8459). Validation at the point scale confirmed that the calibrated model outperforms both the original GEM-CO2 and Maximal Potential Dissolution (MPD) models, particularly in resolving spatial heterogeneity. The model estimates a mean CCSF of 9.18 t C km−2 yr−1 for 2000–2022, revealing a distinct “V-shaped” temporal trend characterized by an initial decline and a post-2011 recovery, concentrated in northern Guangxi. Concurrently, a steady rise in equilibrium HCO3 − concentrations indicates an intensifying carbon sink potential, likely driven by soil CO2 enrichment. Geospatial analyses identified a “precipitation-dominant, multi-factor synergistic” mechanism driving the CCSF's spatial variability. Precipitation was identified as the primary positive driver, with its explanatory power significantly amplified through interactions with factors such as evapotranspiration and NDVI. These findings demonstrate that regional model calibration is critical for refining carbon budget assessments and elucidating the complex interplay of climatic and ecological drivers. This approach provides a robust framework for managing karst ecosystems in the context of carbon neutrality goals.

title: Assessment of groundwater pollution risks in a cold-temperate agricultural region and potential correlations with spectral indices of dissolved organic matter
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 210 Author(s): Mingyue Zhao, Zonghao Zhang, Chenghao Wu, Wei Zhao
abstract: Groundwater quality and dissolved organic matter (DOM) are important for water supply safety and human health. However, traditional monitoring is time consuming and costly, and the value of DOM spectral indices as rapid hydrogeochemical screening indicators in cold-temperate agricultural aquifers remains insufficiently understood. This study analyzed conventional water-quality indicators and DOM fluorescence components in 101 groundwater samples from Qitaihe City, northeastern China. Structural equation modeling (SEM) and redundancy analysis (RDA) were used to identify the spectral indices most strongly associated with conventional water-quality indicators. Zone-spectral indices based models were then developed to screen key groundwater-quality parameters, while random forest models compared relative groundwater-quality responses under different source-control scenarios. The results showed that ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N), nitrate (NO3 −), and iron (Fe) exceeded the relevant standards in 10, 16, and 11 samples, respectively, defining a compliant zone (S1), an NH3-N-NO3 - co-exceedance zone (S2), and an NH3-N-NO3 --Fe co-exceedance zone (S3). Four fluorescent components were resolved in each hydrochemical zone, with DOM fluorescence dominated by terrestrial and microbial humic-like substances. The fluorescence index (FI) was closely associated with NO3 − in S2 and with NH3-N and Fe in S3, indicating links among DOM transport, nitrogen transformation, and redox-sensitive Fe mobilization. Zone-specific FI-based models effectively captured variations in groundwater parameters in subsequent sampling campaigns, indicating strong validation performance. Random forest scenario assessment indicated that coordinated control of socioeconomic pressures, agricultural inputs, and wastewater discharge reduced relative groundwater-quality responses. This applied geochemical framework supports rapid screening, zoned monitoring, and source-control prioritization in cold-temperate aquifers.

title: Mineralogy and elemental geochemistry of coal seams from underground fire-affected Jharia coal fields: Environmental significance
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 210 Author(s): Sukalyan Chakraborty, Wasim Akram Shaikh, Robert Barry Finkelman, Abhishek Kumar, Naomi Ty Asha Nichols
abstract: Uncontrolled coal fires in the Jharia coalfield, India, are examples of one of the worst forms of anthropogenic pollution, as they introduce a broad range of geotoxic compounds into the environment. This study examined the occurrence and distribution of fluoride and heavy metals in fire-affected villages of the Jharia region in various environmental media - coal, soil, plants, condensates/sublimates, standing water, and foliar dust. The levels of fluoride were extraordinary, 411-622 mg kg-1 in coal, 166-147,333 mg kg−1 in condensates, 328-415 mg kg−1 in soils, and 134-150 mg L−1 in water samples-way above the normal levels found in the environment. Fe (up to 37,070 mg kg−1), and Zn (268-449 mg kg−1) were highly enriched, and Mn, Mg, Cr, Cu, and Pb were moderately enriched. Geo-statistical indices showed that there is extreme Fe pollution (Igeo = 6.44-7.43) and moderate Zn contamination (Igeo = 1.09-1.30), PLI value (1.59-2.23). The highest bioaccumulation factor (BAF) for fluoride was observed in Ageratum conyzoides (9.34) and Croton bonplandianum (5.47), indicating that they are potential accumulator. The results indicate that during combustion of coal, volatilized minerals, such as fluorapatite, contribute to extensive contamination of the atmosphere and soil in the immediate vicinity, posing a high ecological and human health risk, particularly in areas with high concentrations in the condensates. Further, the hazard quotients and hazard indices (HI) were <1, indicating no significant non-carcinogenic health risk under the assessed exposure conditions. In addition, the elevated carcinogenic risk was observed in some selected condensate samples. There should be continuous monitoring and remediation measures that will reduce fluoride and heavy metal exposure in this susceptible coal-mining area.

title: Enhanced stacking ensemble learning for predicting fluoride and iodine contamination in groundwater of the lower Yellow River floodplain, Northern China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 210 Author(s): Shishan Xing, Chuanshun Zhi, Xiaonong Hu, Wenbo Chang, Ruchun Wei, Yuxi Li, Hongnian Chen, Hongliang Li, Yulong Dong, Guangwei Wu, Wenwen Bi
abstract: Geogenic fluoride (F−) and iodine (I−) contamination in groundwater poses a persistent threat to public health and the sustainability of drinking-water supply systems, particularly in data-scarce regions where preventive management remains challenging. However, effective groundwater management is often constrained by fragmented monitoring networks and limited decision-support tools capable of translating complex environmental information into actionable risk guidance. In this study, we develop an explainable decision-support framework to support sustainable groundwater management by integrating enhanced stacking ensemble learning, SHAP-based interpretation, and self-organizing maps (SOM). Using 292 groundwater samples and 40 environmental predictors, exceedance probabilities of F− (≥1.0 mg/L) and I− (≥0.08 mg/L) were mapped across the lower Yellow River floodplain, Northern China. The optimized stacking models achieved high predictive performance, with AUC values of 0.94 for F− and 0.92 for I−. Spatial predictions reveal distinct yet overlapping high-risk belts, with 43% of the region exposed to elevated fluoride risk and 57% to iodine risk, indicating that nearly half of the floodplain faces long-term groundwater quality constraints. Feature attribution analysis demonstrates that hydrochemical conditions dominate contamination risk, while hydrogeology, sedimentary environment, climate, human activities and soil physicochemical properties further regulate spatial heterogeneity. SOM clustering further clarified the coupled effects of hydrogeological settings and geochemical processes on F− and I− enrichment. This study demonstrates how transparent and reproducible AI tools can enhance groundwater-quality prediction and guide sustainable water management in large alluvial plains and other data-scarce, hydrogeochemically complex regions.

title: Sorption of metals and metalloids in hydraulic fracturing flowback water to surficial sediments
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 210 Author(s): Sean P. Funk, Katherine N. Snihur, Konstantin von Gunten, Logan R. Swaren, Greg G. Goss, Daniel S. Alessi
abstract: The use of hydraulic fracturing techniques to liberate hydrocarbons from unconventional, tight formations, has increased in the past two decades. Of environmental concerns raised about the process, the potential impact of the wastewater recovered from these operations, called flowback water (FBW), is among the most discussed. FBW is a complex fluid, containing numerous inorganic and organic constituents, many of which may be highly mobile in the subsurface and can pose potential risks to near-surface ecosystems. Components of the fluid may interact with each other, either synergistically or antagonistically, resulting in varied sorption behavior, and furthermore, transient effects induced by groundwater flow may also impact these reactions. In this study, batch and column experiments were conducted using FBW (TDS 145,000 – 168,000 mg/L) and sediments collected from a region of hydraulic fracturing operations in west-central Alberta. In our batch experiments, we found that for many of the dissolved inorganic compounds (e.g. Sr, Cu, and Ni), sorption was depressed, likely a result of competition with other constituents within the fluid and the high ionic strength of the FBW. Column experiments were also conducted to address how groundwater flow may influence sorption, and it was found that some dissolved inorganic constituents (e.g. Sr, Li, and B) exhibited depressed sorption compared to the batch experiments. We argue that sorption is characterized by two stages: a fast adsorption phase onto external sorption sites, followed by a slow absorption phase into internal sorption sites, with the latter process negated by groundwater flow. However, metals exhibited enhanced retention in the presence of flow, possibly due to the anaerobic conditions in the column and precipitation of heavy metal-bearing solids sequestered these elements. Our results demonstrate the importance and need to consider both the full complexity found in real, field-collected FBW samples as well as groundwater flow, as co-contaminant interactions can have profound impact on the sorption behavior of individual solution components. Our results also suggest that many of the dissolved metals in FBW are likely highly mobile in the subsurface. This indicates that retention of these metals, even in high organic matter and high clay-content soils (which should act as a sink), is likely to be minimal, suggesting that if released into the environment, FBW may pose a risk to down-gradient ecosystems.

title: Hydrogeochemical and isotopic monitoring strategies for water resource sustainability: the Pordenone Plain (NE Italy)
description: Publication date: Available online 21 October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Dino Di Renzo, Luca Pizzino, Goran Vižintin, Carmela Vaccaro
abstract: This study investigates the seasonal hydrogeochemical dynamics of the Pordenone Plain hydrogeological system (NE Italy). Despite abundant water resources, the system faces increasing anthropogenic and climatic stress. A hydrogeochemical conceptual model was previously developed for this setting. Building on this foundation, the present study examines the processes governing seasonal groundwater dynamics, recharge variability, and the system's response to extreme hydroclimatic events. The results reveal marked seasonal variations among aquifers, reflecting hydro-lithological differences and providing a baseline for assessing aquifer resilience to future climate-driven recharge changes. The complex and heterogeneous intermediate flow system comprises two main flow paths. The first feeds foothill karst springs, responding rapidly to pre-Alpine/Alpine precipitation and snowmelt but experiencing reduced discharge during dry periods. The second flow path recharges the alluvial plain aquifers. High and Low Plain aquifers contrast, separated by the resurgence belt, a marked permeability transition. High Plain aquifers exhibit seasonal variations closely linked to piezometric fluctuations, whereas Low Plain aquifers display an inverted seasonal pattern. This inversion reflects the permeability contrast along the resurgence belt, which is inferred to decrease groundwater flow velocities and induce a "delayed seasonal recharge response". Conversely, the deep flow system remains unaffected by surface variations, indicating that deep confined aquifers are effectively decoupled from shallow hydrogeological dynamics. This integrated geochemical and isotopic approach enables the characterization of aquifer vulnerability and seasonal recharge dynamics. When integrated with quantitative hydrological assessments, these findings support the development of comprehensive management strategies to prevent water quality degradation and promote long-term groundwater sustainability.

title: Corrigendum to “Geochemical divergence of oxygen and sulfur compounds in high-maturity bitumen: Implications for thermal maturity assessment” [Appl. Geochem. 207 (2026) 106965]
description: Publication date: Available online 14 October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Chi Zhang, Quanyou Liu, Huiyuan Xu, Pengpeng Li, Dongya Zhu, Biqing Zhu

title: Experimental study on the contribution of microbial-induced carbonate precipitation to carbon sequestration in soil from the northern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
description: Publication date: Available online 9 October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Lingjie Huang, Xuelin Li, Shuang Li, Xuefen Sheng, Xinyuan Guo, Baitang Li, Ruoyu Hu, Fuchun Li
abstract: Soil inorganic carbon (SIC) plays a critical role in global carbon cycling; however, the contribution of microbial-induced carbonate minerals (CMs) to the SIC pool remains poorly explored. There is no definitive method for distinguishing between microbial-induced and chemical CMs in soil nor a calculation of the ratio between the two. To fill this gap, a soil profile at a depth of 110 cm, located in the alpine grassland of the northern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), was examined. Incubation experiments were conducted using mixed microbes isolated from soil. Our analysis encompassed vertical variation along the profile in soil organic carbon (SOC), SIC, and Ca2+, as well as the carbon isotopic composition (δ13C) of CMs, dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and SOC. X-ray diffraction and field-emission scanning electron microscopy equipped with energy-dispersive analysis were used to characterise the CMs in the soil. The close negative correlation between microbial biomass and δ13CCMs in both soil samples and incubation experiments suggests that soil microorganisms actively participate in CM formation. To quantify the proportion of microbial-induced CMs in soil, we established an empirical relationship between δ13Ccalcite and δ13CCO2(g) through incubation experimencts. This relationship allowed us to estimate the δ13C of the microbial-induced CMs (δ13CMCMs) using the δ13CCO2(g). Thereby, the calculated average δ13CCO2(g) for the upper soil layer was −36.2‰, corresponding to an estimated δ13CMCMs value of −26.5‰. Based on the above δ13CCMs, the estimated proportion of microbial-induced CMs in the total CM content is calculated, ranging from 43.7% to 4.0% with depth. Consequently, microbial-induced CMs are estimated to contribute approximately 20.2% to the SIC pool within the upper 1-m soil profile at Laohugou. These findings provide a novel framework for quantifying the contribution of microbially induced carbonate minerals to SIC sequestration using carbon isotopes. They highlight a pathway for transferring soil-derived CO2 into relatively stable inorganic carbon pools, with implications for understanding carbon cycling under changing environmental conditions.

title: Arc duration and crustal thickness strongly influence the amount of zircon-bearing felsic crust and zircon volume in arc crust
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Paul Sotiriou
abstract: It has been proposed that arc duration and crustal thickness control the compositions of lavas erupted at active arcs, however, little is known about the relationship between the crustal thickness and duration of arcs and how these relate to the amount of zircon-bearing intermediate to felsic crust in arcs and the volume of zircon in arc crust. In this contribution, data were compiled on the duration, crustal thickness, chemical structure and lava and plutonic geochemical compositions of active and fossil arcs to better constrain the relationship between arc duration, crustal thickness and the amount of zircon-bearing intermediate to felsic crust and volume of zircon in arc crust. Longer-lived, thicker arcs have thicker intermediate to felsic plutonic sections than shorter-lived, thinner arcs. Thicker, longer-lived arcs (Kohistan, Gangdese) that were thickened during mid-crustal growth have greater proportions of intermediate to felsic crust than thinner, shorter-lived arcs (Talkeetna). The longer-lived, thicker Kohistan (115 Ma: 55 km) and Gangdese (200 Ma; 60 km) arcs contain up to an order of magnitude more zircon by volume (11.7 and 4.8 km3 of zircon per kilometre length of arc) compared to the shorter-lived, thinner Talkeetna Arc (35 km; 77 Ma; 1.17 km3/km). There are higher volumes of zircon-bearing felsic crust in the longer-lived, thicker Gangdese (233 km3 of zircon-bearing felsic crust per kilometre length of arc) and Kohistan (255 km3/km) arcs than the shorter-lived, thinner Talkeetna Arc (139 km3/km). Arc duration and crustal thickness strongly influence the amount of zircon-bearing intermediate to felsic crust in arcs and the volume of zircon in arc crust.

title: Dissolved inorganic carbon sources and CO 2 budgets in a permafrost-dominated catchment: Insights from stable carbon isotopes
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Zhou Huiling, Li Zongxing, Bai Ronglong, Wang Yunying, Xue Jian
abstract: As Earth's largest low-latitude permafrost domain, the Tibetan Plateau exerts a pivotal control on global carbon cycling. Nevertheless, lateral export of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) and the resulting catchment-scale CO₂ balance in permafrost-dominated watersheds remain poorly quantified and understood. Here, we investigated DIC sources and seasonal CO₂ dynamics in the permafrost-impacted headwater catchment of the Shaliu River in the southern Qilian Mountains across the thaw seasons of two consecutive years (2021−2022). The results revealed that riverine DIC concentrations varied from 5.36 to 42.00 mg C L−1, with δ13C-DIC values spanning −10.66 ‰ to 1.68 ‰. MixSIAR modeling indicated that sulfuric acid-mediated carbonate weathering served as the predominant DIC source across the Shaliu River watershed. The contribution of this pathway in the permafrost-dominated upper and middle reaches ranged from 44% to 89%, which was 2–3 times greater than that in the lower reaches (18%–52%). The LOADEST model yielded annual DIC fluxes of 13.45–29.91 Gg yr−1, with 95% confidence intervals ranging approximately from −25% to +32%. Nearly 80% of the annual DIC export was delivered during the peak thaw season. Net CO₂ budget estimation further indicated that CO₂ emission derived from sulfide-induced carbonate dissolution (8.13 Gg yr−1) considerably surpassed the total CO₂ consumption via silicate weathering and carbonation-driven carbonate weathering (4.10 Gg yr−1) during the thaw period. This finding suggests that chemical weathering within the catchment functions as a net atmospheric CO₂ source. This carbon-source effect was most pronounced in permafrost regions. These findings suggest that permafrost thaw may promote sulfide oxidation, thereby enhancing DIC production and lateral export and shifting the weathering carbon budget toward a net CO₂ source. This sulfur-mediated weathering pathway may represent an underappreciated mechanism influencing inorganic carbon budgets in alpine permafrost catchments.

title: Chert as a recorder of diagenesis and paleoredox: Insights from the Early Silurian, SW Yangtze, China
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Yan Zhang, Haifeng Fan
abstract: Chert is a valuable archive for reconstructing paleo-ocean environments, such as the silicon cycle and seawater temperature, via Si and O isotopes. However, paleo-ocean redox conditions derived from redox-sensitive trace metals (RSMs) in chert remain underexplored relative to shale, and the processes governing secondary RSM enrichment into polymetallic complexes and sulfides via diagenetic metal redistribution remain poorly constrained. Additionally, diagenetic temperatures, particularly for megaquartz, are inadequately defined. To address the redox issue, we compiled existing chert and iron speciation data and integrated new analyses from 30 Early Silurian polygenetic cherts. Using iron speciation as a robust paleoredox constraint, we evaluated whether Ce anomalies and RSM-based indices in chert reliably record redox states. Our results indicate that Ce anomalies are reliable, whereas shale-based RSM redox proxies cannot be directly transferred and require recalibration. Under anoxic conditions, primary C-chert yields UEF = 255–401 and MoEF = 566–1456, while diagenetically overprinted S-limestone yields UEF = 132–1466 and MoEF = 355–732, reflecting diagenetic U–Mo decoupling. To constrain diagenetic temperature and RSM enrichment, we applied Raman spectroscopy of organic matter and δ 18Ochert thermometry to samples preserving petrographic evidence for megaquartz initiation. Megaquartz formation temperatures are 150–298/300 °C. SEM observations further reveal that RSMs subsequently concentrated as anhedral polymetallic complexes (U, V, As) and euhedral polymetallic and/or monometallic sulfides (Mo, Ni, Zn, V) surrounded by organic matter derived from photosynthetic organisms (δ 13Corg) following deposition. Organic matter-hosted Mo and Ni were later transferred into sulfides. This study demonstrates chert’s potential for reconstructing redox conditions and understanding RSM enrichment mechanisms.

title: Mercury isotopes quantify demethylation pathways mitigating methylmercury accumulation in rice via paddy water
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Kun Zhang, Yurong Liu, Liufeng Liao, Qiang Pu, Jiang Liu, Bo Meng, Xinbin Feng
abstract: Dietary methylmercury (MeHg) exposure via rice consumption poses a significant global health concern. Photo-demethylation and microbial demethylation are key MeHg removal processes in paddy overlying water, yet their Hg isotope fractionation fingerprints remain unclear, preventing quantitative assessment of their relative contributions to mitigating MeHg accumulation in rice. This study establishes Hg isotopic fingerprints for photo-demethylation (ε 202Hg = −2.36 ± 0.26‰, E 199Hg = −4.23 ± 0.36‰), microbial demethylation (ε 202Hg = −1.04 ± 0.20‰, E 199Hg ≈ 0), and their combined processes (ε 202Hg = −2.09 ± 0.19‰, E 199Hg = −3.11 ± 0.38‰) under environmentally relevant conditions. These values differ from those reported for other pure cultures and for freshwater photo-demethylation. Isotopic mixing modeling reveals that photo-demethylation dominates the removal of MeHg (73.6 ± 6.3%), comparable to estimates from lakes and the open ocean, and reduces overall MeHg enrichment in rice grains by 20.6 ± 6.9%. These findings reveal that photo-demethylation consistently dominates MeHg removal across diverse aquatic systems, highlighting the need to determine fractionation factors under environmentally relevant conditions. Overall, this study provides the first quantitative constraints on demethylation pathways in paddy overlying water using Hg isotopes, and advances the understanding of Hg cycling in rice paddy ecosystem.

title: Combined stable isotope systematics and thermodynamic models: Constraints on hydrothermal alteration prior to phreatic eruptions at Te Maari, Tongariro, New Zealand
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Rachelle Sanchez, Gabor Kereszturi, Antonio M. Álvarez-Valero, Geoff Kilgour, Agnes Mazot, Georg F. Zellmer
abstract: Hydrothermal systems hosted on active volcanoes exhibit complex interactions of magmatic heat and fluids, which facilitate changes to host rock physical and chemical properties. These resulting changes from hydrothermal alteration often lead to a decrease in flank stability, enhance sealing of the degassing conduit, and modulate eruption dynamics. However, the timescales of these processes are not well constrained. This study utilizes new stable isotope systematics (S, O, and H) and thermodynamic models of fresh and altered samples from the Te Maari vent, Tongariro volcano, New Zealand, to constrain a maximum timescale over which the observed secondary mineralogy formed as well as refine the physiochemical conditions of their formation. Tongariro hosts a complex multivent hydrothermal system with the most recent phreatic eruptions occurring at the Upper Te Maari crater in 2012. The δ 34 S S O 4 values of alunite from Te Maari are near 0 (−0.7 to 2.7‰), suggesting very limited SO 4 2 − -H2S exchange. Elevated δ 18 O a l u n ( S O 4 ) (15.85 to 19.35‰) values indicate SO 4 2 − exchange with high-18O water, typical of low temperature, low pH fumarole environments. Thermodynamic models of the alteration observed at Te Maari yielded refined physicochemical conditions of pH 1.25 to 2.53. Stable isotope fractionation calculations indicate temperature ranges of 100–150 °C, which is supported by Te Maari field measurements. Experimental equilibrium calculations returned a maximum time frame of 10 years to 200 days to reach 90% equilibrium for temperatures of 100 °C and 150 °C, respectively. These timescales indicate that alteration-induced conduit-sealing mineralization at Te Maari prior to the 2012 eruptions progressed quite rapidly.

title: Deep carbon input and shallow decoupling in Tibetan geothermal gases revealed by a C He isotope consistency framework
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Sanyu Quan, Qinghai Guo
abstract: Geothermal gases constrain deep carbon release in active continental collision zones, but measured CO2/3He and carbon isotope signatures can be modified during crustal transport and shallow hydrothermal circulation. We compile 612 geothermal gas samples from 308 hot spring sites across the Tibetan Plateau and develop a CHe isotope consistency framework to distinguish deep volatile input signals from shallowly modified compositions. A CHe mixing model predicts the CO2/3He ratio expected from deep crust-mantle volatile mixing. A consistency parameter, K, compares predicted and observed CO2/3He ratios and classifies samples by the direction and magnitude of CHe decoupling. 63 samples (10%) are classified as Class A and interpreted as least-modified approximations of the deep CHe baseline. Lower observed than predicted CO2/3He ratios indicate negative CHe offsets caused by CO2 removal and/or radiogenic He enrichment, whereas higher observed ratios indicate positive offsets related to shallow CO2 addition, He depletion, and/or crustal volatile re-equilibration. Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation confirms that the classification is mathematically robust in terms of sample assignability under given analytical uncertainties. But, this statistical stability does not independently verify the specific modification mechanisms inferred for each class. Bearing this caveat in mind, the observed CHe distribution patterns are most parsimoniously interpreted as reflecting multi-stage modification of deep volatile signals, although we cannot uniquely exclude the possibility that source heterogeneity or unaccounted shallow processes contribute to part of the variability. He-derived flux estimates show that measured CO2/3He can misestimate deep carbon input depending on the direction of CHe decoupling. Plain Language Summary Geothermal gases from hot springs can carry information about fluids and carbon released from deep within Earth. However, these gases may be strongly changed as they rise toward the surface, for example by dissolution in groundwater, addition of crustal helium, or loss of carbon dioxide. This study compiles 612 geothermal gas samples from 308 hot-spring sites across the Tibetan Plateau and develops a carbon‑helium isotope framework to test whether measured gas compositions are still consistent with deep sources. The method compares the measured CO2/3He ratio with a predicted value based on helium and carbon isotope constraints. A consistency parameter, K, is then used to classify samples according to the magnitude and direction of their deviation from the predicted deep baseline. Only 63 samples, or 10% of the dataset, show strong internal consistency and are considered candidate least-modified samples. These results suggest that most Tibetan geothermal gases have been modified by shallow processes, and that using all samples without screening could bias estimates of deep carbon release and mantle volatile fluxes.

title: Boric acid dissociation behavior in freshwater and marine conditions
description: Publication date: 5 January 2027 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 727 Author(s): Macarena Martín-Mayor, Robert H. Byrne
abstract: The dissociation constant of boric acid (pK B) is fundamental to marine carbonate system calculations and to boron isotope (δ11B) proxy reconstructions of seawater pH, yet available parameterizations remain limited in salinity coverage and have not been revisited using modern methodology. Here we present a novel characterization of pK B developed in natural seawater, derived from spectrophotometrically calibrated electrode pH measurements spanning salinities from 0 to 45.9 and temperatures between 275.15 and 308.15 K. It is the only pK B parameterization that includes experimental data obtained between salinities 0 and 5. This is particularly important given that nearly half the total variation in pK B across the full salinity range occurs within the narrow freshwater-to-brackish transition. For salinities above 5, our results are in excellent agreement with previous parameterizations obtained in synthetic seawater, confirming consistency while extending coverage to previously uncharacterized conditions. Uncertainties in pK B are small across the full temperature and salinity range and are therefore unlikely to contribute to differences between measured and calculated total seawater alkalinity that are typical for open-ocean seawater. This improved parameterization of pK B benefits carbonate system calculations and boron isotope proxy applications across the full range of estuarine to open-ocean environments.

title: Magmatic water and Fe-Ti oxide mineralization in the Wajilitag intrusion, Tarim large Igneous Province
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Huan Chen, Jia-Min Zhong, Yao Bi, Mo-Qi Wu, Qun-Ke Xia
abstract: Fe-Ti oxide deposits represent important global resources of titanium and vanadium, yet the factors controlling their formation remain debated. Here we investigate the role of magmatic water in Fe-Ti oxide mineralization using clinopyroxene-hosted hydrogen concentrations from the Wajilitag Fe-Ti oxide-bearing intrusion in the Tarim Large Igneous Province. Early-crystallized clinopyroxene with Mg# > 80 records approximately 1.3–2.3 wt% H₂O in the early-stage melts with which it equilibrated. Samples at the high-Ti/Y end of the dataset are also characterized by relatively high H₂O/Ce ratios, indicating an association between magmatic water and Fe-Ti oxide enrichment in the Wajilitag intrusion. Previous experimental and modeling studies show that dissolved H₂O depresses the liquidus temperatures of major silicate minerals and may allow Fe-Ti oxides to reach saturation earlier relative to these silicate phases. In light of these previous studies, our observations suggest that elevated magmatic water contents may have contributed to Fe-Ti oxide enrichment at Wajilitag by modifying the crystallization sequence.

title: Copper isotope variations in loess-paleosol sequences: Insights into paleo-redox processes and average composition of East Asian dust
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Guodong Ming, Maoyong He, Yingzeng Gong, Hong Wang, Peixian Shu, Huimin Yu, Shubin Fang, Fang Huang
abstract: Copper (Cu) is both an essential nutrient and a potential toxin, with dust from East Asia playing a major role in its worldwide distribution. Understanding the average isotopic composition of Cu (δ65Cu, SRM-976) in this dust is important for tracking its sources and understanding its biogeochemical cycling. However, current estimates are limited by sparse data and complications arising from post-depositional processes. Loess—thick deposits of windblown dust—serves as a key archive for tracing dust-borne copper in East Asia. In this study, we analyzed loess samples from several major dust deposits in China to investigate how δ65Cu varies and what influences these changes. Our experiments show that most Cu in these dust deposits is associated with FeMn oxides (73% on average), which dictates bulk δ65Cu (Δ65CuFe-Mn oxides – bulk averages −0.02‰). Organic matter also plays a role, holding Cu with heavier isotopic signatures (Δ65Cuorganic matter – bulk averages 0.33‰), while carbonates have little effect. We found that both particle size and weathering processes, including redox-driven sulphide cycling, can influence δ65Cu. But overall, bulk values remain tightly clustered (−0.04‰ to 0.17‰, 0.05 ± 0.09‰ on average, 2SD), slightly lower than the established value of Upper Continental Crust (UCC, 0.08 ± 0.20‰, n = 329), likely due to low Cu solubility in alkaline settings and minimal influence from post-depositional weathering. Based on our analysis of 61 loess samples, we propose an average δ65Cu value of 0.05 ± 0.09‰ for East Asian dust. This well-constrained value advances the application of Cu isotopes as geochemical and paleoenvironmental tracers.

title: Fluid sources and structural controls of the Pescadores fumarole, Gulf of California Extensional Province, Mexico
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Ivan Barea-Pérez, Claudio Inguaggiato, Loïc Peiffer, John Mackrain Fletcher, Agnes Mazot, Franco Tassi
abstract: This study presents the first geochemical and isotopic characterization of a fumarole at the southern tip of the Pescadores fault (Baja California, Mexico). The fumarole was activated following the Mw 7.2 El Mayor-Cucapah earthquake of April 2010. Gas samples were collected and vent temperature was measured (99.7 °C) during two field campaigns in 2022 and 2023. The principal objectives of this study are to investigate the origin of the fumarolic fluids and evaluate their link to the regional tectonic setting and other thermal fluids across the Baja California rift. The fumarole fluids are essentially from crustal origin, steam-dominated and CO2 as the principal dry gas. The relative abundances of N2, He, and Ar are characteristic of geothermal fluids in divergent and intraplate tectonic settings. The origin of helium is crustal-dominated (0.45 and 0.53 Rc/Ra) with a mantle-derived contribution of up to 6.36%. The δ13CCO2 values (−7.8‰ vs. V-PDB) and CO2/3He ratios (4.82 × 1010 - 9.29 × 1010) suggest that most of the CO2 was generated by decarbonation of carbonate rocks and thermal degradation of organic-rich sediments, with a minor mantle contribution. Likewise, the δ13CCH4 (−31.80‰ to −30.70‰ vs. V-PDB) and δDCH4 (−177.0‰ vs. V-SMOW) values are consistent with a thermogenic origin of methane. The magma aging model reveals lower R/Ra values than those measured in fumarole fluids, which allows us to infer some contribution of mantle-derived fluids ascending through the Pescadores and the intersecting “Unnamed Keystone” faults.

title: Indium enrichment revealed by sphalerite geochemistry and ab initio simulations in the Mengya'a skarn Zn-Pb-In deposit, Tibet
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Jingying Bian, Xiaojia Jiang, Jing Xu, Xin Chen, Xiufang Lei, Yimin Kang, Hao Chen, Youye Zheng
abstract: Although skarn polymetallic systems represent major global reservoirs of the critical metal indium (In), the enrichment mechanisms and fluid evolution in distal skarn systems remain poorly constrained. This study presents an investigation into three principal sphalerite types (SpI-SpIII) from the Mengya'a deposit by integrating in situ geochemistry, SPb isotopes, and ab initio simulations. The results demonstrate that In incorporation into sphalerite is primarily facilitated by CuIn coupled substitution (Cu+ + In3+ ↔ 2Zn2+), with subordinate participation of Sn and additional regulation by Cd-related lattice strain. Ab initio simulations further demonstrate that substitution configurations involving In, Sn, Cu, Cd, and Fe exert different influences on lattice strain and formation energy, providing a crystal-chemical constraint on In incorporation. Consequently, sphalerite records a fluid cooling evolution driven by wall-rock buffering and meteoric water influx: SpIa formed at ∼500 °C under moderate to high fS₂ conditions favorable for In enrichment (up to 300 ppm); SpIb-SpII precipitated during 380 to 290 °C, with SpII attaining peak In concentrations (up to 744.97 ppm); whereas SpIII formed at <250 °C and low fS₂, where stable In incorporation was inhibited (0.4 ppm). Ore-forming sulfur was predominantly magmatic (δ34S of −2.5‰ to +3.9‰), whereas metals show an upper-crustal affinity (206Pb/204Pb = 18.660–18.830), suggesting that the Zn-Pb-In mineralization was related to a crust-derived magmatic-hydrothermal system. Integrating atomistic simulations with fluid evolution reveals the mechanisms of critical-metal enrichment in distal skarn systems and establishes sphalerite as a key recorder of fluid evolution.

title: Insights into the long-term preservation of buried marine cadmium derived from micro-scale observations of Cd distribution and speciation in organic-rich shales
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Hannah C. Elms, Anthony Chappaz, Olivier Mathon, Tobias Salge, Alexander J. Dickson
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a nutrient-like trace metal whose burial in marine sediments influences both the long-term (103–104 yr) oceanic Cd mass balance and the interpretation of Cd-based paleoceanographic records. However, the sedimentary host phases that preserve Cd in the rock record remain poorly constrained. Here, we present the first direct micro-scale observations of Cd distribution and speciation in organic-rich marine shales from the Cape Verde basin (Hatteras Fm, ∼94 Ma) and the North Sea basin (Sele Fm, ∼56 Ma). Synchrotron micro-X-ray fluorescence (μXRF) maps show heterogeneous Cd distributions, ranging from diffuse matrix-bound Cd to discrete Cd-rich hotspots, but no consistent spatial association between Cd and Fe-rich phases, indicating that pyrite is not a major repository for Cd in these samples. Cadmium K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy and linear combination fitting show that Cd is dominated by cadmium sulfide (CdS), which accounts for 33–100% of the Cd in analysed spots; Cd sulfate forms most of the remainder, with minor Cd carbonate in one non-sulfidic sample. We interpret Cd sulfate chiefly as a secondary oxidation product of originally-reduced Cd sulfide, and infer that CdS is the dominant long-term burial phase under euxinic to anoxic conditions. These results indicate that ancient Cd records may reflect diagenetic redistribution and stabilisation in sulfide phases rather than the full diversity of initial Cd host phases buried at the seafloor. Direct speciation constraints are therefore essential for linking sedimentary Cd enrichments and Cd isotope records to marine redox conditions, productivity, and the long-term oceanic Cd cycle. Synopsis The burial of cadmium in marine sediments is a primary control on the global cycle of this important trace metal. Using micro-imaging and X-ray speciation techniques, we show that ancient marine sedimentary deposits are likely dominated by cadmium sulfide.

title: Testing the chromium isotope redox proxy in a South China Permian-Triassic succession: Validation and limitations
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Yuqiu Wei, Anping Hu, Thomas J. Algeo, Qiankun Hu, Anjiang Shen, Feng Liang, Hao Li, Lanping Feng, Lian Zhou
abstract: Chromium (Cr) stable isotopes have emerged as a powerful redox proxy for reconstructing the Earth's oxygenation history. Marine carbonates serve as an important archive of sedimentary Cr-isotopic data, providing critical insights for tracing changes in paleo-oceanic redox conditions. However, whether the δ53Cr values of carbonates can faithfully record the information of ambient seawater at the time of deposition remains a subject of debate. To further evaluate the potential of this proxy, we present a high-resolution Cr-isotope (δ53Cr) record for both the bulk rock and authigenic Cr fractions in a carbonate succession spanning the Permian-Triassic Boundary (PTB) at Meishan, a classic shallow-water section in South China. We show that the bulk-rock and authigenic Cr and δ53Cr profiles exhibit not only consistent stratigraphic trends but also synchronous abrupt shifts. These observations are consistent with control of δ53Cr variation by contemporaneous changes in the redox state of the oceanic water column. Due to the influence of widespread anoxic conditions in the latest Permian ocean, the reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) in seawater was significantly enhanced. This process drove a kinetic fractionation of Cr isotopes in the pre-extinction Upper Permian interval, yielding significantly positive δ53Cr values (δ53Crbulk: +1.24 ± 0.55 ‰, 2SD; δ53Crauth: +1.86 ± 0.21 ‰, 2SD), which is markedly higher than the δ53Cr compositions of Phanerozoic marine carbonates. In contrast, owing to a rapid expansion of oceanic anoxia during the PTB crisis interval, seawater Cr(VI) was quantitatively reduced and sequestered in the eastern Paleotethys, leading to a sharp negative excursion in δ53Cr values (δ53Crbulk: +0.08 ± 0.60 ‰, 2SD; δ53Crauth: –0.06 ± 0.24 ‰, 2SD). A two-endmember mixing model suggests that the pronounced negative shift in the clay-rich boundary horizon (Bed 26) may, in part, record detrital Cr inputs associated with intensified continental weathering. Based on a comprehensive multifactor evaluation, the Meishan δ53Cr records demonstrate the suitability of Cr isotopes as a robust proxy for tracking geological changes in ocean-redox conditions subject to certain limitations.

title: Common controls on Na and Sr in modern and fossil brachiopod shells: Long-term stability of biomineralisation and use for seawater Sr/Ca reconstruction
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Clemens V. Ullmann, Carsten Lüter, Luís Vítor Duarte, Benito Andrade, Emma Court, Trevor Bailey, Martin Aberhan
abstract: Robust reconstructions of element cycles are important for a quantitative understanding of the evolution of the Earth system. Fossil shells of marine macroinvertebrates are abundant and constitute valuable archives of past environmental conditions, which can be tied into precise chronostratigraphic schemes. However, complex, species-specific biomineralisation influences on the expression of geochemical proxies in their shells hinder their use for the reconstruction of seawater chemistry. Here, we investigate the variability and co-variation of element/Ca ratios in the shells of modern and Early Jurassic brachiopods belonging to the orders Rhynchonellida, Terebratulida, and Thecideida. We show that within modern and fossil brachiopods of the orders Rhynchonellida and Terebratulida, shells display uniform and strong co-variation of strontium and sodium content. This co-variation is offset and less well expressed in the thecideide Pajaudina atlantica. The coupling of Na/Ca and Sr/Ca in shells of low-Mg calcite secreting taxa can be explained by joint controls on both elements. The comparability of the NaSr co-variation in modern and fossil examples suggests that biological controls on the uptake of these elements in Rhynchonellida and Terebratulida have remained essentially unaltered since at least the Early Jurassic. The Sr/Ca ratio of past seawater can be calculated using a Na-corrected Sr distribution coefficient of 0.051 established from modern terebratulide and rhynchonellide brachiopods. Based on this calibration, late Pliensbachian - late Toarcian (c. 185–175 Ma) seawater Sr/Ca ratios of 8.8 mmol/mol to 10.3 mmol/mol with uncertainties of 2 to 15% (95% confidence) are reconstructed.

title: Controls of Fe Mn cycling on polymetallic enrichment in Early Cambrian black shales: Evidence from the Huanglongshan manganese deposit, South China
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Wan'er Wang, Zerui Ray Liu, Xiyao Li, Zhengwei Qin, Zhen Yang, Chenglin Liu, Mei-Fu Zhou
abstract: Early Cambrian black shales contain exceptionally high concentrations of polymetallic elements, such as V and Mo. Scavenging and particle-mediated transport by FeMn (oxyhydr)oxides have been widely proposed to explain this enrichment, yet geological constraints on the carrier stage remain limited. The Early Cambrian Huanglongshan manganese (Mn) deposit in the northern Yangtze Block provides a rare archive for evaluating this mechanism and associated metal sources. Although Mn ores in this deposit are dominated by Mn carbonates, particularly rhodochrosite and kutnahorite, their close stratigraphic association with phosphorites and strongly positive Ce anomalies (Ce/Ce* = 1.14–2.11) support Mn-oxide-rich precursors. Markedly negative δ13Ccarb values are consistent with organic-matter-driven reduction of these precursors and early-diagenetic Mn‑carbonate precipitation. Polymetallic enrichment and covariation with MnO further support scavenging by precursor FeMn (oxyhydr)oxides and particle-mediated transfer from the water column to sediments, followed by reductive release and diagenetic redistribution. LogTh–logU relationships, Zn enrichment relative to Co, and negative δ57Fe values collectively suggest additional non-detrital, potentially regional hydrothermal, inputs that increased metal availability in the basin. Similar polymetallic enrichment patterns and MoEF–UEF relationships in the Niutitang Formation black shales are consistent with a possible contribution from Fe–Mn-mediated particulate metal transfer. We therefore propose a coupled source–transport–sink model in which enhanced metal supply, Fe–Mn-mediated particulate transfer, and authigenic fixation under reducing conditions jointly promoted polymetallic enrichment. The Huanglongshan preserves a complementary record of the otherwise poorly preserved FeMn carrier stage.

title: Tourmaline chemistry and boron isotopes record multistage magmatic-hydrothermal evolution of the Beimulang porphyry Cu deposit, Tibet
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Song Wu, Peng Liu, Shuyuan Chen, Sudong Shi, Jiancuo Luosang, Qiong Ci, Yayun Zhao, Xiaofeng Liu, Youye Zheng, Jianzhuang Zhao, Jiazhen Li
abstract: The Beimulang deposit, a newly discovered porphyry Cu deposit in the post-collisional Gangdese porphyry Cu belt, is distinguished by abundant tourmaline spanning late-magmatic crystallization to phyllic alteration. This occurrence is uncommon among other porphyry systems in the belt. We integrate petrography with in situ major-element, trace-element, and boron-isotope analyses of six texturally defined tourmaline types to reconstruct the magmatic-hydrothermal evolution and Cu mineralization of the deposit. Tur1-M formed during the late-magmatic crystallization, Tur2-O records the magmatic-hydrothermal transition, and Tur3-Po through Tur6-Ph represent potassic veining, tourmaline brecciation, propylitic alteration, and phyllic veining. Cu mineralization is principally associated with Tur3-Po and Tur6-Ph. Hydrothermal tourmaline contains approximately eight times more Cu than Tur1-M, whereas Tur1-M is enriched in Mn, Pb, Zn, Y, and rare earth elements. Systematic variations in Na, Ca, Ti, Sr, FeMg exchange, and FeAl exchange record changes in fluid composition, fluid-rock interaction, redox state, and salinity. Mineralized Tur3-Po and Tur6-Ph crystallized from relatively oxidized and saline fluids favorable for Cu transport and deposition. Tourmaline δ11B values range from −10.1 to −5.2‰. Boron-isotope modeling records monzogranitic fluid exsolution followed by Rayleigh fractionation from Tur1-M to Tur4-B. The lighter isotopic signature and Ca-Ti-Sr enrichment of Tur5-Pr record diorite-related input during propylitic alteration, whereas Tur6-Ph records renewed felsic magmatic-fluid discharge. Beimulang therefore developed as an open, multistage system in which wall rock interaction and recurrent inputs from compositionally distinct magmatic sources controlled fluid evolution and Cu mineralization. These results demonstrate that tourmaline provides a mineral-scale record of episodic magmatic-fluid processes in porphyry systems.

title: Potassium and sulfur isotope geochemistry of jarosite in sulfur–rich sediments in Victoria, Australia
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Yuqi Li, Andrew J. Frierdich, Tao Yang, Anne J. Whitworth, Weiqiang Li
abstract: Jarosite is a critical K–bearing indicator mineral of acidic and oxidizing sulfate–rich environments. While S isotope geochemistry of jarosite has been extensively studied, K isotopes remain largely unexplored despite their potential to trace alkali dynamics, mineral formation processes, and fluid–mineral interactions. This study presents a systematic investigation of K and S isotopes in morphologically diverse jarosite samples from two coastal sites in Victoria, Australia: Fossil Beach (FB) and Southside Beach (SB). The jarosite samples exhibit a wide range of δ41K values, from −1.70‰ to +1.14‰. A positive correlation (R2 = 0.42) exists between K/(K + Na) ratios and δ41K values. This trend, where K–rich jarosite is enriched in 41K, contradicts equilibrium fractionation theories and suggests Rayleigh−type fractionation during progressive precipitation. Sulfur isotopes show distinct site variations: FB samples display highly positive δ34S values (+15.47‰ to +40.30‰) that are consistent with closed−system sulfate reduction in a sulfate−limited reservoir with no external sulfate input, while SB samples range from −5.54‰ to +23.39‰ and lack extreme positive enrichments, consistent with a marine-buffered system oxidation and marine sulfate influx. Integrating the K and S isotope data from this study with previously published Fe isotope data thus distinguishes between the environment (recorded by S) and mineral formation mechanism (recorded by K and Fe), enabling a holistic reconstruction of jarosite formation pathways. This work showcases the use of K, Fe, and S isotopes as tracers for reaction pathways in acid–sulfate systems, with significant implications for both interpreting weathering intensity in terrestrial environments and understanding jarosite formation in analogous Martian settings.

title: Halogen behaviour during mantle melting and metasomatism recorded by peridotite xenoliths from Tariat, Mongolia
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Bryden L. Maunder, Mark A. Kendrick, Trevor Ireland, Dmitri A. Ionov, Oliver Nebel
abstract: Peridotite xenoliths from the Tariat region of Mongolia are representative of the MORB-source mantle in terms of trace element patterns and radiogenic isotopic ratios, with rare metasomatic enrichments. A selection of 21 lherzolites with MgO of 37–44 wt% were analysed for halogens (F, Cl, Br, I) by a combination of ion microprobe in clinopyroxene (CPX) orthopyroxene (OPX), olivine (OL), and spinel (SP), and bulk rock methods. We seek to: a) identify the mineral hosts of halogens in mantle peridotites, b) search for variations in halogen abundance related to either melt extraction or metasomatism, and c) test if whole rock samples retain information about these mantle processes or if mineral spot analyses are preferred. SHRIMP measurements of F, Cl and H2O in minerals from six variably melt-depleted samples show that F and H2O are preferentially hosted by CPX > OPX > OL ≈ SP, whereas Cl concentrations (0.5–1.1 μg/g), are close to the detection limit in all minerals. Combining mineral concentration data with modal abundance yields estimated whole rock concentrations of 11–18 μg/g F, 0.6–0.9 μg/g Cl and 78–106 μg/g H2O. In comparison, whole rock powders have 7–40 μg/g F, 8–75 μg/g Cl, 6–84 ng/g Br and 3.4–16 ng/g I. Despite the fresh appearance of the xenoliths, the high concentrations of Cl, Br and I in the bulk rocks are most easily explained by post-eruption alteration present within fractured olivine grains. In contrast, bulk peridotite F concentrations reflect mantle processes. The concentrations of F in individual minerals (OL, OPX, CPX) are fairly constant within the suite of peridotites irrespective of the degree of depletion. However, depleted harzburgites have systematically lower F concentrations than fertile lherzolites because of changes in modal mineralogy. Clinopyroxene is the dominant F host in fertile lherzolite, whereas olivine and orthopyroxene are the dominant F hosts in the depleted mantle. Unlike F, Cl is significantly hosted by non-structural sites and/or in undetected accessory phases on grain boundaries.

title: Kinetic isotope fractionation of gallium in Mars and 4 Vesta: Implications for non-equilibrium volatile loss during planetary accretion
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Zhi Li, Ying-Kui Xu, Shi-Jie Li, Yang Li, Dan Zhu, De-Liang Wang, Yun Liu
abstract: Moderately volatile elements (MVEs) provide important constraints on volatile depletion during planetary accretion. Gallium (Ga) is a moderately volatile, siderophile element whose isotopic systematics remain poorly constrained in differentiated planetary bodies. This study presents the first high-precision Ga isotopic data for martian and vestan meteorites (0.77 ± 0.21‰ and 0.86 ± 0.27‰, respectively), revealing significantly heavy mean δ71Ga values relative to chondrites and Earth. These heavy signatures defy explanation by core formation or equilibrium magma ocean degassing alone. Notably, Ga isotopes on Mars are strongly fractionated relative to potassium (K), despite their similar nebular volatilities, indicating a decoupling among MVEs during planetary processing. Kinetic fractionation during diffusion-limited evaporation, likely in impact melt–vapor environments, best explains both decoupling and heavy isotopes. Ga isotopes thus emerge as a unique tracer of non-equilibrium volatile loss, differing from alkali elements, providing new constraints on MVEs depletion in early planetesimals.

title: High-precision laser ablation U-Pb geochronology using a Neptune PLUS equipped with two 10 13 Ω amplifiers: Age mapping of Jack Hills detrital zircon
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Christopher M. Fisher, Dan Bevan, Aleksey Sadekov, Anthony I.S. Kemp
abstract: An all-Faraday laser ablation U-Pb geochronology method using a Neptune PLUS MC-ICPMS and utilizing two 1013 Ω amplifiers is presented. Using laser conditions and sample volumes similar to those of single collector studies, we measure accurate (∼0.1%) and precise (<0.1 to 0.2%) 207Pb/206Pb dates in ancient zircon, while 206Pb/238U offers accuracy and precision of better than 1.5% in the Phanerozoic and Neoproterozoic zircon analyzed here. This approach negates the need for the complicated detector-cross calibrations of previous LA-MC-ICPMS methods, as well as deadtime corrections associated with secondary electron multipliers, while still taking advantage of substantial improvement in precision offered by multi-collection. The updated LA-MC-ICPMS approach is applied to both mapping and spot analyses of Hadean detrital zircon from the Jack Hills metaconglomerate (Western Australia). The results demonstrate the advantages of the significant improvements in precision offered by 1013 Ω amplifiers and highlight the complex behavior of U-Pb isotope systematics resulting from multiple episodes of Pb-loss in this highly significant archive of Earth's earliest history. This approach is expected to provide a significant advance in the precision and accuracy of in-situ measurement of ancient mineral geochronometers like zircon, baddeleyite, monazite, cassiterite, xenotime, titanite, and apatite.

title: Volcanic sourced input enhances biological export in the Kuroshio Extension
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Zenghui Zhu, Pinghe Cai, Qian Liu, Wen Liu, Xueyan Jiang, Xiaoyi Guo, Shibin Zhao, Wenkai Guan, Honghai Zhang, Guangchao Zhuang, Ergang Lian, Shuo Ren, Ran An, Shanshan Chen, Zhaohui Chen, Bochao Xu
abstract: The Kuroshio Extension lies at the confluence of the North Pacific subtropical and subarctic gyres and receives particulate inputs from Asian dust and volcanic arcs. Constraining the provenance and burial fluxes of these materials is key to understanding how external nutrient supply regulates oceanic productivity. Here we quantify mass fluxes and sediment source contributions across a north–south transect of five sediment cores, using a combined approach of 230Th profile dating and 230Th normalization. Mass flux shows a pronounced north-to-south gradient, decreasing from 2.7 g cm−2 ka−1 in the north to 0.38 g cm−2 ka−1 in the south. Aeolian dust provides a regionally uniform lithogenic flux (0.18–0.25 g cm−2 ka−1), whereas volcanic inputs are more localized but more potent, with fluxes ranging from 0.06 to 1.72 g cm−2 ka−1. Volcanic flux co-varies spatially with biogenic–authigenic burial flux (r = 0.78), and elevated volcanic inputs in the northern cores are accompanied by enhanced burial of biogenic and authigenic materials (0.07–0.75 g cm−2 ka−1) This pattern suggests that volcanic iron fertilization may enhance biological export and promote the co-sequestration of trace metals such as rare earth elements. Our findings show that aeolian dust supplies a background level of trace metals, while volcanic inputs drive localized hotspots of biological productivity and metal burial. This framework highlights the interconnected roles of lithogenic sources in regulating the biological pump, although direct constraints on iron bioavailability await further investigation.

title: Textural features and chemical constraints on the formation of REE-U-Nb minerals in the Si-rich carbonatite complexes: Implications for REE and rare-metal mineralization
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Longgang Gao, Ruizhong Hu, Youwei Chen, Xianwu Bi, Jianfeng Gao
abstract: Carbonatite-related deposits, as the world's primary sources of light rare earth elements (REE) and niobium (Nb), are typically characterized by monazite- and/or bastnäsite- and pyrochlore-dominated assemblages formed from volatile-rich magmatic-hydrothermal systems. Some deposits, however, deviate from this conventional model by exhibiting allanite- and betafite-dominated assemblages, yet the chemical evolution driving this unique metallogenic divergence, particularly the generation of abundant REE-rich allanite, remains poorly understood. Compounding this problem, pervasive coupled dissolution-reprecipitation textures during later hydrothermal overprint can easily obscure the primary mineralization processes, further complicating genetic interpretation of the deposit. The giant Huayangchuan deposit in the Qinling Orogen (central China) exemplifies this atypical style, being hosted by carbonatites and associated ore veins across six lithofacies but strikingly dominated by allanite-(Ce) and betafite-(U, Nb) rather than monazite-bastnäsite and pyrochlore associations. Integrated textural-compositional analyses document reaction sequences involving monazite-(Ce), allanite-(Ce), apatite, biotite, betafite-(U, Nb), and uraninite-(U), recording multistage evolution since the Late Triassic. Key reactions are quantified by chemical equations to decode ore formation and mineral stability, including the generation of allanite-(Ce), replacement of monazite precursors by allanite-apatite assemblages under high-temperature, acidic, Si-rich conditions involving biotite and K-feldspar, and U-Nb-REE redistribution via coupled dissolution-reprecipitation of betafite. Results demonstrate that subsequent hydrothermal overprint, although texturally pervasive, was not the primary control on REE and rare-metal mineralization. We further reveal that Si-rich carbonatite systems inherently favor allanite-type over monazite-type REE mineralization. This finding provides a predictive framework for global exploration targeting allanite-type REE mineralization and exemplifies how decoding mineral reaction pathways reconstructs ore-forming mechanisms.

title: Multi-elemental plagioclase-melt modeling unravels (dis)equilibrium crystal growth during dynamic magmatic processes
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Alessio Pontesilli, Fabrizio Di Fiore, Silvio Mollo, Daniele Andronico, Jacopo Taddeucci, Manuela Nazzari, Ben S. Ellis, Olivier Bachmann, Piergiorgio Scarlato
abstract: Assessing magma storage conditions relies critically on crystal-melt equilibrium models. However, natural rocks are replete with disequilibrium features that testify to open-system processes and episodic crystal growth. Interface kinetics at the crystal-melt boundary lag behind changes of physicochemical conditions determined by magma dynamics. This poses petrological modeling with a circularity problem due to the interdependence between models based on intensive and extensive parameters. Here we discuss results of a numerical approach that aims at circumventing these difficulties, applying it to an extensive new dataset of plagioclase crystals from Stromboli volcano, characterized by sieve-like An-rich crystal zones with An 69–92 and oscillatory-zoned An-poor crystal zones with An 59–74, paired with a comprehensive database of matrix glass compositions. Our approach exploits major element partitioning between plagioclase and melt to identify equilibrium melt compositions and solve for the best-fit intensive parameters, and then tests the equilibrium pairs with trace element partitioning models. The well-constrained plumbing system of Stromboli, in which shallow, degassed magma frequently interacts with deeper, volatile-rich magma, represents the ideal test bed to evaluate iterative modeling approaches. Results show that the method used reproduces known equilibrium conditions and identifies disequilibrium crystal compositions formed during dynamic processes, including magma mixing, ascent and crystal resorption. By deconstructing the chemical record preserved in individual crystal zones, this study provides new quantitative constraints on crystallization processes within the Stromboli plumbing system. It is found that, while An-poor compositions invariably resemble equilibrium, the composition of the An-rich plagioclase zones is the result of disequilibrium partitioning triggered by concurrent magma interaction, cooling and degassing. Ultimately, our findings provide fundamental insights into crystal-melt partitioning during plagioclase near- and far-from-equilibrium growth, demonstrating also the broad utility of similar numerical approaches for interpreting magma evolution in open-conduit volcanic systems.

title: Why does the Himalayan–Tibetan orogen lack Cenozoic classical A-type granites?
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Shan-Shan Yang, Jian Wang, Derek A. Wyman, Wei Dan, Qiang Wang, Gong-Jian Tang
abstract: A-type granites are commonly considered to crystallize from high-temperature (>900 °C) melts. Yet almost no classical A-type granites have been identified in the Himalayan-Tibetan orogen. Here we investigate a rare Miocene A-type granitoid association from the East Pamir to West Kunlun, northwestern Tibetan Plateau, comprising syenite, syenitic granite, monzogranite and granite porphyry. They show typical A-type geochemical affinities, e.g., high alkali contents (K2O + Na2O > 7.2 wt%) and elevated 10,000 × Ga/Al ratios (mostly 2.1–6.6). Syenites and syenitic granites contain Fe-rich aegirine-augite, whereas biotite in granite porphyries is F-rich (up to 6.2 wt%). However, they differ from classical A-type granites: some are magnesian; most have high Sr (> 250 ppm) and Ba (> 500 ppm), significant REE fractionation [(La/Yb)N = 7–228], low HREE abundances, insignificant Eu anomalies (Eu/Eu* = 0.51–1.36), and relatively low emplacement temperatures (mostly <850 °C). We therefore propose that they represent a distinctive group of non-classical A-type granites. The syenite–syenitic granite and monzogranite–granite porphyry suites formed by fractional crystallization of mantle-derived magmas and melting of thickened lower-crustal sources, respectively. The rarity of classical A-type granites and the occurrence of these distinctive analogues in the Himalayan–Tibetan collisional orogen reflect the combined and interacting effects of a cold mantle, thick crust, and fertile crustal sources. Similar distinctive A-type granitoids may have been overlooked in other collisional orogens in Earth's history, where recognition relies mainly on classical high-temperature and ferroan A-type characteristics. Their identification provides a comprehensive model for understanding A-type magmatism and geodynamic evolution in collisional orogens.

title: The Moon's mantle, as recorded by olivine in Apollo 17 dunite 72415
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): E.S. Jennings, H. Downes, K.K. Bhanot, D. Cooper
abstract: Several samples of lunar material have been claimed to represent deep olivine-rich cumulates derived from crystallisation of the lunar magma ocean (LMO). These samples should contain an important direct record of lunar mantle composition and key insights into the Moon's formation history. We present new measurements of olivine and metal grains from the Apollo 17 dunite sample 72415, including zoning profiles, maps and high-precision minor element data. The data highlight a high degree of inter- and intra-grain compositional homogeneity, suggesting a prolonged cooling history following crystallisation. We identified a polycrystalline clast that is internally unbrecciated and shows a high degree of textural equilibrium; olivines in this clast have a higher Ti content than other olivines, which may relate to mantle redox heterogeneity. Generally, all olivines in 72415 have low CaO contents and compositions that, apart from NiO, are similar to olivines found in terrestrial mantle xenoliths. These characteristics, alongside their symplectites that record a garnet+olivine stoichiometry, make a strong case for 72415 being mantle-derived, specifically from the earlier and deeper layers of the LMO. However, accepting this interpretation raises some interesting questions. Firstly, 72415's olivine composition is not easily reconciled with high-Ni olivines in a Chang'e-6 soil sample that have previously been interpreted as being mantle-derived, suggesting a different origin for the two groups. Secondly, we show that the very low NiO (0.012 wt%) paired with the low Ni/Co of approximately 1.6 of olivines from dunite 72415 cannot be explained by core formation and equilibrium crystallisation alone. Even if all of the Ni in the rare small metal grains in 72415 was diffusively transferred from the olivines, the olivine prior to equilibration with metal had only a slightly higher Ni/Co of 2.5, which still cannot be explained by core formation. Assuming an Earth-mantle-like bulk Moon, we demonstrate that additional differentiation processes beyond just core formation are required to further deplete Ni in the LMO, such as the fractional crystallisation of olivine. Even then, it is difficult to deplete Ni to the extent required by the olivine compositions, suggesting perhaps that a further process occurred such as the segregation of iron sulfide in the LMO. Alternatively, the bulk Moon is depleted in Ni relative to bulk silicate Earth, but not other refractory elements, which is difficult to reconcile with our current understanding of the Earth-Moon system.

title: First-principles study of hydrated and hydrolyzed Nd(III) adsorption on kaolinite (001) and 00 1 ¯ surfaces
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Yingzi Xia, Shanqi Liu, Huiquan Tian, Yongbing Li, Shuping Yin, Jianming Liu
abstract: Ion-adsorption deposits (IADs) are important sources of heavy and selected light rare earth elements (REEs), yet the adsorption mechanisms of hydrated and hydrolyzed Nd(III) on clay-mineral surfaces remain incompletely resolved. Structural refinement of adsorbed Nd by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) is challenging because the Nd L3-edge region is susceptible to interference from nearby Ce and Pr absorption edges. In this study, first-principles calculations were performed to investigate the adsorption of [Nd(H2O)9]3+ and [Nd(OH)(H2O)8]2+ on the (001) and ( 00 1 ¯ ) basal surfaces of kaolinite. Optimized isolated complexes show that nine-coordination represents the saturated first hydration shell of Nd3+. Upon adsorption, [Nd(H2O)9]3+ remains outer-sphere on both basal surfaces. Partial dehydration occurs on the (001) surface, whereas the dehydration behavior on the 00 1 ¯ surface depends on the adsorption geometry. For [Nd(OH)(H2O)8]2+, adsorption remains outer-sphere on the (001) surface without dehydration. On the 00 1 ¯ surface, the adsorption mode of [Nd(OH)(H2O)8]2+ is influenced by the Nd–OOH bond orientation, with a toward-surface orientation leading to partial dehydration and inner-sphere complexation. Electronic-structure analyses reveal localized interfacial charge redistribution on the (001) surface, pronounced Si-O framework polarization on the 00 1 ¯ surface, and more pronounced overlap between Nd-d and surface O-p states in the inner-sphere complex. DFT + U tests for [Nd(H2O)9]3+ indicate no substantial changes in adsorption geometries or net interfacial charge redistribution. These results indicate that Nd hydrolysis, Nd–OOH bond orientation, and basal-surface chemistry jointly influence the adsorption mode of Nd on kaolinite, providing molecular-level constraints on pH-dependent light REE retention in IADs.

title: Turbidite-associated pyritization in deep-sea sediments: Geochemical insights from the Bengal Fan
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Xiangyu Chen, Jingrui Li, Yu Gu, Xin Chang, Xuefa Shi, Shengfa Liu, Xiting Liu
abstract: Marine microbial sulfate reduction (MSR) is the principal process driving authigenic pyrite formation in marine sediments, yet the influence of episodic turbidite deposition on pyritization and early diagenetic sulfur cycling remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated a turbidite-bearing core (BOB-91) and a hemipelagic reference core (BOB-4) from the western Bengal Fan by integrating sedimentological observations, bulk-sediment geochemistry, reactive iron speciation, pyrite sulfur isotopes, and in situ pyrite trace-element analyses. Two turbidite intervals in BOB-91 are distinguished from adjacent hemipelagic sediments by abrupt grain-size coarsening followed by fining-upward trends, prominent XRD peaks of quartz and albite, and higher Fe/Al, Ti/Al, and K/Al ratios. Compared with adjacent hemipelagic sediments, the turbidites contain more nitric-acid-extractable iron (FeHNO3), lower contents of dithionite- and oxalate-extractable iron (FeD and FeO), a modestly higher mean degree of pyritization (DOP = 0.034 versus 0.023), and lower δ34Spy values. These changes are consistent with more efficient conversion of reactive iron into pyrite and larger apparent sulfur-isotope offsets between seawater sulfate and sedimentary pyrite within the turbidites. Turbidite-hosted pyrite is generally enriched in Mg and Mo and depleted in Cr relative to pyrite in adjacent hemipelagic sediments. This trace-element pattern records distinct pyrite-forming conditions within the turbidite intervals, but does not independently resolve the relative contributions of organoclastic sulfate reduction (OSR) and sulfate-driven anaerobic oxidation of methane (SD-AOM). In addition, FeHR/FeT and MoEF/UEF relationships do not indicate a persistent shift toward strongly reducing bottom-water conditions. Taken together, these observations suggest that turbidite deposition reorganized local early diagenetic reaction–transport conditions, rather than causing a sustained change in bottom-water redox state, and was associated with more efficient pyritization. These findings highlight the importance of depositional processes and sedimentary facies in regulating pyrite formation and interpreting sulfur cycling in deep-sea sediments.

title: Determination of ferrous iron in biotite by EPMA using the flank method: development of a mineral-specific calibration
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Shahed Shahrestani, Ioan V. Sanislav, Yang Liu, Kevin Blake, Avish Kumar, Shane Askew
abstract: The oxidation state of iron in biotite provides key information on redox conditions, magma evolution, and fluid–rock interactions in igneous, metamorphic, and hydrothermal systems, yet routine determination of Fe2+ and Fe3+ by electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) remains difficult. This study presents a biotite-specific calibration of the flank method for estimating Fe2+ from Fe Lβ/Lα intensity ratios. Rather than defining flank positions from garnet end-members, as in the conventional approach, flank positions were established directly from biotite spectra, exploiting the comparatively narrow Fe3+/ΣFe range of biotite to achieve more consistent spectral behaviour. Twelve biotite samples spanning a wide range of total iron content (8.29–22.61 wt% ΣFeO) were analysed by EPMA and independently characterised by wet chemistry to calibrate and test the method. A simple linear regression of Fe2+ against Lβ/Lα produced a strong correlation with wet-chemistry values (R2 = 0.95, average error 0.47 wt%), and incorporating total iron (ΣFe) into a multiple regression model improved the prediction of Fe2+/ΣFe, accounting for matrix-dependent effects associated with total Fe concentration. Leave-one-out cross-validation was applied to evaluate the performance of both models, and independent validation against a well-characterised reference biotite (LP-6) yielded Fe2+ estimates within 0.4–0.6 wt% of the reported composition. These results demonstrate that mineral-specific calibration of the flank method, combined with controlled instrumental conditions, offers a practical, and in-situ alternative to Mössbauer spectroscopy or synchrotron XANES for constraining Fe2+/Fe3+ in biotite, with potential application to other Fe-bearing silicates and to broader petrogenetic, ore-deposit, and metamorphic studies in which iron oxidation state provides information on mineral-forming conditions.

title: The Sutrakar trachydacite: volcanology, 40 Ar/ 39 Ar systematics and petrogenesis of a crystal-rich silicic flood lava in the western Deccan Traps, India
description: Publication date: 20 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 726 Author(s): Arunodaya Shekhar, B. Astha, Hetu Sheth, Hijas Hameed, Anmol Naik, Waliur Rahaman, Ghulam Rabbani, Hugo K.H. Olierook, Fred Jourdan, Christopher L. Kirkland
abstract: The 16-km-long Sutrakar flow, in the western Deccan Traps, is a fissure-fed, crystal-rich, silicic flood lava with an original volume > 4.8 km3. It contains abundant phenocrysts and glomerocrysts of plagioclase (andesine), and minor augite and Fe–Ti oxides, in a glass-rich groundmass with oligoclase, anorthoclase and sanidine microlites. Its composition is mainly trachydacite, less commonly rhyolite or trachyte, due to slightly variable phenocryst contents; an altered vitrophyric variety is a dacite. Most samples are metaluminous. Phenocryst cores yield crystallisation temperatures of 1123–1089 °C (± 35 °C, 1σ, clinopyroxene) and 1071–1021 °C (± 12 °C, 1σ, plagioclase) at 1 kbar pressure.
