However, deterministic models generally neglect the effects of natural spatial variability in soil hydraulic and thermal properties on thermo-hydrological responses. This study therefore develops a stochastic framework for coupled heat and moisture transfer in heterogeneous permafrost active layers during seasonal thawing. The formulation explicitly incorporates the spatial variability of saturated hydraulic conductivity and thermal conductivity and derives analytical expressions in the Fourier spectral domain for the temperature semivariogram, heat-flux semivariogram, and variance of capillary pressure head. Closed-form solutions are obtained for the case in which the random fields of the natural logarithms of saturated hydraulic conductivity and thermal conductivity are characterized by hole-type exponential covariance functions. The analytical solutions show that the perturbation fields for temperature, heat flux, and capillary pressure exhibit nonstationary spatial variability, despite the assumption of second-order stationarity in log-hydraulic and −thermal property perturbation fields. The results are also used to analyze the influence of key parameters in coupled stochastic heat and moisture transfer models on the spatial variability of coupled thermo-hydrological responses. The proposed framework provides a physically based means of quantifying uncertainty propagation from heterogeneous soil properties to coupled heat and moisture transfer, thereby improving the understanding of active-layer dynamics and providing a theoretical basis for uncertainty analysis and stochastic parameterization in permafrost hydrological models.

title: Seasonal shift from phosphorus retention to remobilization along an aquaculture pond–sediment–groundwater pathway in a monsoon-influenced shallow lake margin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Saier Chen, Teng Ma, Zhijia Zeng, Ting Jiang, Liuzhu Chen
abstract: Pond-based aquaculture is an important source of phosphorus (P) to adjacent shallow lakes, and previous studies have mainly examined P dynamics at the pond sediment–water interface or along surface-water pathways. In monsoon-influenced lake margins, pond-water leakage may carry aquaculture-derived P through underlying sediments into shallow groundwater, yet how seasonal hydrological connectivity and sediment Fe/P reactions regulate P retention, remobilization, and potential lakeward transfer remains poorly understood. We combined wet- and dry-season field surveys in an aquaculture-affected margin of Honghu Lake, China, with a sequential wet-to-dry column experiment to examine how the balance between P retention and export changes along this pathway as boundary conditions shift from pond-water leakage to groundwater throughflow. Field observations showed an apparent inconsistency between groundwater redox indicators and soluble reactive phosphorus (SRP) concentrations: SRP was lower in the relatively reducing wet season but higher in the relatively oxidizing dry season. In the column experiment, the sediment strongly attenuated SRP from simulated P-rich pond water (0.86–0.99 mg·L−1), with cumulative net SRP retention reaching 93.35 mg·m−2 and Fe-bound P (Fe–P) enrichment. After switching to simulated low-P, more mineralized groundwater influent (0.27 mg·L−1 SRP), the wet-stage-conditioned sediment shifted to net SRP export, and the cumulative net SRP balance declined by 85.34 mg·m−2 from the wet-stage endpoint, accompanied by Fe–P depletion and an increased Fe(II)/Fe(III) ratio, consistent with selective remobilization of previously retained sediment P. Together, the column responses and the more favorable dry-season groundwater–lake hydraulic conditions suggest a seasonal reorganization of functional connectivity within the aquaculture pond–sediment–groundwater–lake continuum: wet-season pond-water leakage favored temporary retention of incoming P within the pond–sediment segment, whereas dry-season remobilization coincided with greater potential for lakeward P export. Management should therefore consider aquaculture-derived P inputs, seasonal hydrological connectivity, and the stability of retained sediment P.

title: Changes in the annual cycle of shallow subarctic groundwater regimes over 50 years
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Pietari Pöykkö, Mira Tammelin, Anna-Kaisa Ronkanen, Lauri Ahopelto, Pekka M. Rossi
abstract: Seasonal groundwater level regimes are exposed to climate change, with implications for drought and flood risks, water supply, agriculture, and ecosystems. Changes in the intra-annual groundwater fluctuations are accentuated in quickly responding shallow aquifers found worldwide, but particularly in subarctic regions, where the cold winter season attenuates infiltration and evaporation. To identify the types of subarctic groundwater regimes and their responses to the changing climate, 50-year groundwater level data from 52 monitoring stations throughout Finland were analyzed. This was done by partitioning around medians (PAM) clustering of Pearson correlations and a principal component analysis (PCA) of normalized monthly values. Four distinct regimes were identified, mostly following the southwest–northeast temperature and snow condition gradients. The migration of regimes towards the colder northeastern regions could be seen between the clustering periods of 1975–1999 and 2000–2024. This migration manifested as rising winter levels and lowering summer levels, in addition to changing seasonality timing, such as the spring recharge peak advancing by an average of half a month and by up to two months. Furthermore, seasonal groundwater level responses were seen to depend on the projected surface area of the aquifer, as comparatively larger aquifers among the studied 0.1– 41 km2 scale showed a lagged regime. The results suggest that the selected approach effectively captures the spatially evolving conditions. They also highlight the importance of long-term monitoring for effective decision-making and preparedness for shortages in water availability in the changing climate.

title: Soil temperature governs deep soil water infiltration in alpine meadows on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Jie Li, Qiaoyan Chen, Junna Feng, Bo Fan, Yangong Du, Licong Dai, Ruiyu Fu, Xiaowei Guo
abstract: Deep soil water infiltration is a critical process linking surface water inputs with deeper soil water storage and potential groundwater recharge, yet its seasonal dynamics and controls remain poorly understood in alpine meadows of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Based on growing-season (May–September) observations from 2017 to 2023, this study quantified seasonal variations in deep soil water infiltration and identified controlling factors using an XGBoost machine-learning model combined with SHAP (Shapley additive explanations). We found deep infiltration showed pronounced seasonal variability and was not directly synchronized with precipitation patterns. During the growing season, cumulative evapotranspiration (361.7 mm) slightly exceeded cumulative precipitation (344.7 mm), suggesting that all rainfall was consumed by evapotranspiration rather than contributing directly to deep recharge. Among the examined variables, soil temperature (ST) was identified as the most important predictor of deep infiltration, accounting for 33.3% of the total SHAP-based importance, followed by air temperature (T; 29.5%) and volumetric soil moisture (VSM; 15.3%), which accounted for nearly 80% of the total SHAP-based importance, whereas precipitation and evapotranspiration display relatively limited contributions. Notably, ST exhibited a distinct nonlinear threshold effect, i.e. lower soil temperatures enhanced deep infiltration, but substantially reduced when ST exceeded approximately 9.2 ∼ 9.6 °C. Besides, deep infiltration was also significantly negatively correlated with aboveground biomass (P < 0.01), suggesting that enhanced plant water use during the peak growing season may restrict downward water movement. Meanwhile, plant water-use analysis showed that dominant alpine meadow species mainly relied on 0–40 cm soil water, with limited use of deeper soil water, which further explain the enhanced root-zone water consumption and reduces deep recharge during growing season. These findings suggested that soil thermal conditions and vegetation jointly regulate deep infiltration by altering soil water availability, and vertical water transfer. Our study provided new insight for improving process-based hydrological models and assessing the vulnerability of alpine meadow water cycling under future warming scenarios.

title: An adaptive Picard-SBFEM-level set formulation for three-dimensional saturated-unsaturated seepage flow analysis and free-surface tracking
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Chuhao Huang, Jun Liu, Fuming Wang, Chengchao Guo, Lei Gan, Wenbin Ye, Binghan Xue, Gao Lin
abstract: This study presents a semi-analytical numerical framework for three-dimensional steady saturated–unsaturated seepage analysis with free-surface tracking. The proposed method integrates the scaled boundary finite element method, an adaptive linearized Picard iteration scheme, and a level-set method into a unified formulation. The nonlinear Richards equation with pressure-head-dependent hydraulic conductivity is solved using a coefficient-frozen Picard strategy, while the unknown free surface is implicitly represented by a level-set function and corrected until both the hydraulic and kinematic conditions are satisfied. Five three-dimensional examples comprising 16 cases are investigated, covering spatially varying permeability, zoned heterogeneous media, non-uniform boundary conditions, complex geometries, confined seepage fields, and internal defects. The computed phreatic surfaces, total head distributions, pressure head distributions, and local seepage patterns agree well with the corresponding reference solutions, thereby validating the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method. Computational efficiency is further assessed using the global degrees of freedom (DOFs), matrix-assembly time, nonlinear-iteration time, peak memory usage, and total wall-clock time rather than the element count alone. For five representative cases, the proposed method reduces the global DOFs by 52.8%∼87.1%, the total matrix-assembly time by 15.5%∼32.4%, the average nonlinear-iteration time by 12.0%∼27.6%, and the peak memory usage by 31.7%∼44.3%. The corresponding total computational time is reduced by 28.0%∼58.3% relative to the reference models. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately and efficiently solve complex three-dimensional saturated–unsaturated seepage problems while maintaining stable convergence and reliable free-surface tracking.

title: Lithium isotopes as a proxy for hydrological-climate variation in the modern catchments and geological archives of salt lakes, Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Jilei Yang, Fei Zhang, Qingkuan Li, Tianyuan Chen, Qishun Fan
abstract: Reconstructing the paleohydrology of Tibetan Plateau (TP) saline lakes is essential for assessing current hydrological expansion and predicting future changes. However, conventional proxies like δ18Ocarbonate are often confounded by temperature or precipitation effects. This study proposes lithium isotopes (δ7Lidissolved) from river-lake systems and lacustrine sediments as a novel hydrological-climate proxy. We compiled published δ7Li-δ18O data from TP waters (hot springs, rivers, saline lakes) and analyzed two sediment δ7Li sequences from Bangor Co (southern TP) and Qarhan Salt Lake (northern TP). Results show that δ7Lidissolved is more sensitive to hydrological change than δ18O and progressively increases along the source-transport-sink continuum. Riverine δ7Li correlates positively with high discharge in geothermal recharge catchments but negatively in silicate weathering catchments. Sediment Li isotopes record distinct hydrological responses during the evolution from mega lakes to saline lakes since the last interglacial. In Bangor Co, δ7Liwater-soluble decreases due to geothermal input, with limited δ7Licarbonate data supporting this pattern, whereas in Qarhan, δ7Li in both phases increases under silicate weathering. These sediment patterns match modern catchment-specific δ7Liriverine behavior, reflecting divergent mechanisms: mixing of low-δ7Li geothermal water with high-δ7Li meteoric water in geothermal catchments, versus water–rock interaction time regulated by discharge in weathering-dominated catchments. We conclude that δ7Liwater-soluble in sediments is a sensitive hydrological proxy with weaker temperature dependence than δ18O, in combination with consistent hydrological-climate variation patterns across terrestrial archives over multiple temporal scales. These comparisons offer a significant advantage over δ18Ocarbonate for reconstructing lake paleohydrological-climate and serve as a compelling alternative proxy.

title: Hydraulic sorting and retention of microplastics in a cascade reservoir system, Southwest China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Yu Chen, Yuchuan Meng, Guodong Liu, Yichen Liu, Xiaohua Huang, Tishan Peng, Yingqian Hou
abstract: Freshwater reservoirs are considered important microplastic (MP) accumulation hotspots due to altered hydrodynamic conditions. However, research on MP occurrence in cascade reservoirs, particularly regarding their influence on MP transport and distribution, remains relatively limited. This study investigated MP pollution in a typical cascade reservoir system along the mainstream of the Dadu River in Southwest China, with a focus on the effect of hydrodynamic heterogeneity on longitudinal MP profiles. A retention index (RI) was defined as the relative change in MP abundance between the upstream near-dam area (UDA) and downstream near-dam area (DDA) of a dam, which served as an indicator for comparing MP retention potential among reservoirs. Results showed that MP abundance ranged from 1.16 to 6.01 items/L, with a mean of 3.29 items/L. PE (31.9%), PET (31.1%), and PP (15.5%) were the predominant polymer types, while fragments (52.9%) and fibers (41.2%) were the dominant shapes. From upstream to downstream, MP abundance and diversity exhibited a significant increasing trend, and MP abundance was positively correlated with population (p < 0.05). Density-based sorting was identified as the dominant hydraulic sorting pattern across the cascade reservoir system, whereas the size-based sorting signal was weaker and statistically conditional. At the regional scale, the UDAs of the reservoirs were the MP accumulation hotspots in the cascade system due to the retention effect of dams, with several reservoirs exhibiting a longitudinal enrichment pattern from the reservoir tail to the dam. Finally, reservoir characteristics were found to relate to the retention indicator: reservoirs with larger storage capacity (and statistically equivalently, longer hydraulic retention time) showed higher RIs in the cascade reservoir system. These findings advance our understanding of MP transport and retention in cascade reservoir systems at the basin scale.

title: A constrained deep learning framework for spatiotemporal downscaling of GRACE-derived terrestrial water storage anomalies over China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Min Wei, Hao Zhou, Yifeng Chen, Wenjing Ma, Siyou Xu, Zhicai Luo
abstract: Terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) play an important role in characterizing hydrological variability, particularly under changing climate conditions. Representing TWSA at finer spatiotemporal scales is essential for characterizing water-storage variations across spatial and temporal scales. Although the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (GFO) missions provide valuable TWSA observations, their inherent spatiotemporal resolution limits the representation of short-term variability and localized spatial features. While hydrological simulations such as GLDAS provide fine-scale spatial and temporal hydrological variability, their simulated signal magnitude and long-term trends may differ from GRACE/GFO observations. To address these limitations, this study proposed a multi-scale constrained deep learning model with a spatiotemporally constrained loss function to produce a daily TWSA reconstruction over China on a 0.25° grid. This proposed spatiotemporal downscaling (STDS) framework integrates the large-scale gravimetric constraints from GRACE/GFO with the fine-scale spatiotemporal variability represented by GLDAS. Experimental results show that, compared with GLDAS, STDS reduces the RMSE relative to GRACE/GFO observations by 62.07%, while maintaining a high temporal correlation (0.91) and spatial structural consistency (0.96) with GLDAS, indicating that the fine-scale spatiotemporal variability informed by GLDAS is largely preserved under the GRACE/GFO constraints. During Typhoon Doksuri and the Zhengzhou flash flood events, the STDS further exhibited localized TWSA variations that evolved consistently with the precipitation fields. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a GRACE/GFO-constrained representation of TWSA while preserving the fine-scale spatiotemporal variability informed by GLDAS. The resulting product has potential applications in hydrological studies, including the analysis of short-term extreme events.

title: A dimensionally consistent reformulation of the HyMoLAP rainfall–runoff model: interpretability and robustness across CAMELS datasets
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Lionel Cédric Gohouede, Sianou Ezéckiel Houénafa, Eliézer Iboukoun Biao, Olatunji Johnson, Cenk Sezen
abstract: Rainfall–runoff modelling is a central tool for understanding and managing water resources. The Hydrological Model based on the Least Action Principle (HyMoLAP) is a parsimonious model that represents the rainfall–runoff transformation as an ordinary differential equation (ODE) at the catchment scale. This study revisits the HyMoLAP framework by reformulating it through the introduction of scaling parameters to ensure dimensional consistency, leading to d-HyMoLAP. The model is evaluated on 549 CAMELS-FR and 623 CAMELS-GB catchments. Model performance is investigated using Random Forest and XGBoost with SHAP analysis, while parameter sensitivity and predictive uncertainty are assessed using Morris sensitivity analysis and GLUE, respectively. Compared with the original HyMoLAP, d-HyMoLAP substantially improves performance, increasing the mean validation NSE from 0.165 to 0.649 on CAMELS-FR and from −2.570 to 0.650 on CAMELS-GB. Although HBV shows stronger performance across most catchments, d-HyMoLAP substantially reduces catastrophic failures relative to the original HyMoLAP and can match or exceed HBV in a subset of catchments under specific hydroclimatic conditions. In the CAMELS-FR comparative classification analysis, d-HyMoLAP is more likely to match or exceed HBV in catchments characterized by low runoff ratio, low high-flow frequency, and a gentle flow-duration-curve slope. Its highest performance is associated with humid catchments exhibiting stable hydroclimatic conditions and limited hydrological extremes. Analysis of calibration period length indicates that stable predictive performance can be achieved using relatively short calibration records. Parameter sensitivity analysis identifies the introduced scaling parameters as the dominant controls on model performance. GLUE analysis for four selected representative catchments provides evidence consistent with practical equifinality and relatively constrained prediction intervals, although coverage remains below the nominal 90% level and these findings should not be generalized to the full large-sample datasets. Overall, the results support the potential of d-HyMoLAP for large-sample rainfall–runoff modelling and enhanced water resource management.

title: Scenario-adaptive scheduling of cascade hydro-wind-solar-pumped storage systems driven by hydrological variability
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Lu Liu, Chao Ma, Muhan Li, Zexing Deng
abstract: Hydrological variability changes both water availability and reservoir regulation margins, but its implications for scheduling-window selection under uniform bundled power delivery remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a scenario-adaptive scheduling framework for a cascade hydro-wind-solar-pumped storage complementary system (CHWSPCS). A coordinated operation model combines long-term reservoir boundaries, shared-reservoir pumped storage, transmission limits, and a daily delivery profile repeated over multi-day windows. Monthly cumulative-runoff quantiles distinguish high-runoff (alpha), normal, and low-runoff (beta) scenarios while retaining concurrent wind and photovoltaic inputs. Recommended windows are extracted from optimization results using a tolerance-based hierarchical rule that prioritizes delivered energy, followed by loss of load probability (LOLP) and curtailment rate (CR). The framework is verified using a CHWSPCS in the middle reaches of the Yalong River, China. The results indicate that: (1) The proposed strategy effectively coordinates hydropower, wind, photovoltaic and pumped storage units, significantly improving the reliability of bundled power delivery under diverse scenarios; (2) Abundant inflow supports greater delivery but can increase hydropower curtailment and planned-delivery shortfalls under constrained release and transmission conditions. Limited inflow increases the importance of inter-day water allocation and coordination with variable renewable generation. (3) With a 1.0% delivered-energy tolerance, alpha flood-season recommendations are 3–5 days, whereas beta non-flood recommendations vary from 3 to 15 days across months. (4) Under repeated 7-day delivery, reducing pumped-storage capacity from 1200 to 600 MW increases median LOLP by 1.323–2.053 percentage points. The framework links scheduling-window selection to hydrological conditions and reservoir flexibility, while numerical recommendations require recalibration for other systems.

title: Agricultural land-use change rivals climate variability in driving blue water consumption in arid Xinjiang: a factorial counterfactual attribution
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Qixiang Liang, Yanfeng Di, Xingming Hao, Mengtao Ci, Fan Sun, Jingjing Zhang, Zulipiya Kulaixi, Chuan Wang, Xue Fan, Xinran Guo
abstract: Agricultural expansion and crop structure adjustments in arid regions have profoundly reshaped regional water consumption patterns. Yet, a quantitative understanding of the independent and combined impacts of agricultural land-use (ALU) conversion and climate change on water resources remains limited. In this study, we developed a 30-meter resolution crop type dataset for Xinjiang spanning 2013–2024, derived from multi-source remote sensing imagery and field sampling data. By integrating evapotranspiration (ET) products with counterfactual simulations, we quantitatively disentangled the causal effects of ALU conversion and climate change on blue water consumption. Results show that relative to the 2013–2015 baseline, Xinjiang’s total agricultural water use increased by 35.45 × 108 m3 during 2016–2024, with climate change contributing 22.50 × 108 m3 and ALU conversion contributing 12.95 × 108 m3. For irrigation (blue) water, the total increase was 32.87 × 108 m3, to which ALU conversion contributed 16.67 × 108 m3 and climate change 16.20 × 108 m3—almost equal magnitudes. The expansion of cotton and reclamation of non-agricultural land (Non-ALU) substantially intensified irrigation demand, whereas conversion to orchards and other economic crops effectively reduced blue water consumption. These results show that climate change dominates the increase in total agricultural water use, whereas ALU adjustment exerts a comparable influence on blue water consumption. Accordingly, water-resource planning should constrain further regional cotton expansion and non-agricultural reclamation in water-stressed areas, dynamically adjust irrigation quotas in response to climate-driven evapotranspiration demand, and protect part of the resulting water savings for environmental flows and wetland maintenance. These measures can help reconcile agricultural production with ecological water requirements under continued climate change.

title: Climate-driven future changes in Arctic river discharges using hydrological modelling and CMIP6 projections
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Asfand Tehseen, Joy Bhattacharjee, Aino Saarinen, Elina Kasvi, Ville Kankare, Petteri Alho
abstract: Arctic amplification is intensifying the hydrological cycle of high-latitude river systems, yet quantitative projections of future discharge remain scarce for many Arctic catchments. This study quantifies the impacts of climate change on the discharge regime of the Tana River, a pristine transboundary Arctic catchment in northern Fennoscandia, using the SWAT+ hydrological model driven by five CMIP6 GCMs and an ensemble under four SSP scenarios. The model was calibrated and validated against observed daily discharge at three gauging stations. The findings demonstrate that the Tana River’s discharge regime is already on a trajectory of significant change. The future simulations reveal systematic, SSP-dependent changes in the monthly discharge distribution, seasonal flow patterns, and annual projections through 2100. The timing of peak flow is projected to shift from June to May across most of the GCMs and scenarios, reflecting earlier snowmelt driven by rising temperatures. Seasonal analysis indicates increased flows in winter, spring, and autumn, and decreased flows in summer. By the end of the 21st century, annual discharge, precipitation and mean temperature are projected to increase, while the snow fraction is projected to decline. Under different SSPs, discharge exhibits statistically significant increasing trends, with Pettitt tests identifying change points around mid-century. These predicted changes may have significant implications for the ecosystem, flood risk, and water resource management in the Arctic region.

title: A novel analytical method for transient advection–dispersion–reaction equations with arbitrary source term in layered media
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Zhang-Long Chen, Tian-Chyi Jim Yeh, Bo Guo, Chen-Xu Liu, Hongwei Fang
abstract: The transport and accumulation of naturally occurring contaminants (NOCs) in soils may deteriorate groundwater and soil environmental quality and pose potential risks to ecosystems. To date, no analytical solution is available for modeling transient NOC transport with zero-order generation in layered porous media. We present a novel analytical method for solving layered advection–dispersion–reaction–source equations (ADRSEs) and apply it to model NOC transient transport in layered porous media. Our exact analytical solution can accommodate an arbitrary number of layers, an arbitrary spatiotemporally dependent source term, and arbitrary initial and boundary conditions. An analytical solution, two semi-analytical solutions, and a numerical solution are used to verify the new analytical solution. Taking radon exhalation from a radon cover layer system as an example, we illustrate the effects of spatiotemporally dependent source terms, cover layer thickness, and advection on radon transport. The results indicate that neglecting the spatiotemporal variability of source terms can lead to inaccurate predictions of radon exhalation flux. Furthermore, with decreasing permeability of the cover layer, both the fluctuation amplitude and the peak value of radon exhalation flux decrease significantly. The solution is then applied to the radon deficit technique to provide a theoretical basis for quantifying residual non-aqueous phase liquid (NAPL) in the aquifer. Comparisons with laboratory and field experimental results demonstrate the potential of the analytical solution for practical applications. More broadly, the solution provides a unified analytical framework for advection–diffusion problems involving source terms and can serve as a benchmark for related numerical models.

title: Integrating rainfall event and antecedent depths into a single probabilistic framework for deriving event depth-duration-antecedent depth-frequency curves
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Enrico Creaco
abstract: This paper aims to show how rainfall event depth and antecedent depth can be integrated into the same framework for deriving depth-duration-antecedent depth frequency (DDAF) curves, which map a mathematical relationship between event depth, duration and antecedent depth for a given return period. These curves are obtained by means of a multi-step analysis of annual extrema in the trade-off between event depth and antecedent depth, which are dealt with by means of copula-based bivariate distributions for various durations. Unlike conventional depth-duration-frequency (DDF) curves, DDAF curves enable generating various combinations of event and antecedent depths, the return period staying the same. These equiprobable combinations can be input to event-based hydrologic modelling, to enable identification of the most critical one for the preset return period in the design phase. In the testing/verification phase, the new methodology allows estimating the return period to a new event occurring with specific values of duration, depth and antecedent depth. The applications of the paper are performed on a long horizon dataset of rainfall measurements with fine temporal resolution in three case studies (Erice and Pavia in Italy, Helsinborg in Sweden), proving the benefits of the novel methodology.

title: Land surface model snow formulation sensitivity and a solar-zenith-angle snow covered area scheme evaluated across the western United States
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Reed M. Maxwell
abstract: Accurate representation of snow water equivalent (SWE) remains a central challenge for land surface and integrated hydrologic models. This work expands the ParFlow-CLM snow model with several new parameterizations, including a formulation that modulates fractional snow covered area (fSCA) by solar zenith angle. I evaluate these parameterizations across 220 site-years from the SNOTEL observation network, spanning three experiments and 58 configurations that represent the major snow parameterization choices in the literature, including three albedo schemes, five rain-snow partitioning methods, and band-separated snow aging formulations. A systematic sensitivity analysis shows that fSCA is the dominant control on SWE prediction accuracy among the tested parameterizations, with fSCA changes producing larger improvements than any tested change to albedo scheme, rain-snow partitioning, or snow aging. Static fSCA corrections improve peak SWE but introduce a trade-off with melt timing. The new solar-zenith-angle-modulated fSCA scheme resolves this trade-off by using seasonal solar geometry to transition between snow-preserving accumulation and snow-exposing ablation conditions. Across all configurations, the SZA-fSCA scheme achieves the best balance of peak accuracy and melt timing (NSE of 0.79, melt bias of −1 day), surpassing reanalysis products and default process-model benchmarks and approaching LSTM performance (NSE of 0.82 versus 0.86) when combined with forcing bias correction. These advancements provide physics-based snow options for ParFlow-CLM comparable to those in other widely used land surface and snow models. Improved representation of snow water equivalent supports more accurate integrated continental hydrologic simulation over the United States.

title: Physical and numerical modeling of a novel unsaturated multilayered cover system for mining closure
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Yunlong Zhu, Udesh Wijepala, Soumya Roy, Sanandam Bordoloi
abstract: Hydraulic cover systems used in tailings storage facilities (TSFs) in cold region mines commonly depend on thick compacted layers or geosynthetic liners, both of which tend to lose functionality when subjected to prolonged snowmelt or extreme precipitation. This work introduces an alternative cover concept: a lightweight, fully unsaturated multilayered cover system (MLCS) composed predominantly of locally available tailings and waste rock. In this approach, tailings are engineered either through clay–biochar amendment or by inducing surface hydrophobicity, enabling them to function as key components of a capillary-controlled barrier. The MLCS incorporates a capillary break, and a hydrophobic interface specifically designed to trigger water entry pressure (WEP) dependent resistance during severe ponding events. Comprehensive laboratory tests including soil–water retention characteristics, hydraulic conductivity functions demonstrated that modified tailings mixtures exhibit enhanced capacity to delay wetting. The hydrophobic layer, characterized by a WEP of approximately 4.71 kPa, permitted the construction of an exceptionally thin 0.5-m cover while still providing breakthrough resistance. Performance was evaluated using a fully instrumented one-dimensional physical model subjected to a constant ponding head of 115 mm maintained for 61 days. No percolation was detected beneath the MLCS for 61 days, and the hydrophobic interface remained unsaturated even as the overlying layers approached saturation. Coupled finite-element simulations employing WEP-based hydraulic switching reproduced the temporal evolution of suction, moisture distribution, and percolation observed in the physical experiment. Overall, the study shows that the MLCS can function as a robust, climate-tolerant hydraulic barrier and offers a cost-effective closure solution that minimizes reliance on imported geomaterials.

title: Assessing multi-flood hazard zones for stormwater infrastructure in highly urbanized coastal cities
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): L.T. Cardenas-Caro, F.L. Santiago-Collazo, O.M. Viloria-Marimón, J.B. Robider, E.R. Gavin, L.T. Bayer, M.V. Bilskie
abstract: Coastal cities are increasingly exposed to compound flooding driven by interactions between coastal water levels and inland hydrologic processes. While previous studies have focused primarily on overland flooding, compound flood hazard zones (FHZs) within stormwater drainage systems remain poorly understood. This study investigates subsurface compound FHZs using the Storm Water Management Model (SWMM) for two urban watersheds in Savannah, Georgia. Simulations combined two rainfall events (10% and 4% annual exceedance probabilities), astronomical tides, and an intermediate 2050 sea-level-rise (SLR) scenario. Compound FHZs were delineated using conduit-depth-relative transition-zone thresholds (0.5%, 2%, and 5%) and analysed to evaluate water-level profiles, spatiotemporal FHZ behavior, and drainage-network response. Results show that subsurface transition FHZs develop within confined stormwater systems and are highly sensitive to threshold selection, network configuration, and downstream tidal forcing. Under the 0.5% threshold, the coastal FHZ in the Fells Street watershed shortened by approximately 80% under SLR relative to the 10% no-SLR scenario, accompanied by expansion of the transition FHZ and up to an 8% increase in transition-zone water depths. The results further demonstrate that simple linear superposition of isolated rainfall and tidal responses may produce physically unrealistic water levels in confined drainage systems, highlighting the need for dynamically coupled compound-flood simulations. Tidal influence was also observed farther upstream than implied by existing overland FHZ definitions. These findings extend the FHZ framework to subsurface stormwater systems and improve understanding of how tidal backwater, sea-level rise, and drainage-network characteristics influence compound flooding in coastal urban environments.

title: Interval-based multi-objective optimization for multireservoir operation under uncertain inflows
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Li Zhang, Wen-jing Niu, Zhong-kai Feng, Hong-wu Tang, Yang Xiao, Tie-sheng Guan, Tao Yang
abstract: Climate change and evolving water-use patterns have increased the uncertainty involved in cascade reservoir operation. Existing deterministic approaches based on point inflow estimates, as well as scenario-based approaches relying on prescribed probability distributions, may be inadequate for explicitly representing uncertainty propagation across cascade reservoirs and for evaluating the feasibility and risk of joint operation schemes when probabilistic information is limited. This study proposes an interval-based multi-objective operation method for cascade multireservoir systems under uncertain inflows. The proposed method defines inflow uncertainty through prescribed interval bounds and evaluates its operational effects using representative inflow realizations. Sample-based constraint-feasibility assessment and quantitative constraint-violation measures are incorporated to identify feasible operation schemes and characterize their associated operational risks. An interval dominance-based ranking method is further introduced to compare non-dominated schemes with respect to flood control, power generation, and risk characteristics, thereby supporting preference-aware selection among alternative operation strategies. A two-population dynamic cooperation (TPDC) algorithm is employed as the solution engine to efficiently search the constrained interval decision space. A real-world cascade reservoir case study shows that the proposed method can generate well-distributed feasible interval non-dominated solutions, explicitly reveal the uncertainty-related trade-offs between flood-control safety and power-generation benefits, and delineate feasible decision domains under different inflow uncertainty levels. The results further show that objective intervals gradually contract as inflow uncertainty decreases and progressively approach deterministic operation results. The proposed method provides a practical basis for risk-aware and adaptive cascade reservoir operation under uncertain inflow conditions.

title: A novel approach for forecasting lake heatwaves using MSAPE-ML: A deep learning framework with WRF-derived physical features coupled with the air2water model
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Mariusz Ptak, Teerachai Amnuaylojaroen
abstract: Lake heatwaves threaten freshwater ecosystems, yet projections for individual lakes remain scarce. We introduce MSAPE-ML, an LSTM-Attention model whose input features encode analytical relationships derived from the RRTMG, MYNN2, and Noah-MP parameterisations for climate downscaling. Coupled with the air2water ODE lake model and driven by Bayesian model averaging of CMIP6 ensembles, the framework projects heatwave characteristics for 37 Polish lakes under three SSPs, achieving water temperature RMSE of 1.89 ± 0.15 °C (R2 = 0.94). Mean annual heatwave days increase from 23 historically to 84 (SSP1-2.6), 191 (SSP2-4.5), and 334 (SSP5-8.5) by end-of-century. Under SSP5-8.5, discrete events coalesce until 97% of lakes exceed 350 days yr⁻1 above the fixed 1985–2014 90th-percentile envelope by 2100 — a quasi-permanent departure from the historical thermal regime, though fixed ecological thresholds are crossed far less often (17–45 days yr⁻1 above 28 °C by end-of-century). Severity shifts from predominantly Moderate (87%) to Strong-or-above (80%), and occurrence expands into all seasons. Shallow lakes exhibit more intense but shorter heatwaves, while deep lakes experience prolonged events. These projections establish MSAPE-ML as a transferable framework for lake heatwave assessment based on physics-derived features. This regime departure erodes the cool-season recovery windows on which cold-water species depend, while the accelerating exceedance of absolute thresholds (25–28 °C) increasingly favours harmful algal proliferation and eutrophication across Polish lake ecosystems. These projections provide an evidence base for freshwater-specific climate adaptation, including revised thermal discharge regulations and prioritised monitoring of shallow lakes most vulnerable to regime shifts.

title: The importance of measurement uncertainties in the regression of hydrogen and oxygen isotope values
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Matteo Nigro, Michele Barsanti, Stefano Natali, Marco Luppichini, Polona Vreča, Daniele Penna
abstract: The isotopic composition of hydrogen (2H) and oxygen (18O) in water is an established and powerful tool in hydrological sensu lato investigations. Since Craig (1961) first documented the δ2H-δ18O linear relationship in meteoric water across the globe, the Global Meteoric Water Line (GMWL − δ2H = 8 ∗ δ18O + 10), researchers have explored the variability in meteoric water lines both globally and locally. The isotopic composition of precipitation reflects fractionation processes during evaporation, condensation, and moisture transport, which are conditioned by the temperature, humidity, and morphological location of each site. Local Meteoric Water Lines (LMWLs) represent the relationship of δ2H-δ18O at one specific site or area and are used for numerous hydrological, hydrogeological, and ecohydrological applications. A correct computation of LMWLs is, therefore, crucial. Several statistical regression methods have been employed to compute LMWLs: the Ordinary Least Squares regression (OLS), the Reduced Major Axis regression (RMA); the Major Axis regression (MA, also known as orthogonal regression), and the Error-In-Variables regression (Argiriou and Lykoudis, 2006 and Boschetti et al., 2019) which considers measurement uncertainties in δ2H and δ18O. Some landmark papers in isotopes hydrology correctly argued that measurement uncertainties in δ2H and δ18O should be included in the regression methods, and consequently suggested the use of RMA and MA regression as the most suited for computing LMWLs. RMA and MA thus became the most common regression approaches. However, in those works, variables’ uncertainties are not inserted in RMA and MA equations; consequently, uncertainties are not used in the following works. A complete description of the implementation of δ2H and δ18O measurement uncertainties in the computation of MWL regression is absent in the isotope hydrology literature. In this work, we illustrate how to correctly account for measurement uncertainties on both hydrogen and oxygen when performing their linear regression with the long established least-squares estimation (LSE). We discuss the assumptions to carry out the regression, the statistical methodology, and the evaluation of the goodness of fit. When computing the slope and intercept fit parameters the LSE regression is the least biased compared with OLS, RMA, and MA regressions. Four simulations are presented along to better illustrate the method application and evaluation of goodness of the fit statistic. Software tools, in R and Python, for computing the regression of water isotopes data (indeed any data) with uncertainties in both variables are provided. The use of the proposed method provides a better computation of MWLs (and of linear regressions of isotopic data in general) and the possibility of effectively evaluating the goodness of the computed linear fits. This method is not specific and thus applicable to any case in which the X and Y variables are characterised by measurement uncertainties.

title: Agricultural land-use composition modulates hydroclimatic coupling of cropland water use efficiency under prolonged aridification: sub-watershed evidence from Chile’s megadrought
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Francisco Zambrano, Francisco Fernández, María Molinos-Senante
abstract: Cropland water-use efficiency (WUE; net primary productivity divided by actual evapotranspiration) is widely expected to improve under technological intensification, yet its response to prolonged aridification at regional scales is poorly understood. We analyzed spatiotemporal patterns of WUE across 127 Chilean agricultural sub-watersheds from 2001 to 2020, a period spanning an unprecedented megadrought. WUE responses were spatially heterogeneous: arid and semi-arid sub-watersheds showed predominantly negative Δ WUE, while irrigated Mediterranean sub-watersheds showed positive Δ WUE; negative long-term trends and structural breaks were concentrated in the 30–35 ∘ S band. Precipitation deficit indices dominated cross-sectional WUE sensitivity; at the 36-month accumulation scale, SPEI (Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index) and SPI (Standardized Precipitation Index) showed practically equivalent explanatory power (two one-sided tests p < 0.001, 90% CI [−0.004, +0.003]). Crop system composition is associated with WUE drought sensitivity through two contrasting patterns, each constrained by a different form of confounding. Annual-crop prevalence is robustly and negatively associated with drought sensitivity across all latitude-control specifications (spatial error model [SEM] β range: −0.341 to −0.591, p < 0.01); whether this reflects structural buffering or drought-driven reduction of annual cultivation cannot be established from the observational data alone. Irrigation infrastructure prevalence shows a positive association with WUE-drought coupling that is not distinguishable from the latitudinal aridity gradient: it is significant in the full sample (SEM β = +0.438, p < 0.001) but attenuates to non-significance when latitude is explicitly controlled ( β = +0.117, p = 0.309; Δ AIC = 19.8). Geographic cross-validation confirms that the quantitative crop-composition model does not transfer across latitude bands within Chile (per-block out-of-sample R 2 range: −1.25 to −0.29), with every held-out block being predicted worse than its own mean, indicating that the coefficients capture a spatially contingent configuration rather than generalizable structural parameters. Both crop-composition associations are correlational; causal inference is precluded by the observational design and spatial confounding. These findings are consistent with crop-portfolio flexibility reducing structural drought exposure under prolonged aridification, and with WUE-based efficiency metrics being insufficient indicators of agricultural resilience where irrigation supply is hydrologically coupled to the same signals that suppress crop productivity. These results carry implications for water governance and agricultural planning in snowmelt-dependent dryland regions globally.

title: Small floods, not large ones, drive oxygen decline in a subtropical estuary via hydro-biogeochemical coupling
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Dan Yu, Minxiang Zhu, Qihui Zheng, Peng Cheng, Yik-Lam Poon, Yiqi Yu, Xiyu Zhang, Shaobin Li, Nengwang Chen
abstract: River floods mobilize large amounts of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) to estuaries, but how flood magnitude modulates the subsequent estuarine oxygen response remains unresolved. Here we show that small floods (310 m3/s ≤ peak flow < 1030 m3/s), not large ones (≥1030 m3/s), drive dissolved oxygen (DO) decline in a dam-regulated subtropical estuary. By integrating high-frequency monitoring, biodegradation incubations, and hydrodynamic modeling in the Jiulong river-estuary continuum during 2023, we identified two contrasting flood-induced oxygen response pathways. The small floods mobilize phytoplankton-derived DOC from upstream reservoirs, which was highly biodegradable (bioavailable fraction up to 39%, with low SUVA254). Concurrently, these events triggered estuarine algal blooms (Chl-a increased 2.3- to 10.8-fold) due to modest nutrient pulses, improved light availability, and extended water residence time. The senescent bloom provided additional labile carbon. The combination of riverine and autochthonous labile carbon fueled microbial respiration, resulting in a net DO decline of 3%∼17% across the five small-flood events in 2023. In contrast, four large floods deliver predominantly terrestrial and refractory DOC. These large floods induced high turbidity that suppressed algal blooms (no Chl-a peaks), limiting the supply of labile autochthonous carbon. The enhanced vertical mixing promoted re-aeration, while shortened water residence time minimized microbial oxygen consumption. Consequently, oxygen depletion was prevented and yielded a net DO increase of 1%∼8%. This study suggests that river flood magnitude modulates the balance between physical and biological controls on carbon‑oxygen dynamics in the river‑estuary continuum, providing a predictive framework for water quality responses to hydrological extremes in dam-regulated systems.

title: Comparative analysis of rainfall erosivity estimation approaches and temporal resolution effects: A critical review supported by an observational case study
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Athanasios V. Serafeim, Andreas Langousis, Paolo Nasta, Dario Pumo, Nunzio Romano, Roberto Deidda
abstract: Accurate estimation of the rainfall erosivity factor (R-factor) is fundamental for soil erosion prediction and informed land conservation. This study provides a comprehensive review of the historical evolution and current status of R-factor estimation, ranging from simplified empirical equations to complex process-based models. Special emphasis is placed on data requirements, model assumptions, and method transferability. We introduce an alternative process-based algorithmic procedure (AAP) for identifying erosive events that strictly aligns with the original Renard et al. (1997) criteria, effectively mitigating the overestimation of wet spell durations common in traditional approaches. Using a high-resolution (1-min) rainfall dataset from 134 stations in Sardinia, Italy, we evaluate the performance of USLE, RUSLE, and RUSLE2 under various event identification procedures and temporal resolutions (1 to 1440 min). Furthermore, we compare these process-based results against 51 widely used simplified empirical models from global literature. Our analysis reveals a significant dependence of erosivity estimates on temporal resolution; coarser data systematically smooth intensity peaks, leading to substantial R-factor underestimation. Additionally, simplified empirical models exhibit high epistemic uncertainty, with estimates often deviating by over 100% from process-based benchmarks due to local calibration constraints. The study concludes with recommendations regarding possible future research directions, based on important gaps identified in the existing literature.

title: Nitrate attenuation regulated by hydrofacies mean length in heterogeneous riparian aquifers
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Tian Jiao, Jinxi Song, Jing Yang, Yan Zhang, Bing Xu, Ming Ye
abstract: Hydrofacies spatial organization strongly regulates groundwater flow and reactive transport in riparian aquifers, yet the influence of hydrofacies mean length on nitrate attenuation remains poorly understood. We developed a two-dimensional reactive transport model to investigate the effects of hydrofacies mean length on nitrate attenuation in a heterogeneous riparian aquifer under losing-river conditions. Five mean-length levels were combined with five hydrofacies compositions with varying proportions of sand, coarse sand, and silt, yielding 25 hydrofacies configurations. Results showed that increasing hydrofacies mean length generally enhanced river-aquifer exchange, nitrate transport, and nitrogen transformation, with magnitude of these responses strongly dependent on hydrofacies composition. Across the five hydrofacies compositions, increasing mean length from 0.2 to 2.0 times the baseline increased denitrification by 32–84% and nitrate removal efficiency by 8–47%. Coarse-sand-rich aquifers exhibited larger absolute changes in nitrate transport and nitrification, consistent with enhanced transport through more persistent high-permeability pathways, whereas silt-rich aquifers showed greater relative sensitivity to mean length, partly reflecting their lower baseline transport rates. The strongest enhancement in denitrification and the highest nitrate removal efficiency tended to occur near intermediate hydrofacies compositions, where enhanced solute transport coincided with sufficient organic-rich silt to support denitrification. Solute-spreading analysis further showed that increasing hydrofacies mean length enhanced plume spreading across all hydrofacies compositions, but larger increases in spreading did not necessarily translate into greater improvements in nitrate removal efficiency, as the response also depended on organic-rich silt abundance. Thus, hydrofacies mean length influenced nitrate attenuation by modifying hydrofacies persistence, transport pathways, and solute redistribution, while hydrofacies composition modulated the resulting biogeochemical response.

title: Extreme basin-scale flood-dry events induce dramatic alterations in water–sediment dynamics within the Yangtze Estuary
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Ying Zhou, Zhijun Dai, Weihua Li, Xuefei Mei, Wenjun Zeng, Aoyang He
abstract: Against the backdrop of increasing attention to the frequent occurrences of global extreme flood and dry events, understanding how these extreme hydrological events impact estuarine water and sediment dynamics remains insufficient. To address this, this study focuses on the Yangtze Estuary, a typical estuarine system governed by the hydrological processes of the Yangtze Basin, and selects the North Channel (NC), a representative bifurcated branch, as the study area. Based on continuous hydrological observations conducted at eight monitoring stations during the flood seasons of an extreme flood year (2020) and an extreme dry year (2023), combined with water–sediment analyses and the Empirical Orthogonal Function (EOF) method, the spatiotemporal variation characteristics of water and sediment dynamics under extreme hydrological conditions were systematically diagnosed. The results show that the average flow velocity during the extreme flood year reached 1.08 m/s, exhibiting a three-peak longitudinal structure. In contrast, during the extreme dry year, a double-peak structure was observed, with the flow velocity decreasing to 0.85 m/s and stagnant flow characteristics beginning to emerge. In Turbidity Maximum Zone (TMZ), peak flow velocities during the flood year exceeded 1.20 m/s, with Suspended Sediment Concentration (SSC) reaching up to 1.26 kg/m3 and showing a “peak dilution effect.” Conversely, during the dry year, flow velocity significantly weakened, with a peak of only 0.95 m/s, while SSC decreased to 0.66 kg/m3, its high-concentration layer exhibited a more vertically extended distribution. These variations in water and sediment dynamics reveal that during extreme flood year, river runoff suppresses marine tidal effects, leading to an overall increase in estuarine flow velocity and sediment supply. During extreme dry year, tidal effects are significantly amplified, causing the TMZ to migrate upstream. Accordingly, sediment resuspension and deposition are modified, jointly reshaping the estuarine water and sediment transport patterns. This study provides empirical evidence for understanding the response mechanisms of large river estuaries under extreme hydrological conditions.

title: Hydrogeological controls on radial collector well intake: interactions among aquifer properties, clogging, and lateral hydraulics
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Seonmin Lee, Min-Ho Koo, Jaeyun Jung
abstract: Radial collector well (RCW) intake is governed by complex interactions among aquifer properties, river–aquifer connectivity, clogging processes, and hydraulic losses within collector laterals. This study investigates these controls using a coupled aquifer–lateral flow formulation implemented in MODFLOW, in which laterals are represented as Drain cells with iteratively updated heads and conductances to account for near-lateral resistance and internal frictional and momentum losses. A conceptual model was used to examine aquifer hydraulic conductivity and anisotropy, aquitard properties, river-to-caisson distance, filter-pack and riverbed clogging, caisson operational head, and lateral design parameters. Intake increased with aquifer hydraulic conductivity, although the response became nonlinear as lateral head losses intensified. Vertical hydraulic resistance caused by anisotropy or aquitards reduced intake and, under some conditions, produced a finite optimal river-to-caisson distance. Well clogging exerted a much stronger influence than riverbed clogging, and severe reductions in filter-pack hydraulic conductivity reduced intake to near-zero levels. Among the lateral design variables, lateral diameter had the strongest effect, particularly in high-conductivity aquifers. Longer laterals were more effective in low-conductivity aquifers, whereas adding laterals was more beneficial in high-conductivity aquifers, where groundwater could be supplied from multiple directions. These results show that RCW performance depends on the location and magnitude of the dominant hydraulic resistance within the coupled river–aquifer–well system. The findings provide a process-based framework for RCW design, performance interpretation, and clogging management under site-specific hydrogeological conditions.

title: Perturbation of dissolved organic matter reactivity by tributary inflows in a large reservoir unveiled by reactomics and explainable machine learning
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Qiaoqiao Li, Hai Huang, Mingxing Cao, Yixuan Ye, Yuhan Jiang, Hua Ma
abstract: River confluences serve as biogeochemical hotspots in watersheds, yet the molecular-level mechanistic linkage between tributary-induced perturbations in dissolved organic matter (DOM) and their functional consequences for ecosystem processes remains poorly quantified. Here, we integrated ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry, reactomics (inference of reactivity potential networks from periodic mass difference analysis), and explainable machine learning across four confluences in the Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR). We demonstrate that despite tributaries delivering chemically distinct DOM pools, which distinguish urban-derived, protein-like molecules from terrestrial, aromatic compounds, their mixing with the mainstem is predominantly conservative. In contrast, functional profiling revealed that tributary DOM possesses higher intrinsic reactivity potential, with oxidoreductase pathways dominating the reaction network. A discharge-weighted mixing model confirmed overall conservatism in reactivity potential: measured values deviated from conservative predictions by less than ± 5%. We identified a critical exception: a low-discharge tributary created a disproportional reactivity potential hotspot, underscoring that even minor inputs can drive non-conservative processes. Explainable machine learning (SHAP) showed that higher O/C and NOSC values were associated with greater DOM reactivity potential, while higher S/C values were associated with lower reactivity potential. These three features together accounted for > 90% of feature importance, and the site-grouped cross-validated R2 (3 folds) of the XGBoost model ranged from 0.72 to 0.73 across the four reaches (mean = 0.73). Our findings, based on this synoptic survey, establish a framework that links molecular traits to DOM reactivity potential, providing predictive insights for managing carbon cycling and water quality in regulated river systems.

title: Stage-specific water-quality reorganization and spatially differentiated risks during snowmelt in an arid urban river
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Weihong Chen, Huili Bao, Yanyan Li, Rui He, Hao Wang, Dayi Qian, Hongzhi Ma
abstract: Static assessments may underestimate snowmelt-driven water-quality changes in arid urban rivers. Eight sites in the Yining reach of the Ili River were monitored across three snowmelt stages in 2024, with ERA5-Land providing regional hydroclimatic context. Water quality was assessed using the improved comprehensive water quality identification index (ICWQII) with game-theory-based adaptive weighting and ecological risk coding. PMF-PCA, ecological risk and trophic assessments, and exploratory PLS-SEM characterized source-related composition, environmental pressures, and variable associations, respectively. TN exceeded 1.0 mg L–1 in 95.8% of site–stage records. NH3–N declined across stages and consistently met the Class III criterion, whereas NO3 ––N, TP, and COD reached their highest stage means during late snowmelt. Total recoverable Cr reached 0.383 mg L–1 at Y5 during peak snowmelt (Cr-related risks evaluated under conservative upper-bound Cr(VI) screening). Mean ICWQII increased from 2.42 to 3.12 and 3.40, with Y5 reaching 3.82 during peak snowmelt, approaching Class IV. PMF–PCA resolved source-related compositional factors, with F2 associated with domestic inputs during early snowmelt, Cr-dominated F3 contributing 67.67% at Y5 during peak snowmelt, and agriculture-associated F1 contributing over 50% at Y1, Y3 and Y8 during late snowmelt. RI remained low overall; during peak snowmelt, RI and the Cr-specific risk index at Y5 reached 21.48 and 15.31, respectively. Maximum late-snowmelt TLI was 75.91. Exploratory PLS–SEM indicated significant positive associations of F1 with TLI and of F3 with RI and the Cr-specific risk index. These findings reveal stage-specific shifts in water-quality composition and environmental pressures, supporting targeted monitoring and management of snowmelt-affected urban rivers.

title: Dynamic reliability analysis via stochastic unsteady seepage for high core-wall rockfill dams
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Bo Jing, Mingyang Xu, Bin Xu, Yang Zhou, Jianan Shao, Rui Pang
abstract: Seepage safety of high core-wall rockfill dams during impoundment and drawdown is affected by uncertain hydraulic-gradient responses induced by the spatial variability of hydraulic parameters. This study develops a dynamic reliability analysis framework for high core-wall rockfill dams under stochastic unsteady seepage conditions. First, the maximum hydraulic gradient in each material zone is selected as the controlling seepage response. Second, the probability density evolution equation (PDEE) is formulated based on probability conservation and solved using the exponential-spectral mapping method (ESMM) to obtain stochastic response distributions. Furthermore, the equivalent extreme-value event method and two-dimensional joint response distributions are used to evaluate whole-process dynamic reliability and conditional reliability among materials. Finally, the framework is applied to a 300 m-class high core-wall rockfill dam. Results show that high-probability regions of hydraulic-gradient responses migrate toward larger values during impoundment, and reliability reduction mainly occurs during water-level rising stages. During drawdown, most hydraulic gradients decrease, whereas the transition layer fluctuates due to delayed hydraulic-head dissipation and seepage-path redistribution. Joint response distributions provide additional information on the probabilistic relationships between the core wall and adjacent seepage-control materials. The proposed framework supports dynamic reliability assessment and operational safety analysis of high core-wall rockfill dams.

title: Nitrate source–pathway coupling concentration varies across seasons in contrasting land-use catchments
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Xuan Huang, Yuting Xie, Yifan Shen, Xing Yan, Yuhang Zhang, Weiyue Shi, Jian Guo, Dongli She, Yongqiu Xia
abstract: Riverine nitrate loading depends not only on how much each source supplies and which pathway carries it, but on how the two are coupled. Source apportionment and pathway partitioning quantify these components separately, but neither resolves which source reaches the stream through which pathway, so neither shows whether delivery is dominated by a few strong couplings or spread across many weak ones. Using entropy-regularised optimal transport, we coupled isotope-based source apportionment to hydrograph-based pathway partitioning in three sub-catchments of the Qinhuai River Basin representing individual traditional-agricultural, intensive-agricultural and urban sites, in dry and wet seasons. The model routes each source along its least-resistance pathways and resolves allocation to delivery pathways before in-stream attenuation. Coupling was most concentrated in the dry seasons of the traditional-agricultural and urban catchments, where a single sewage–baseflow link carried 29.9% and 30.7% of nitrate, and most diffuse in the traditional-agricultural wet season, where no link reached 20% in the baseline solution. The intensive-agricultural catchment showed no comparable seasonal separation, consistent with the lack of coincident source and pathway dominance within a season. Coupling concentration informed management priorities: the intensive-agricultural fertilizer–surface runoff link was 76–77% re-routable at the defined inflection intensity but carried only 2.9–4.6% of the load, whereas the larger sewage–baseflow link supplied 29.8–30.7% of dry-season nitrate yet was far less responsive to increased transport resistance. Coupling concentration may therefore serve as a case-specific screening diagnostic for prioritizing nitrate management.

title: Linking urban sanitation practices to water resource quality: A multi-tracer approach in a humid tropical context using nitrate isotopes and emerging organic contaminants
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Boris Djieugoue, Bertil Nlend, Suzanne Ngo Boum-Nkot, Kamel Zouari, Rim Trabelsi, Wassef Ben Nasr, Jacques Etame, Frédéric Huneau
abstract: Urban water resources in large cities of sub-Saharan Africa are increasingly impacted by anthropogenic activities, mainly due to the limited access to adequate sanitation systems. In these highly anthropized contexts surface water and groundwater contamination sources are multiple. However, the interactions between these contamination sources and urban water bodies remain poorly investigated, despite the need for such understanding to support sustainable water-resource management. This study applied a multi-tracer approach combining hydrochemistry, nitrate stable isotopes (δ15N-NO3 and δ18O-NO3), and Emerging Organic Contaminants (EOCs) to identify contamination sources and pathways, and to characterize the biogeochemical processes affecting shallow aquifers and surface waters in a tropical urban environment. High Cl/Br molar ratios (>1000), indicated that NO3 – and Cl- primarily originate from domestic wastewater inputs. Enriched δ15N-NO3 (6.6 to 25‰) and δ18O-NO3 (+3.3 to + 9.9‰), further confirmed the predominance of wastewater-derived contamination and revealed the occurrence of partial denitrification processes. Intermediate isotopic ranges (soil organic nitrogen and sewage) suggested the influence of mixed contamination sources. Widespread occurrence of EOCs, particularly persistent contaminants such as fluconazole (FCZ), highlighted the significant impact of wastewater on both groundwater and surface water quality. Strong correlations of FCZ with Cl-, δ15N-NO3, together with their similar spatial distribution, identified FCZ as the most effective wastewater co-tracer in the study area. Furthermore, the co-occurrence of FCZ with non-persistent compounds such as paracetamol indicated recent and continuous wastewater inputs affecting urban water resources. Sporadic detection of non-ubiquitous compounds such as carbamazepine reflects localized wastewater infiltration from septic or pit latrine sources. These results underscore the high vulnerability of shallow urban aquifers and demonstrate the relevance of nitrate isotopes and EOCs coupling to better understand contamination dynamics and support sustainable urban water management.

title: HydroTreeNet: differentiable hydrological process trees for physically consistent rainfall–runoff modeling
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Xuerui Zhou, Baowei Yan, Jianbo Chang, Shixiong Du, Dongxu Yang, Mingbo Sun
abstract: Differentiable hydrological models increasingly combine process structure with neural parameterization, yet jointly representing spatially heterogeneous runoff generation, constrained flux partitioning, and explicit river-network propagation remains challenging. We present HydroTreeNet, a process-constrained differentiable rainfall–runoff framework that integrates node-scale snow and liquid–water storages, generalized complementary allocation at the infiltration, evapotranspiration, and recharge interfaces, and explicit routing over a mapped upstream–downstream river network. The model was evaluated across nine diagnostically selected CAMELS-SPAT catchments using repeated calibrations, validation-tuned neural and conceptual benchmarks, controlled component experiments, and numerical conservation audits. Predictive performance was strongly basin dependent, and no model dominated all catchments. HydroTreeNet was competitive in selected Mediterranean, humid, rain–snow, and large lowland-network settings, but exhibited a pronounced structural failure in an intermittent pulse-flow basin. Removing snow processes reduced NSE by 0.32–0.41 in two snow-influenced basins, whereas removing explicit network routing reduced NSE by up to 0.20 in several selected basins. Whole-system water-balance residuals remained below 2 × 10−7 relative to cumulative input, while repeated-seed differences in internal states revealed persistent equifinality despite similar outlet skill. HydroTreeNet therefore provides an auditable framework for separating predictive behavior, structural hypotheses, and numerical conservation within differentiable rainfall–runoff modeling; broader transferability and process realism require larger-sample, held-out-basin, and independent-state evaluation.

title: Soil water movement and vapor effects in cold-region sandy land: implications for diurnal evaporation at the soil–atmosphere interface
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Li Lu, Menglu Wang, Shinian Wang, Xiaosi Su, Rongda Li, Hang Lyu, Tiejun Song, Xiaofang Shen, Weihong Dong
abstract: Vapor transport is important in coupled soil water–heat processes, but how temperature-gradient variations and liquid–vapor partitioning reorganize internal water transport and regulate diurnal evaporation after dry surface layer (DSL) formation remains unclear. This study combined lysimeter observations from the Songnen Sandy Land with HYDRUS-1D simulations of coupled liquid water–vapor–heat transport to quantify shallow flux partitioning and controls on thermally driven vapor flux ( q vT ). Total soil water flux was generally dominated by isothermal liquid flux ( q lh ). During dry periods, q vT increased markedly within the 3–10 cm layer, contributing 7–14% and up to 45% around midday. Temperature gradients determined q vT direction, whereas soil moisture regulated its magnitude through gas-phase connectivity. After DSL formation, evaporation showed a pronounced morning enhancement–midday suppression transition: nighttime vapor retention allowed actual evaporation ( E a ) to approach potential evaporation ( E p ) shortly after sunrise, whereas subsequent downward q vT offset upward q lh and reduced effective water supply. This transition formed the core of a four-stage pattern of nighttime recharge, morning enhancement, midday suppression, and weak afternoon recovery. Rainfall suppressed q vT by weakening near-surface temperature gradients and gas-phase connectivity, with delayed post-rainfall recovery. Sensitivity analyses showed that n exerted the strongest control on daily evaporation and vapor redistribution, whereas water-table depth had limited effects because the capillary fringe remained below the vapor-active layer. Although vapor transport did not dominate the overall water balance, it regulated the timing and effectiveness of shallow water supply, helping explain diurnal soil–atmosphere water exchange in cold-region sandy land.

title: How reporting cadence shapes hourly precipitation extremes
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Marc Semper, Manuel Curado, Jose F. Vicent, Leandro Tortosa
abstract: Hourly precipitation products are often assembled from station records with heterogeneous sub-hourly reporting cadences, yet users rarely know how much of the resulting difference in extreme diagnostics reflects temporal support, clock-hour alignment, the aggregation implementation, or the temporal structure of the rainfall. We present a controlled coarsening framework that separates these four causes within a single experiment in which the meteorology is held fixed and precipitation mass is conserved. That separation, rather than the well-established attenuation of short-duration intensity under aggregation, is the contribution. Using three years (2023–2025, UTC) of 5-min observations from 30 AVAMET stations in eastern Spain, we coarsen the same records to 15-, 30- and 60-min reporting across all phase offsets and reconstruct hourly products by naive and by overlap-aware aggregation. For the 99th percentile of the hourly interval-rate maximum during wet hours, the relative difference reaches − 69.6 % at 60-min reporting, and − 76.0 % when reporting windows are aligned with clock hours, so it is not an artefact of phase shifts. It is strongly regime-dependent: − 66.2 % for temporally concentrated rainfall against − 5.2 % for distributed rainfall, which is almost cadence-invariant. A cadence- and regime-aware correction reduces systematic differences but leaves substantial residual uncertainty, and an independent replication at 30 DWD 1-min stations (2023–2024) reproduces the main cadence-dependent signatures of the mechanism. Hourly extreme diagnostics should therefore not be treated as directly comparable across stations unless temporal support, phase alignment, aggregation method and rainfall regime are accounted for.

title: Soil evaporation dominates shifts in evapotranspiration seasonality in the Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Zelong Yang, Xiaomang Liu, Kaiwen Wang, Kang Liang, Zhengjie Yin, Changming Liu
abstract: Understanding the seasonal dynamics of evapotranspiration (ET) is essential for assessing intra-annual water availability and regional water security. Although widespread shifts in ET seasonality have been well documented, how individual ET components shape these shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we used two metrics—the center of mass concentration (CMC) and center of mass timing (CMT)—to characterize the seasonality of ET and its components across the Yangtze River Basin during 1980–2023. A novel decomposition framework was developed to quantify the contributions of individual components to changes in ET seasonality (ΔCMC and ΔCMT). The results show that ET in the Yangtze River Basin has shifted toward an earlier and less concentrated seasonal regime. Decomposition analysis demonstrates that soil evaporation (E b) is the largest contributor to shifts in both seasonal ET concentration and timing, contributing 47% and 57% to the ΔCMC and ΔCMT of ET at the basin scale, respectively. In contrast, although vegetation transpiration (E t) is the largest ET component in the basin and exhibits seasonal changes consistent with ET, its contributions to ET seasonality shifts (42% and 35%) are smaller than those of E b. This is because the increasing magnitude of E t amplifies its intrinsically later and more concentrated seasonal characteristics relative to ET, thereby partially offsetting the contribution arising from its own seasonal shifts. These results show that the effects of ET components on ET seasonality shifts depend not only on changes in their magnitude and seasonality, but also on their seasonal phase relationships with total ET. Overall, our findings provide new insights into the mechanisms through which individual ET components drive ET seasonality shifts.

title: Physics-guided virtual sensors for low-cost spatial inference of river water quality under sparse monitoring
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part B Author(s): Yue Zheng, Weitian Chen, Huihui Wang, Yiping Zhang, Yongchao Zhou, Raziyeh Farmani
abstract: Spatially distributed river water quality information is essential for effective monitoring and management. However, the cost of installing and maintaining in situ monitoring stations limits the spatial coverage of river water-quality observations. This study developed a physics-guided virtual sensor to reconstruct water quality at sparsely monitored sites using adjacent-station observations and meteorological data. A long short-term memory (LSTM) encoder-decoder was trained with a regularization term that penalizes disagreement with estimates from an analytical advection–dispersion model. The framework was trained and tested using hourly observations of conductivity, dissolved oxygen, ammonia nitrogen, and total phosphorus from five river monitoring stations during 2021–2023.
