Their fertility is therefore more likely controlled by high magmatic H2O contents, which may promote deep magma storage in transitional mid- to upper-crustal reservoirs and focused fluid release through porphyry fingers.

title: Source evolution controls the molybdenum isotope composition of Archean continental crust
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Eric D. Vandenburg, Oliver Nebel, Laura M. Spencer, Marc-Alban Millet, R. Hugh Smithies, Peter A. Cawood, Alexandra Churchus, Wenli Liang, Emilie Bruand, Jean-François Moyen, Alex McCoy-West, Priyardarshi Chowdhury
abstract: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. Numerous studies have investigated its stable metal isotope character to understand its formation and secular evolution. Molybdenum (Mo) isotopes are useful tracers of petrogenetic processes in Phanerozoic igneous rocks, but Archean granitoids, which make up much of Earth’s early continental crust, remain poorly characterized. Here, we report high-precision whole-rock Mo isotope data for 28 Archean granitoids from Australia’s Pilbara and Yilgarn cratons, with crystallization ages from 3.52 to 2.63 Ga. The samples cover a spectrum of magmatic series, including tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG), TTG hybrid, sanukitoid, potassic, and potassic hybrid magmas. After assessing the effects of alteration, crustal contamination, and fluid exsolution, we interpret the observed δ 98/95Mo range of −0.93 to +0.25‰ as primarily reflecting magmatic source characteristics. TTG and TTG hybrid granitoids, together with samples derived from unenriched meta-mafic or mantle-like sources, have mean and median δ 98/95Mo values close to, or slightly higher than, chondrite and depleted MORB mantle (DMM). In contrast, potassic, potassic hybrid, and sanukitoid series granitoids, as well as samples derived from enriched meta-mafic or felsic crustal sources, extend to lower, sub-mantle δ 98/95Mo values. Elemental proxy relationships, major- and trace-element modeling, and phase-equilibrium constraints indicate that source composition and residual mineralogy during partial melting primarily control Mo isotope variability in these rocks. In crustally-derived granitoids, lower δ 98/95Mo values are associated with more mature source compositions and with changes in the abundance and composition of residual feldspar. Amphibole, garnet, and biotite may also have subordinate effects. These relationships suggest that Mo isotopes track the progressive reworking of Archean crust. Juvenile crust-derived TTG magmatism is characterized by near- to suprachondritic δ 98/95Mo, whereas later sanukitoid and potassic granitoid magmatism, linked respectively to mantle metasomatism and reworking of TTG-dominated gray gneiss, shifts toward lower δ 98/95Mo values. The observed trends imply that intracrustal reworking alone can push continental averages to sub-mantle values, with ramifications for mass-balance models. Although TTGs are generally suprachondritic, their δ 98/95Mo values are not high enough to easily support models requiring large volumes of Hadean to Paleoarchean continental extraction from a chondritic mantle to offset the subchondritic Mo isotope composition inferred for the depleted mantle from Archean komatiites. The strong Mo isotope contrast between continental crust and upper mantle may therefore have developed after 2.6 Ga, once crustal recycling became more extensive.

title: Nitrous oxide cycling and isotopic overprinting in lake basins with contrasting mixing regimes
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Teresa Einzmann, Moritz F. Lehmann, Annie Bourbonnais, Jakob Zopfi, Fabio Lepori, Claudia Frey
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas and ozone-destroying substance, and lakes contribute variably to its atmospheric budget. We investigated the seasonal variability of N2O cycling in two contrasting basins of Lake Lugano, Switzerland: the meromictic North Basin (NB) and the holomictic South Basin (SB). Over one full seasonal cycle, we measured N2O concentration and site-specific isotopomer compositions to assess spatio-temporal dynamics. Both basins showed near-neutral N2O exchange with the atmosphere, without clear seasonal patterns of N2O emission versus uptake (average air–water exchange flux of 0.04 ± 0.3 µmol m−2 d−1). Keeling-plot analysis indicated a nitrification-driven N2O source in the oxic water column in both basins, as inferred from its position-specific isotopic nitrogen composition. In the anoxic water column in the North Basin, N2O was persistently depleted, whereas in the deep South Basin N2O consumption was observed only during late-stage stratification. Net N2O consumption in the hypolimnia of both basins was accompanied by isotopic shifts toward lighter δ15Nbulk and δ15Nβ values, contrary to trends observed in pure cultures. These inverse apparent isotope effects suggest concurrent N2O production during net consumption. Using a simplified box-model (i.e., isotope mass balance) approach, we estimated that 5–17% of the consumed N2O needed to be replaced by simultaneous N2O production in order to match the observed in situ δ15Nbulk-N2O data. Our findings highlight the complexity of N2O cycling in lake systems and reveal that isotopic overprinting from simultaneous N2O production and consumption can obscure traditional isotope-based interpretations. At the same time, they underscore the value of stable isotopes in disentangling N2O production and consumption mechanisms.

title: Porewater nitrate isotope dynamics in selected benthic habitats: Modulation by sediment reactivity and process coupling via nitrite
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Alessandra Mazzoli, Peter Reichert, Cameron M. Callbeck, Claudia Frey, Paul M. Magyar, Tim J. Paulus, Donald E. Canfield, Sergei Katsev, Jakob Zopfi, Moritz F. Lehmann
abstract: Denitrification is the primary pathway for fixed nitrogen (N) removal from aquatic systems. Its occurrence in sediments is promoted by suboxic conditions, high organic matter reactivity, sharp redox transitions, and the co-occurrence of multiple N-transformation processes. Benthic denitrification can be investigated through natural abundance nitrate N and oxygen (O) isotope ratio measurements to trace nitrate reduction and related N-transformation processes within the sediment. Yet, while the biological and apparent (i.e., in the overlying water) isotope effects for nitrate reduction, εDen, have been widely investigated, the controls on their expression at the sediment porewater level remain underexplored, particularly in lacustrine systems. Additionally, it is unclear how simultaneously occurring N-cycle processes may modify the resulting nitrate isotope signatures. Since apparent εDen values are commonly used to estimate benthic denitrification, it is also crucial to identify how these processes affect their expression. Here, we measured nitrate isotope ratios in sediment porewaters from multiple lacustrine and marine settings and quantified denitrification, dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium, and anammox rates using 15N-tracer incubations. We further employed a novel diagenetic N isotope model to estimate εDen under different sedimentary reactivity and redox conditions. In most investigated environments, Rayleigh-derived N and O isotope effects are strongly reduced (mostly < 4‰) in porewaters compared to reported biological isotope effects, whereas model-based estimates provide intermediate fractionations. We attribute the generally low isotope fractionation to high sediment reactivity and insufficient nitrate diffusion to the nitrate-reducing zone, leading to near-complete nitrate consumption at the microbial level (i.e., before the cellular level effect is expressed at the porewater level). Consistent with this interpretation, environments characterized by higher organic matter reactivity exhibited the lowest isotope fractionation. The N and O isotope values in nitrate exhibited partial decoupling, resulting in both negative and positive Δδ18O:Δδ15N deviations from 1:1. Negative deviations may reflect an enhanced contribution of the periplasmatic nitrate reductase, particularly in lacustrine environments with fluctuating O2 concentrations. Positive deviations likely indicate nitrate (re)generation via nitrification or anammox, and tight nitrate-nitrite redox cycling (i.e., nitrate reduction coupled to nitrite oxidation). The spatial overlap of N transformations (e.g., nitrification–denitrification) in our model results increased the coupling of processes through nitrite, which strongly influences nitrate isotope dynamics. Model simulations indicate that nitrite-reducing processes generate 15N-enriched nitrite due to N isotopic fractionation; subsequent nitrite oxidation, associated with an inverse kinetic isotope effect, produces highly 15N-enriched nitrate. Such 15N enrichment of nitrate should therefore not be interpreted as evidence for nitrate reduction and fixed-N loss. Our findings demonstrate that explicit consideration of nitrite dynamics is essential for correctly interpreting nitrate isotope data in sediment porewaters and for avoiding inaccurate estimation of benthic N-transformation pathways and N-loss rates.

title: Oxygen isotope exchange unravels million-year long hydrogeochemical evolution of a deep carbonate aquifer in the Swiss Molasse Basin
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Christoph Wanner, Lukas Aschwanden, Mirjam Kiczka, H. Niklaus Waber, Michael Heidinger, Emiliano Stopelli, Daniel Traber
abstract: The stable isotope composition of groundwaters is essential to characterize their origin and processes of their hydrogeochemical evolution. In carbonate aquifers, the interaction between groundwater and carbonates enriched in 18O may shift groundwater δ18O values to the right of the global meteoric water line. Although experimental studies showed that the exchange of oxygen isotopes between groundwater and carbonates may proceed rapidly under ambient conditions, there is little information regarding the kinetics of the exchange under geological conditions. To better quantify the relevance of carbonate-groundwater interaction on oxygen isotope signatures of both groundwater and carbonates, we present an extensive hydrogeochemical characterization of deep groundwaters collected during a deep drilling campaign in the Swiss Molasse Basin. Combining information from chemical and isotopic analyses, groundwater residence time tracers, the geological evolution of the area, as well as geochemical modeling we quantitatively demonstrate that the exchange of oxygen isotopes is mainly relevant for carbonate-dominated aquifers consisting of fractured rock with a low porosity and a large solid to liquid ratio. For such conditions, isotopic equilibrium is reached in more than a few hundred thousand but less than 20 Mio years at temperatures below 70 °C. It follows that the equilibration of groundwater δ18O values may serve as independent proxy for the residence time of very old groundwaters. Moreover, our study shows that for rock buffered systems the oxygen isotope exchange has only minor effects on the oxygen isotope composition of rock-forming calcite. Accordingly, it does not affect the use of the δ18O signature of calcite as environmental proxy.

title: Volcanically driven manganese mineralization mediated by carbonate substrates during the Early Triassic
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Li Wang, Ling Gan, Chenchen Yang, Yinqiang Zhao, Hai Xu, Runsheng Yin, Hanjie Wen
abstract: Sedimentary manganese (Mn) deposits are critical Mn resources whose formation is intricately linked to marine redox conditions. This study conducts mineralogical, elemental, and mercury (Hg) isotopic analyses of the Early Triassic Dongping sedimentary Mn deposit (South China) to constrain the drivers of Mn deposition. Manganese ore layers exhibit anomalously high Hg concentrations and Hg/TOC ratios, indicating intense volcanism during Mn mineralization. The temporal coincidence of Mn mineralization (∼250 Ma) with Siberian Traps eruptions points to a causal link. Mn ores, dominated by rhodochrosite with minor Mn calcite and kutnohorite, exhibit core-rim structures, indicating nucleation on pre-existing carbonate (calcite/dolomite) surfaces followed by crystal growth and/or metasomatic replacement. Redox-sensitive elements (Mo, U, V) and Ce/Ce* ratios reveal a transition from oxic to anoxic conditions during mineralization, with a return to oxic conditions post-mineralization. Based on these findings, we propose a three-stage metallogenic model: (1) Volcanic CO2 emission during this period sustained greenhouse warming, enhanced continental weathering, and increased nutrient influx into oceans, promoting primary productivity, ocean stratification and frequent shifts in the oxic-anoxic interface; (2) Redox changes in the oceans drove large-scale Mn deposition in the form of rhodochrosite at basin margins; and (3) Pervasive carbonate grains facilitated rhodochrosite nucleation and growth. This work establishes a genetic link between Siberian Traps volcanism and Early Triassic Mn ore formation, and offers key insights into the genesis of shallow-water sedimentary Mn deposits.

title: Prebiotic organic compounds in asteroid Bennu and Ryugu reflect divergent parent body histories
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Angel Mojarro, José C. Aponte, Daniel P. Glavin, Jamie E. Elsila, Jason P. Dworkin, Harold C. Connolly
abstract: The return of pristine samples from carbonaceous asteroids Ryugu by JAXA’s Hayabusa2 mission and Bennu by NASA’s OSIRIS-REx mission has enabled the direct comparative study of prebiotic organic compounds across the two primitive bodies. Using pyrolysis, thermochemolysis, and one-pot derivatization coupled to gas chromatography-triple quadrupole-mass spectrometry, we analyzed free volatile, insoluble, and soluble organic matter in a Ryugu aggregate and compared results to a Bennu aggregate and stones of interest. Pyrolysis of the Ryugu sample revealed polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, their alkylated homologues, and sulfur-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-bearing heterocyclic aromatic compounds consistent with aqueous alteration of the parent body. One-pot derivatization of the Ryugu aggregate yielded only tentative detections of β-alanine and 2,4-diaminopyrimidine. This is in contrast to the 14 proteinogenic α-amino acids and five canonical nucleobases previously detected across Bennu samples using the same technique. Thermochemolysis of the Ryugu sample revealed limited methylated derivatives while Bennu samples did not yield compounds above the procedural blank. The sparse thermochemolysis detections in samples from both asteroids are notable given that diverse methylated derivatives have been reported from the Orguiel (CI1) and Murchison (CM2) meteorites. We interpret these results as most likely originating from reagent-mineral interactions suppressing TMAH yields. Overall, contrasting organic inventories reflect divergent-parent body histories. Results from the Ryugu samples are consistent with a CI1-like classification, displaying increased alkylation of insoluble organic matter alongside depleted soluble organic matter abundances. In contrast, Bennu preserves heterogeneous organic signatures across stones recording multiple distinct alteration episodes. The presence of prebiotic molecules including amino acids and nucleobases across both asteroids further highlights the significance of carbonaceous bodies in contributing the chemical building blocks of life throughout the early Solar System.

title: Zinc isotope evidence for intrusive Siberian Traps magmatism during the end-Permian mass extinction
description: Publication date: Available online 22 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Na Li, Mengchun Cao, Guolin Xiong, Yi-Bo Lin, Mohammad N. Gorgji, Dongxun Yuan, Guangyi Wei, Thomas J. Algeo, Quan-feng Zheng, Hua Zhang, Shu-zhong Shen
abstract: The end-Permian mass extinction (EPME) coincided with catastrophic changes in global climate, the carbon cycle, marine redox conditions and nutrient cycling. Volcanism associated with the Siberian Traps Large Igneous Province (STLIP) is widely recognized as a primary driver of these changes. However, the mechanisms by which different modes of magmatism influenced marine biogeochemical cycles remain incompletely resolved. Here, we present high-resolution zinc isotope (δ66Zn) records through the Permian-Triassic transition from two well-preserved marine carbonate successions located on opposite margins of the Paleotethys Ocean: Dajiang (South China) and Abadeh (Iran). Despite marked differences in paleogeographic setting and depositional environment, both sections display comparable δ66Zn ranges and coherent stratigraphic trends. Both records exhibit a pronounced negative δ66Zn excursion of ∼ 0.5–0.6‰ in the uppermost Permian that is closely associated with the onset of the negative δ13C excursion, indicating a broadly coeval perturbation to the marine zinc and carbon cycles prior to the EPME. Carbonate-hosted δ66Zn values records remained perturbed throughout the lowermost Triassic, suggesting that disruption of the marine Zn cycle in shallow-marine environments extended beyond the initial biotic crisis. Mass-balance constraints indicate that changes in biological utilization alone are insufficient to explain the observed isotopic shift. We suggest that a sustained input of isotopically light Zn to the ocean–atmosphere system is likely to account for the excursion, plausibly linked to large-scale sill-complex intrusions and contact metamorphism associated with STLIP magmatism. Sustained low δ66Zn values following the extinction coincided with an enhanced influx of isotopically light Zn during peak thermogenic devolatilization, whereas reduced deposition of Zn-bearing organic matter likely represented a secondary effect on the marine Zn cycle. Our results demonstrate that shallow-marine carbonates preserve first-order changes in shallow seawater δ66Zn associated with large-scale perturbations of the marine Zn cycle and highlight the role of prolonged, sill-dominated intrusive magmatism in altering marine Zn source-sink balance during the end-Permian environmental crisis

title: Recycling of juvenile arc crust in an ancient convergent margin revealed by Hg isotopes
description: Publication date: Available online 21 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Han Qi, Jun-Hong Zhao, Runsheng Yin, Anbo Luo
abstract: Recycling of newly formed arc crust at convergent margins is critical to the long-term balance between growth and destruction of the continental crust. However, identifying this process in ancient convergent systems remains challenging because direct geological evidence is rarely preserved. Here, we measure Hg stable isotopes and Nd–Hf radiogenic isotopes in subduction-related igneous rocks from the Neoproterozoic (870–730 Ma) active continental margin of the Yangtze Block in South China to investigate the recycling of juvenile arc crust. Both mafic rocks and granitoids exhibit variable whole-rock Δ199Hg values that largely overlap the depleted-mantle range, ranging from −0.13‰ to +0.15‰ (mean = −0.04 ± 0.15‰, 2SD) and −0.18‰ to +0.11‰ (mean = −0.05 ± 0.14‰, 2SD), respectively, suggesting variable contributions from mantle-, marine-, and terrestrial-derived Hg. Samples with negative Δ199Hg signatures show variable but mostly positive whole-rock εNd (−3.4 to +6.4) and positive zircon εHf (+1.8 to +14.7), and all samples with Δ199Hg below the depleted mantle range (< −0.10‰) have positive εNd values (+0.3 to +3.1). These combined isotopic characteristics indicate that terrigenous sediments formed by weathering and erosion of juvenile arc crust and carrying terrestrial-derived Hg were recycled into the mantle source of arc magmas. Such recycling was likely achieved through subduction of arc-derived trench sediments and/or tectonic erosion of forearc materials. The results of this work suggest that recycling of newly formed arc crust in convergent margins may have been an overlooked means of crustal destruction throughout Earth’s history.

title: Electrostatic discharge triggers troilite‑to‑magnetite oxidation in Mars dust activity
description: Publication date: Available online 20 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Xiaojia Zeng, Xiongyao Li
abstract: Electrostatic discharge in Martian dust storms may significantly drive the chemical alteration and cycling of surface materials. Troilite is expected on Mars from magmatic and meteoritic sources but remains undetected by rovers, raising the question of possible electrostatic discharge-driven alteration. However, this hypothesis lacks direct experimental support. In this study, we experimentally simulate electrical discharge under Martian conditions by exposing troilite to such discharge in a CO2 atmosphere at low pressure. We found that electrical discharge rapidly oxidizes troilite to magnetite (Fe3O4), forming a ∼ 100 nm thick, polycrystalline, defect-rich alteration layer on the troilite surface. This oxidation is driven by reactive oxygen species attack Fe-S bonds, displace sulfur, and convert the residual iron framework into magnetite. Such an electrical discharge-driven pathway offers a new water-free mechanism for magnetite formation on Mars, specifically active during the hyper-arid Amazonian epoch. This work also provides an additional explanation for the missing troilite in Martian soils and the widespread occurrence of magnetite in Martian dust. More broadly, this study expands our understanding of Martian surface evolution beyond water-dominated scenarios and highlights oxidative role of ongoing dust activities on present-day Mars.

title: Simultaneous formation of DNA and RNA nucleosides in shock-recovery experiments
description: Publication date: Available online 16 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jiawen Zhao, Koichi Mimura
abstract: Whether RNA, DNA, or both emerged as the first genetic system remains an important question in origin-of-life research. The RNA world hypothesis proposes that RNA preceded DNA, whereas alternative scenarios allow for the coexistence of RNA- and DNA-related building blocks during early chemical evolution. A key chemical question is whether deoxyribonucleosides can be generated abiotically from molecular precursors that could have been available under prebiotic conditions. Meteorite impacts generate transient high-pressure and high-temperature conditions that can promote rapid chemical reactions in solid-state environments. Here, we investigate the formation of ribonucleoside and deoxyribonucleoside frameworks from ribose and canonical purine and pyrimidine nucleobases under simulated meteorite impact conditions. Shock compression generated both ribonucleoside and deoxyribonucleoside frameworks during a single shock event. Single- and dual-13C-labeling experiments confirmed the incorporation of carbon from both ribose and nucleobase. Experiments conducted under different reaction conditions showed that nucleoside yields and product distributions varied with mineral composition, organic loading, nucleobase composition, and water content. These results demonstrate that shock compression provides a solid-state reaction regime in which both ribonucleoside and deoxyribonucleoside frameworks can be generated from common molecular precursors. This study provides experimental constraints on nucleoside formation and the environmental factors affecting this process under impact-driven conditions.

title: Bomb- 14 C signals in santa barbara basin sediments and radiocarbon constraints on terrestrial organic carbon
description: Publication date: Available online 16 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Hanyue Xu, Hong-Chun Li, Da-Wei Li, Meng Yu, Hailong Zhang, William M. Berelson, Meixun Zhao
abstract: The anthropogenic bomb-14C signal (produced by nuclear bomb tests in the atmosphere during 1945 ∼ 1964 yr CE) provides a powerful tracer for quantifying organic carbon (OC) dynamics in marine sediments. This study uses two 210Pb-dated box cores (SBB-190629 and SBB-8-2012) from the Santa Barbara Basin (SBB), and the measured total organic carbon (TOC), total nitrogen, δ 13C and Δ14C of TOC (Δ14CTOC) to track the propagation of bomb-14C signal. Although bulk sedimentary Δ14CTOC values were strongly negative (−384‰ to −64‰), a distinct Δ14CTOC enrichment (up to ∼ 90‰) was identified in both cores after 1960 yr CE. This enrichment is identified as a bomb-14C event through its temporal synchronicity with the Δ14C records of established atmospheric carbon dioxide and surface seawater dissolved inorganic carbon. To deconvolve this signal, we employed a series of mixing models. A δ 13C-based binary mixing model was used to quantify the marine and terrestrial OC fractions since 1815 yr CE. Subsequently, the time-parallel surface seawater dissolved inorganic carbon radiocarbon record was used as the marine end-member to reconstruct the Δ14C composition of terrestrial OC. Finally, through the application of a petrogenic-biospheric mixing model, we revealed a significant bomb-14C enrichment within the biospheric component of the terrestrial OC and quantified a stable, background contribution of 14C-free petrogenic carbon (∼18%). Our findings demonstrate the attenuation of the bomb-14C signal through a complex terrestrial-marine system can still be recorded on sediment in SBB. This study establishes a framework to disentangle the bomb-14C signal on marine, biospheric-terrestrial, and petrogenic-terrestrial components. It also provides an approach for interpreting radiocarbon data in continental margin sediments and for constraining carbon cycling processes across these dynamic interfaces.

title: Rapid changes to permeable, continental shelf sediment pore water geochemistry in response to olivine addition as a marine carbon dioxide removal technique
description: Publication date: Available online 16 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Matthew Quinan, Aaron Celestian, Nick Rollins, Zvi Steiner, William Berelson
abstract: Marine enhanced rock weathering using the silicate mineral olivine has emerged as a promising ocean alkalinity enhancement/marine carbon dioxide removal technique in recent years. However, we lack an understanding of olivine dissolution and the concomitant alkalinity production in a marine sedimentary environment, where much of the dissolution is likely to occur, and the geochemical feedbacks therein. Previous olivine enhanced rock weathering experiments have typically been conducted at high fluid-to-mineral ratios using sediments composed predominantly of olivine, conditions that are not representative of olivine addition to natural sedimentary environments. They have also generally been done over long time periods (i.e. weeks to months) to obtain steady state dissolution/alkalinity production rates, thereby looking past the early, transient impacts of fresh olivine addition to marine sediment. Our uncertainty is compounded by the heterogeneity of continental shelf sediments, where variations in composition, grain size, permeability, diagenetic reactions, and pore water flow are likely to produce spatially variable olivine dissolution and alkalinity production. To help close these knowledge gaps, we conducted experiments to investigate the impacts of olivine dissolution on sediment geochemistry immediately following addition to shelf sands under varying physical conditions, all producing consistent results. Olivine dissolution and/or ion exchange resulted in rapid alkalinity production, even at short fluid:mineral contact time (residence times) and low fluid:mineral ratios. However, the precipitation of secondary minerals (CaCO3, Fe oxides, and potentially phyllosilicates) consumed a substantial portion of the produced alkalinity (28–88%), while increasing pore water pH slowed further olivine dissolution/ion exchange. These saturation effects decreased the efficiency with which alkalinity was durably produced by olivine dissolution in the sediment.

title: Coupled kinetics of Mn(II) oxidation and Cd sequestration on ferrihydrite with varying crystallinity
description: Publication date: Available online 15 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Lizhu Xu, Meiying Huang, Tongliang Wu, Peixin Cui, Cun Liu, Yujun Wang
abstract: Ferrihydrite (Fh) serves as a crucial geochemical interface for Mn(II) adsorption-oxidation in various soils and sediments, influencing the fate of associated Mn and cadmium (Cd). However, the impact of Fh crystallinity on the coupled kinetics and mechanisms of Mn(II) oxidation and Cd sequestration remains incompletely understood, particularly regarding the kinetic interplay. Here, we systematically investigated these coupled reactions on two-line Fh (2LFh with low crystallinity) and six-line Fh (6LFh with high crystallinity). 2LFh has a lower isoelectric point, a lower conduction band potential (E CB), and more abundant vacancy defects, while 6LFh exhibits higher isoelectric point and E CB but fewer vacancy defects. Kinetic experiments across pH 6.0 − 8.0 revealed similar trends in Cd and Mn(II) removal, with the most pronounced effects observed at pH 8.0. Based on the most pronounced reaction extents observed at pH 8.0, we developed a kinetic model that quantitatively describes the crystallinity-dependent kinetic coupling in Fh-Mn(II)-Cd ternary system. Dissolved Cd(II) and Mn(II) were rapidly adsorbed onto both 2LFh (k Cd = 5.43 × 106 M−1 s−1, k Mn(II) = 5.28 × 102 M−1 s−1) and 6LFh (k Cd = 2.85 × 105 M−1 s−1, k Mn(II) = 1.37 × 103 M−1 s−1). Subsequently, Mn(II) catalytic oxidation by O2 proceeded preferentially on 6LFh via an electrochemical pathway, driven by its higher E CB. This facilitated the abundant formation of amorphous manganese oxide (AMO) and groutite nanorods. In contrast, Mn(II) oxidation on 2LFh predominantly yielded abundant AMO and moderate amounts of manganite nanowires. Although secondary MnOx formation on Fh surfaces transiently increased dissolved Cd(II) by 1.3 − 15.8% relative to the Mn-free system, the extractable Cd fraction progressively decreased by 2.1 − 24.0%, with substantial Cd immobilized in secondary MnOx. Mechanistically, the model captures these Mn(II) oxidation pathways and dynamic redistribution of Cd between Fh and MnOx surfaces. These findings highlight that Fe‑Mn redox cycling and secondary mineralization critically govern the fate of heavy metals in redox‑dynamic soil environments, with crystallinity-dependent reaction pathways providing key mechanistic insights

title: A new view of Xe and Ne in the Paleoarchean atmosphere from paired noble gas isotopic and trace element analyses of Barberton cherts
description: Publication date: Available online 15 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): K.A. Woody, R. Parai, D.A. Fike, C. Jones, G. Avice, M.H. Barickman, J.B. Rodriguez, X.J. Zhang, A.H. Knoll
abstract: The terrestrial atmosphere governs Earth’s habitability and remains our most accessible analogue to distant planetary atmospheres, making the evolution of its composition over Earth history a topic of great interdisciplinary scientific interest. Many different natural samples are capable of trapping and retaining atmospheric gases on billion-year timescales, providing a geochemical archive of bygone processes. These trapped gases record a progressive depletion in the abundance of xenon (Xe) accompanied by its isotopic fractionation in Earth’s Archean atmosphere. However, the detailed history of this loss and isotopic fractionation of Xe is imperfectly constrained, in part because calculations focus on the non-radiogenic light isotopes of Xe (which are the least abundant isotopes) to determine ancient atmospheric compositions. In this study, we employed the full spectrum of Xe isotopes measured in four cherts from the 3.55–3.26 Ga Onverwacht Group of the Barberton Greenstone Belt, South Africa to quantify Xe isotopic fractionation in the Paleoarchean atmosphere. First, we measured the concentration and spatial distribution of Te, Ba, U, and Th by secondary ion mass spectrometry in subsamples of each chert to estimate the expected composition of Xe produced in situ by nuclear reactions. We then analyzed chips of these subsamples for Ne, Ar, and Xe elemental and isotopic compositions. We find that Xe data from Onverwacht bulk cherts reflect mixing between Paleoarchean atmospheric Xe and modern atmospheric Xe, with minor inputs from Xe produced by U, Ba, and Te decay. A mixing model incorporating these five components and testing a range of possible Archean atmospheric compositions indicates that Xe in the ∼ 3.26–3.28 Ga atmosphere was fractionated by ≥ 19 - 3.2 + 3.1 ‰u−1 relative to modern air. Our results emphasize that even samples with noble gas compositions dominated by trapped ancient fluids may in detail reflect multicomponent mixing, and that estimates of the extent of mass-dependent Xe fractionation reported in previous studies are lower limits. Barberton chert 20Ne/22Ne ratios extend below the modern atmospheric ratio, which could reflect post-entrapment fractionation that preferentially retained heavy Ne isotopes, or may indicate the preservation of a trapped multi-component mixture including paleo-atmospheric 20Ne/22Ne that was subsequently raised by volcanic outgassing

title: Molybdenum redistribution and extreme isotope fractionation in a Barremian weathering profile revealed by scientific drilling
description: Publication date: Available online 14 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qin Lin, Philip A.E. Pogge von Strandmann, Ming-Dao Sun, Peng-Li He, Le Zhang, Man Li, Yi-Jun Xiong, Jin-Long Ma, Jie Li, Yi-Gang Xu
abstract: Molybdenum (Mo) redistribution and isotope fractionation during continental weathering provide an important link in the biogeochemical cycles in Earth’s history, but their preservation in ancient weathering systems remains poorly constrained. Complete palaeo-weathering profiles are rarely recovered without overprinting by modern weathering. Here, we investigate Mo mobility and isotope behavior in the YSDP-1 scientific-drilling core from the Chaoyang Basin, Northeast China. The continuous core intersects a ∼ 17 m-thick Barremian palaeo-weathering profile preserved between two andesite flows, which records a downward gradation from calcrete to saprolite. Relative to the fresh andesite, the calcrete is Mo-depleted and shows limited Mo isotope fractionation. In contrast, through the gradational transition into saprolite, whole-rock Mo concentrations increase and the δ98Mo values decrease significantly to a minimum of −3.36‰. In-situ analyses show that Mo is concentrated mainly in saprolite-hosted pyrite, and pyrite separates yield lighter δ98Mo values of −3.43 to −3.66‰. Together with Fe speciation and S content variations, the results indicate depth-focused sequestration of isotopically light Mo at a subsurface Fe–S reduction front in a redox-stratified weathering system. Such profiles may act as isotopic filters, substantially altering exported Mo isotope signatures with little change in Mo concentrations or fluxes, with implications for marine and lacustrine records and low-oxygen weathering on early Earth and Mars.

title: Nickel isotope fractionation by EDTA complexation
description: Publication date: Available online 13 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yen-Po Lin, Chih-Chiang Hsieh, Shotaro Takano, Kuo-Fang Huang, Tung-Yuan Ho
abstract: The marine biogeochemical cycling of nickel (Ni) has recently emerged as an important research topic, with studies suggesting that Ni isotopes may serve as a proxy for tracing marine nitrogen fixation. Field studies in low-to-mid latitude surface waters typically report nutrient-type dissolved Ni patterns alongside enriched Ni isotopic signatures, indicating a biological preference for lighter isotopes. However, a laboratory culture study utilizing the organic chelator EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid) to regulate metal bioavailability has found relatively heavy Ni isotopes in phytoplankton cells. Ni in both natural seawater and culture media is predominantly complexed by organic ligands, whereas phytoplankton primarily take up non-EDTA-bound Ni. This raises the question of whether the discrepancy between field observations and laboratory results arises from abiotic fractionation induced by EDTA complexation. In this study, we first developed an anion-exchange chromatography method to effectively separate and quantitatively recover non-EDTA-bound Ni ions and organic Ni-EDTA complexes (Ni(EDTA)2−). Through optimization of analytical conditions, we achieved complete separation with total recoveries of 100 ± 4%. While separation efficiency slightly decreased at pH 5 due to partial breakthrough of Ni-EDTA from the resin, optimal separation was achieved under neutral to alkaline conditions (pH 7 and 9), where non-EDTA-bound and EDTA-bound Ni were stably partitioned. Isotopic analysis revealed that Ni(EDTA)2− is significantly enriched in light isotopes, leaving the residual non-EDTA-bound pool isotopically heavy. The measured isotopic fractionation, Δ60Ni(Ni(EDTA)2−–Ni2+) = −1.65 ± 0.27‰, defines the isotopic offset between EDTA-bound and non-EDTA-bound Ni species under neutral to alkaline conditions and agrees with theoretical predictions based on coordination environment and zero-point energy effects. The abiotic fractionation induced by EDTA chelation is substantial and may potentially mask and confound biological isotope signatures. Our study provides a critical methodological foundation and a necessary correction framework for laboratory trace metal incubation studies, enabling more accurate interpretation of Ni isotope fractionation in EDTA-amended, environmentally controlled experiments. Such a large isotopic fractionation induced by EDTA complexation also suggests that isotopic fractionation may occur between organically complexed and inorganic Ni species in natural seawater.

title: Lead isotopes trace interhemispheric transport of water masses and pollution to the tropical western North Atlantic Ocean
description: Publication date: Available online 12 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Hui Xu, Tina van de Flierdt, Arianna Olivelli, Yee-Lap Leung, Alex Griffiths, Katharina Kreissig, Barry J. Coles, Dominik J. Weiss, Rebekah E.T. Moore, Rob Middag, Mark Rehkämper
abstract: The use of leaded gasoline significantly impacted North Atlantic seawater during the 20th century, leaving a legacy of pollution that remains traceable despite the global ban reached in 2021. This study presents new Pb concentration and isotope data from four depth profiles in the western tropical North Atlantic along Leg 2 of GEOTRACES section GA02 from 31.7°N to 1.2°N. The data capture atmospheric inputs and water masses from both hemispheres, revealing latitudinal variability in Pb isotope signatures in the upper part of the water column. In surface waters, low 206Pb/207Pb ratios (1.166–1.173) indicate South American and North African anthropogenic sources at the southern stations, and higher 206Pb/207Pb ratios (1.174–1.179) reflect anthropogenic North American and natural North African mineral dust inputs at the northern stations. A comparison of North Atlantic surface water data for 1981–1999 and 2010–2014 reveals distinct shifts in Pb concentrations and isotope ratios, confirming the effectiveness of Pb isotopes as tracers for identifying and tracking Pb sources over time in the North Atlantic. The Pb concentrations and isotopic signatures of central water masses (formed 4–15 years ago relative to sampling time) and intermediate water masses (formed 20–50 years ago) are consistent with the expected atmospheric Pb sources at the time and location of their formation, emphasizing the influence of both spatial and temporal variations in atmospheric Pb deposition. However, in the intermediate layer, where northern- and southern-sourced water masses mix, a deviation of the Pb concentration from the expected water mass mixing trend suggests removal of some dissolved Pb by particles. North Atlantic Deep Water exhibits persistent anthropogenic Pb signals from historical US and European emissions (20–30 years ago), while bottom waters within a nepheloid layer show evidence of natural Pb release from sediments. Overall, these findings suggest that Pb isotope ratios predominantly act as conservative tracers of water masses in the strongly advective western tropical North Atlantic Ocean.

title: Multi-site Li diffusion and coupling to Cr, REE, and P in garnet: Experimental data and implications for interpreting diffusion profiles in natural systems
description: Publication date: Available online 11 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): E.M. Bloch, A. Devoir, O. Müntener, R. Hervig, J.J. Barnes, M.J. Kohn
abstract: We present diffusion experiments on almandine and spessartine garnet conducted at 700–900 °C and 1 atm under Ni–NiO fO2 buffering, designed to evaluate the role of coupled substitution and defect chemistry in controlling Li mobility. Experiments employing source powders doped with Li and either REE or P demonstrate that Li diffusion varies systematically with the identity of the coupled species. In REE-doped systems, Li profiles evolve over the same length scale as REEs and yield diffusivities consistent with established REE diffusion rates, indicating that Li transport is limited by the slower trivalent cation flux. In contrast, undoped Li-out diffusion experiments produce substantially longer Li profiles over identical timescales, reflecting faster transport. Comparison with published inversions of multielement diffusion in natural garnets reveals no clear inconsistency between those natural datasets and experimentally derived slow REE diffusivities, supporting application of the Li–REE results to natural systems. Lithium–Phosphorus experiments yield extremely short P diffusion profiles, consistent with a much slower Li mechanism involving P on the tetrahedral site. Additional experiments reveal fast Li transport associated with multi-site diffusion behavior and with processes linked to Cr redistribution. Across all experiments, effective Li diffusivity varies by at least three orders of magnitude as a function of experimental conditions and substitution mechanisms. These results demonstrate that Li diffusion in garnet cannot be described by a single Arrhenius relationship but instead reflects a spectrum of coupled and multi-site diffusion mechanisms. The dataset presented here likely captures only a subset of the mechanisms active in natural systems and Li diffusivity may span an even broader range than we observe here. Consequently, quantitative interpretation of Li diffusion in natural garnets requires consideration of multiple diffusion mechanisms, potentially including processes not yet characterized, and should be approached with appropriate caution

title: Halogen behavior during high-grade metamorphism and partial melting in the deep continental crust (Ivrea-Verbano Zone, NW Italy)
description: Publication date: Available online 9 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Peng-Yuan Han, Madison S. Huising, Jaime D. Barnes, Michael A.W. Marks, Tao He, Fernando Bea, Zhao-Chu Hu, Roberta L. Rudnick
abstract: Halogen (F, Cl, Br, and I) concentrations and Cl isotope (δ37Cl) ratios in a suite of well-characterized amphibolite- to granulite-facies metapelites, metabasites, and associated leucosomes from the Ivrea-Verbano Zone (IVZ), Northwest Italy, document halogen behavior during high-grade metamorphism and partial melting of the deep continental crust. With increasing metamorphic grade, metapelites record a progressive decrease in F, I, and possibly Br concentrations, likely due to metamorphic dehydration. By contrast, Cl is slightly elevated in granulite-facies metapelites, suggesting a relatively Cl-rich environment in the lower crust. Together with previously reported high Cl contents (up to 0.3 wt%) in garnet-hosted melt inclusions produced during partial melting of metapelites, this suggests that the elevated Cl was present during peak metamorphism and partial melting. All samples (metapelites, metabasites, and leucosomes) exhibit scattered but relatively narrow δ37Cl values, ranging from −1.3 to + 0.8‰, indicating that minimal Cl isotope fractionation occurs during metamorphic dehydration, partial melting, and fluid infiltration in the deep continental crust. The inferred Cl-rich environment in the IVZ lower crust is consistent with the Cl enrichment observed in many other granulite terranes, suggesting that such fluids may be common. Moreover, halogens present in the lower continental crust, whether released by metamorphic dehydration or introduced from other parts of the crust and/or mantle, may have facilitated partial melting and the generation of granitic magma, playing a vital role in the chemical differentiation of the continental crust

title: Apatite in Chang’e-6 mare basalts reveals a heterogeneous distribution of chlorine in the Moon
description: Publication date: Available online 8 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Sen Hu, Mengfan Qiu, Linxi Li, Hejiu Hui, Jialong Hao, Huicun He, Yubing Gao, Liang Gao, Zhan Zhou, Mahesh Anand, Wei Yang, Yangting Lin, Xian-Hua Li, Fu-Yuan Wu
abstract: Chlorine (Cl) serves as a crucial volatile element, providing insight into the magmatic processes and volatile inventory of the Moon. The lunar rocks have notably elevated Cl isotopic compositions; however, no information is available about the Cl and its isotopes on the farside. Here, we report a petrographic, chemical, and Cl isotopic study of apatite in the Chang’e-6 (CE6) mare basalt collected from the South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin. CE6 mare apatite was measured to have a Cl abundance of 0.04–3.36 wt%. We estimated a Cl abundance of ∼0.6 μg g−1 for the CE6 mantle source, slightly higher than that (0.26–0.32 μg g−1) estimated from Apollo low-titanium mare basalts and lower than that (∼1.3 μg g−1) of Chang’e-5 low-titanium mare basalt. Cl abundances in the mantle source of low-titanium mare basalts exhibit a positive correlation towards the crystallization ages, highlighting a heterogeneous distribution of chlorine in the lunar mantle. The measured chlorine isotopic compositions (δ37Cl, 14.5 ± 2.0‰ to 27.2 ± 2.2‰) are mostly higher than that of nearside mare basalts (0–20‰). CE6 mare apatite shows a positive correlation between Cl abundances and Cl isotopic compositions, comparable with the trend defined by the low-titanium mare apatite collected from the nearside hemisphere. We infer that the high δ37Cl values of CE6 mare apatite were associated with magmatic fractionation of Cl coupled with an elevated chlorine isotopes in the mantle source, favoring the model that the massive formation impact event of SPA would have imprinted the chlorine isotopic compositions in the underlying mantle rocks.

title: Boron isotope fractionation in siliceous hot spring sinters: Geochemical implications for biosignatures
description: Publication date: Available online 8 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Eizo Nakamura, Chie Sakaguchi, Katsura Kobayashi, Nghiem Van Dao, Elena Kalinina, Hidehisa Tsuchida, Steven W. Ruff, Luke Steller, Martin Van Kranendonk, Ayrton Hamilton, Kathleen Campbell
abstract: Siliceous hot spring sinters preserve coupled mineralogical, geochemical, and isotopic signatures generated during microbial silicification and therefore represent valuable archives of biosignature formation. However, the mechanistic criteria for distinguishing biologically influenced silicification from abiotic silica precipitation remain poorly constrained. Here we present paired boron-isotope and comprehensive multi-element datasets (up to 57 elements) for opaline silica sinters and coexisting waters from four hydrothermal systems spanning a wide range of physicochemical conditions (pH 2–8; 30–98 °C): the Taupo Volcanic Zone (New Zealand), Misasa (Japan), Puga (India), and El Tatio (Chile). Hydrothermal waters exhibit a relatively restricted range of δ11B values (≈ −5 to − 1‰, except Puga at ≈ −13‰), whereas associated silica sinters display much larger isotopic variability (≈ −10 to − 40‰), with in situ secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) analyses revealing microscale domains with values as low as − 50‰. Strongly negative δ11B values are systematically associated with boron enrichment (up to > 10,000 ppm), laminated microbial fabrics, and enrichments of multivalent and high-field-strength (HFS) cations. Stepwise leaching experiments and SIMS observations indicate that the measured boron-isotope signatures predominantly preserve primary depositional characteristics despite minor localized evaporative modification. To explain these coupled observations, we propose an EPS microenvironmental reactor model in which microbial activity within EPS-rich microenvironments generates localized physicochemical conditions distinct from those of bulk fluids. Within these microenvironments, local pH gradients associated with microbial activity promote the formation of tetrahedral borate, while EPS-associated multivalent and HFS cations facilitate boron retention during early opal-A polymerization. Progressive silica precipitation preferentially immobilizes isotopically light boron, producing strongly negative δ11B values together with characteristic multi-element enrichments. The model provides a mechanistic framework linking microbial activity, aqueous boron speciation, element partitioning, and silica precipitation, thereby accounting for the observed hierarchy of boron-isotope fractionation across geothermal systems spanning acidic to alkaline conditions. These findings indicate that opaline silica exhibiting δ11B ≤ − 20‰, together with boron enrichment, HFS-cation enrichment, and stromatolitic microfabrics, provides a powerful and testable geochemical criterion for biologically influenced silicification. Such negative δ11B values extend far beyond those of primary silicate reservoirs and, when coupled with complementary elemental and microstructural evidence, are consistent with biologically influenced boron sequestration during silica precipitation. The consistency of this signature across chemically diverse hydrothermal environments, together with its potential preservation in Paleoarchean hydrothermal deposits, suggests that boron isotopes offer a valuable tool for evaluating biosignatures in ancient terrestrial hydrothermal systems and silica-bearing environments, including Mars.

title: Archaeal lipid hydrogen isotope fractionation reveals carbon and energy metabolism in seep ecosystems
description: Publication date: Available online 6 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jiachen Fan, Hongxiang Guan, Zeji Wang, Xiaoyan Xu, Xiaoming Miao, Qi Li, Huaichun Wu, Sanzhong Li, Nengyou Wu
abstract: The hydrogen isotope composition (δ2H) of lipid biomarkers from aquatic and terrestrial organisms is a key paleohydrological proxy. However, the biogeochemical controls on the δ2H of archaeal lipids remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed δ2H values of archaeal lipids from seep carbonates collected at two seep sites: Haima, South China Sea, and AC818, Gulf of Mexico. The hydrogen isotope fractionation (ε2H) between anaerobic methanotrophic archaea (ANME)-derived isoprenoids and porewater ranges from −227‰ to −205‰ (interquartile range). Across all existing data from seep carbonates and sediments, ε2H values average −218 ± 23‰, which indicates mixotrophic physiology based on the reported values for autotrophs (−252 ± 39‰) and heterotrophs (−203 ± 24‰). This pattern is consistent with the lifestyle of ANME, which aggregate with sulfate-reducing bacteria and consume methane, a metabolic mode fundamentally different from that of axenic cultures of non-ANME archaea. Based on our data and those from pure cultures, we suggest that archaeal ε2H is primarily controlled by carbon metabolic mode (autotrophic vs. heterotrophic) rather than respiratory mode (aerobic vs. anaerobic), and more fundamentally, by cellular bioenergetic status. This interpretation is quantitatively evidenced by its universal negative correlation with metabolic energy yield (ΔG/n), reflecting control of cellular bioenergetic status that integrates both energy yield and demand. ANME-1 lipids show relatively negative ε2H (−233 ± 29‰) and positive ε13C (−53 ± 9‰) compared to ANME-2 (−211 ± 21‰ and −62 ± 6‰, respectively), which is consistent with a divergence in carbon source utilization: ANME-1 may rely more on autotrophic CO2 fixation, whereas ANME-2 adopts a more mixotrophic strategy with greater dependence on methane. Collectively, our findings suggest that archaeal lipid ε2H has the potential to serve as a proxy for cellular bioenergetic status, complementing δ13C-based reconstructions of carbon metabolism, and providing a promising framework for deciphering archaeal bioenergetics in modern and ancient ecosystems.

title: Diagenetic pathways and preservation of bulk and amino acid δ 15 N in bivalve shell organic matter across the Holocene to the Pliocene
description: Publication date: Available online 6 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qian Huang, Kirsty E.H. Penkman, Ellie Nelson, Daniel Vigelius, Thomas Tütken, Lukas Fröhlich, Bernd R. Schöne
abstract: Nitrogen isotope (δ15N) records preserved in mollusc shells have strong potential to reconstruct changes in nitrogen sources, transformations and transport in the ocean beyond instrumental observations. This is because mollusc shells can be precisely dated and often preserve highly temporally resolved records. In addition to bulk nitrogen isotope analysis, compound-specific nitrogen isotope analysis of amino acids (CSIA-AA) further enables the separation of biogeochemical processes from the trophic effects. However, the extent to which bulk and amino acid-specific δ15N are preserved in shell-bound organic matter in (sub-)fossil materials over the multi-millennial to multi-million-year timescales remains poorly understood. Furthermore, intra-crystalline organic matter (intra-OM), which is encapsulated inside calcium carbonate biomineral units, has not been systematically evaluated for its ability to preserve original isotopic signals relative to total shell organic matter (total-OM). Here, we investigate the effects of diagenesis on bulk and amino acid-specific nitrogen isotope compositions in the shell-bound organic matter (both intra-OM and total-OM) of the long-lived bivalve Arctica islandica, a well-established geochemical archive in the North Atlantic. We analysed live-collected and sub-fossil shells spanning the Holocene from the northern North Sea and fossil specimens from several Crag formations in East Anglia, UK, dating to Plio-Pleistocene. Using spectroscopic, chemical, and isotopic approaches, we assessed the preservation of the biomineral structure, shell organic chemistry and nitrogen isotope compositions in bulk shell organic matter (δ15NBulk) and their amino acids (δ15NAA). Only minimal modifications of the original aragonitic shell mineralogy were detected as indicated by low (<5 %) calcite content in all specimens analysed from the different studied time periods (Plio-Pleistocene, Early or Mid-Holocene, Late Holocene and Modern). Then we identified a diagenetic trajectory in which inter-crystalline organic matter was progressively lost through open-system interactions during taphonomy, reflected by declining nitrogen content and convergence of amino acid compositions between total-OM and intra-OM. In contrast, intra-OM remained physically protected within the biomineral matrix and retained nitrogen over ca. 2–3 million years, despite internal molecular reorganisation including peptide hydrolysis and selective loss of labile amino acids (e.g., serine and threonine). Given lack of net nitrogen loss, intra-OM showed robust preservation of δ15NBulk. However, while δ15NAA of intra-OM in Holocene shells retained patterns consistent with limited diagenetic alteration, CSIA-AA δ15N patterns in Plio-Pleistocene shells deviated from the Holocene pattern, even within intra-OM, with changes in the relative isotope spacing among amino acids associated with degradation. These findings provide mechanistic insight linking organic matter preservation and nitrogen isotope preservation in molluscs shell biomineral archives and highlight intra-OM as a promising substrate for reconstructing past marine nitrogen cycling within certain diagenetic limits.

title: Salinity-driven controls on arsenic mobility in naturally coated sands: multi-mineral sorption, kinetic limitations, and metal-facilitated transport
description: Publication date: Available online 6 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Lucien Stolze, Massimo Rolle
abstract: Arsenic mobility in groundwater is sensitive to hydrodynamic and hydrochemical perturbations, yet the coupled mechanisms controlling arsenic transport in natural sands remain poorly constrained. This study uses a series of column experiments, combined with chemical extractions, surface microscopy, and reactive transport modeling, to explore how transient pore-water chemistry and co-existing mineral surfaces in sandy porous media control arsenate transport under oxic conditions. The detailed experimental investigation and the quantitative model-based interpretation, coupling surface complexation reactions with kinetic mass transfer limitations, allowed us to identify three concurrent hydrogeochemical processes governing As partitioning and transport: (i) an increase in salinity mobilizes aluminum, which complexes with arsenate in the pore water and facilitates its transport; (ii) background cations exchange with protons on the silica surface, lowering the pore water pH and promoting protonation of the metal oxide coatings, which increases As sorption onto these coatings; (iii) major ions adsorb as outer-sphere complexes on the oxide coatings, modifying the surface charge and thereby the binding of arsenate, which is enhanced at circumneutral pH. The first mechanism favors arsenic mobility while the latter two promote its retention, producing a biphasic breakthrough under saline perturbation. Furthermore, kinetic mass-transfer limitations significantly favor As elution and indicate that equilibrium, complete mixing assumptions can substantially overestimate the true retention capacity of an aquifer. Our findings show that these coupled mechanisms have important implications for As mobility in natural porous media under transient hydrochemical conditions and need to be simultaneously considered.

title: Solubility of tholins in hexane, acetonitrile, and acrylonitrile: Implications for Titan’s lakes
description: Publication date: Available online 6 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yohann Layssac, Troy L. Williams, Rohana Liyanage, Jackson O. Lay, Vincent F. Chevrier
abstract: Aerosols formed in the atmosphere of Titan sediment and accumulate on the surface where they may interact with the liquid hydrocarbons and organics composing the lakes and seas. In this study, Titan tholins made from nitrogen and methane (95/5) exposed to a cold plasma discharge have been mixed with acetonitrile, acrylonitrile, hexane and a saturated solution of acetonitrile in hexane, under an inert atmosphere at room temperature. The liquid phase has been monitored through time (days to weeks) using gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy has been used to characterize tholins before and after solubilization events, in both the near and mid infrared regions. Infrared spectra do not show differences induced by the interaction of tholins with the liquid phases used in this work. Gas chromatograms indicate that many organics are extracted from our tholins in acetonitrile, with the characterization of nitriles, amines and other nitrogen bearing molecules. Among the three other solvents tested, only acrylonitrile shows limited solubilization of organics from tholins, but no structure could be identified. Pure hexane fails to solubilize any organics detectable in our conditions, as expected by its nonpolar nature. Despite the high solubility of our tholins in acetonitrile, no organics are solubilized when this molecule is saturated in hexane. The positive results obtained with polar solvents (acetonitrile and acrylonitrile) and the negative results obtained with nonpolar liquid phases (hexane with or without acetonitrile) are consistent with previous studies. However, these studies also showed that the composition of tholins is highly dependent on the conditions used for their synthesis, which cannot capture the complexity of Titan’s atmosphere where many processes co-exist. This suggests that Titan haze could contain a rich reservoir of organics that, given the geological timescales available, would make the presence of dissolved organics in the lakes and seas a real possibility.

title: Accessory mineral control on δ 88/86 Sr variation during granitic magma evolution and implications for tracing fluid-melt interaction
description: Publication date: Available online 5 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Nian-Qin Zhang, Yi-Xiang Chen, Kun Zhou, Xu-Qi Chen, Fang Huang
abstract: The formation and differentiation of granitic magmas play a fundamental role in the growth and evolution of continental crust, as well as in the formation of metal ore deposits. Stable Sr isotopes show great potential for tracing fluid-melt interaction during the extensive evolution of granitic magmas. However, the effect of mineral crystallization on stable Sr isotope variation in such magmas remains poorly constrained. To address this issue, we report the stable Sr isotope composition (δ 88/86Sr) of syn-exhumation granites from the Sulu ultrahigh-pressure metamorphic belt. The granites exhibit a wide range of δ 88/86Sr values (−0.63‰ to +0.53‰), mostly lower than those of the mantle and upper continental crust. Petrological observations and whole-rock geochemical compositions suggest that such variations cannot be explained by post-magmatic alteration or assimilation of country rocks. In addition, thermodynamic modeling shows that partial melting of granitic gneiss produces only a slight decrease in δ 88/86Sr values of ca. 0.13‰. Although feldspar crystallization can induce significant stable Sr isotope fractionation, the opposing effects of plagioclase and K-feldspar largely offset each other and cannot explain the observed values. Furthermore, trace element ratios (Zr/Hf, K/Rb, and Nb/Ta) provide no evidence for extensive fluid-melt interaction. Instead, mineral-separate analyses show that apatite has substantially higher δ 88/86Sr values than those of the corresponding whole rocks, whereas titanite and epidote-group minerals show smaller and more variable heavy isotope offsets. The stable Sr isotope variations in the granites correlate with geochemical proxies of accessory mineral fractionation, such as P2O5, TiO2, Nb/Zr, and LREEs, suggesting that the crystallization of such Sr-rich minerals is the dominant factor driving δ 88/86Sr values to as low as −0.63‰. Therefore, fractional crystallization of accessory minerals is proposed to be the primary mechanism for generating light Sr isotopic compositions in the Sulu syn-exhumation granites. These results underscore the pivotal role of accessory minerals in the geochemical evolution of granitic magmas and demonstrate the sensitivity of stable Sr isotopes as tracers of accessory mineral behavior during crustal differentiation. While stable Sr isotopes have great potential for tracing fluid-melt interaction, caution should be exercised because only samples with δ 88/86Sr values lower than ca. −0.6‰ can be more reliably ascribed to such a process. Moreover, by combining Sr-Ba-Fe isotope systematics, we can decode a progressive crystallization sequence from feldspar and mica crystallization to late-stage precipitation of Fe-Ti oxides and Sr-rich accessory minerals during granitic magma evolution.

title: Quantitative constraints on fluid-induced extreme oxygen isotope fractionation from crystal–fluid interactions in highly evolved granite–pegmatite systems
description: Publication date: Available online 4 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Zhen-Hua Wang, Chang-Zhi Wu, Ru-Xiong Lei, Xiang-Long Luo, Matthew J. Brzozowski
abstract: The mechanisms of rare metal mineralization within highly evolved granite–pegmatite systems remain a topic of debate, particularly regarding the role of magmatic–hydrothermal processes in rare metal enrichment. While hydrothermal fluids play a critical role in transporting rare metals in some mineralizing systems, their transport effectiveness varies significantly depending on their origin and physicochemical properties. The highly evolved F–Rb-rich Baishitouquan (BST) pluton is a representative rare metal granite–pegmatite system in NW China. It exhibits a progressive lithological transition from amazonite-free granite in the lower lithological zones (LLZ) to amazonite-rich granite and pegmatite veins in the middle lithological zones (MLZ) to amazonite-poor granite in the upper lithological zone (ULZ), which formed as a result of the magmatic–hydrothermal evolution of a single granitic melt. Accordingly, this pluton provides a unique opportunity to investigate the mechanisms of rare metal mineralization through quantitatively constraining the origin and physicochemical properties of fluids, and by evaluating how these fluids drive geochemical fractionation during magmatic–hydrothermal evolution. This is accomplished here by characterizing the δ18O values of microtexturally and chemically heterogeneous domains in zircon and quartz from the different lithological zones of the BST pluton. Magmatic zircon domains (Zrn-I; δ18OZrn-I = 5.88–7.39‰) have δ18O values that reflect that of the parental granitic melt. In contract, quartz phenocrysts (δ18OQtz = 8.71–10.97‰) and hydrothermal zircon domains (Zrn-II and Zrn-III; δ18OZrn-II = 6.67–12.18‰; δ18OZrn-III = 15.03–20.69‰) exhibit systematically elevated δ18O values. Quartz record syn-magmatic hydrothermal perturbations, whereas hydrothermal zircon domains reflect post-magmatic crystal-fluid interactions and progressive isotopic re-equilibration. The transition from magmatic to hydrothermal conditions is constrained between the oxygen isotope closure temperatures of the Zrn-I domain (∼698 °C) and quartz (∼527 °C). The fluid evolution trajectory is reconstructed from zircon–fluid oxygen isotope fractionation relationships, in which Zrn-I defines the initial isotopic state of the fluid in equilibrium with the magma, whereas Zrn-II and -III record progressive isotopic re-equilibration with evolving hydrothermal fluids during cooling. Modeling results demonstrate that fluid-induced geochemical fractionation during fluid evolution generates pronounced intra-crystal heterogeneity in both oxygen isotopes and trace elements. The quantitatively reconstructed δ18Ofluid–temperature trajectory of the hydrothermal fluids that exsolved from the BST granitic magmas demonstrates that their internal evolution, driven by progressive cooling and crystal–fluid interactions, is sufficient to trigger extreme oxygen isotope fractionation and pegmatite formation without requiring an influx of externally derived fluids.

title: Impact-induced formation of low-Ca pyroxene in a partially melted troctolitic clast from the Chang’e-5 lunar regolith
description: Publication date: Available online 4 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yang Bai, Zhuang Guo, Yuqi Qian, Shichuan Sun, Jingru Ma, Kangjun Huang, Li-Hui Chen, Yunpeng Dong, Simon A.T. Redfern, Charles K. Shearer, Guochun Zhao
abstract: The composition of the lunar deep interior remains debated, as remote sensing observations indicate that impact-excavated materials from within and around large basins contain both olivine and low-Ca pyroxene (LCP). Here we show a partially melted exotic troctolitic clast from Chang’e-5 lunar soils that records impact-induced mineral transformations. The exotic clast consists of forsteritic olivine grains with magnesium-rich rims and pyroxene crystals embedded in a feldspathic glassy matrix. Pyroxene crystals occur as elongated aggregates, with dendritic crystallites growing along the grain edges. The elongated pyroxene crystals show distinct zoning, with Fe-enriched, low-Ca cores and Al-enriched, high-Ca rims, while the dendritic crystallites are compositionally identical to the rims. Elemental mass-balance considerations suggest that impact-induced melting and recrystallization of olivine and anorthite generated the observed LCP–Al-rich high-Ca pyroxene (HCP) assemblage, with Si released during anorthite transformation compensating for the substantial Si consumption during LCP formation. These observations indicate that the LCP formed through impact-induced partial melting of an olivine-rich troctolite under rapid cooling conditions, rather than being a primary phase excavated from the lunar deep interior. Our findings demonstrate that LCP signatures observed around large impact basins, e.g., Imbrium and South Pole-Aitken basins, may originate from impact-modified olivine-rich lithologies, rather than being directly excavated from the deep interior. These results raise the possibility that such transformations may be a widespread process associated with large-scale impacts on the Moon and have important implications for the interpretation of remote sensing data and constraints on the composition of the lunar interior.

title: Sulfur isotope fractionation during metal–silicate equilibration and implications for Earth’s mantle
description: Publication date: Available online 3 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Lucas Calvo, Jabrane Labidi, Anat Shahar, Edith Kubik, Julien Siebert
abstract: Sulfur (S), a moderately siderophile and volatile element, may have been delivered to Earth during the planet’s main stage of accretion. Alternatively, it may have been supplied by the late veneer, after the core was fully segregated from the mantle. Mid-ocean ridge basalts present a systematic depletion in the heavier S isotope, 34S, relative to chondrites. This has been suggested to reflect isotopic fractionation during core–mantle differentiation or during evaporative loss from Earth’s magma ocean. Two studies have estimated the metal–silicate S isotope fractionation but yielded conflicting results. Laboratory experiments suggest that equilibrium fractionation favors the heavy 34S in metal during metal–silicate equilibria. However, the magnitude of the 34S/32S fractionation between metal and silicate appears too small to explain the composition of mid-ocean ridge basalts. In contrast, ab-initio calculations predict fractionation in the opposite direction, with a much smaller magnitude. Here, we present a series of experiments conducted with the triple-isotope technique. This approach allows for a robust determination of sulfur isotope fractionation between metal and silicate. We also report a set of conventional time-series experiments with variable starting isotopic compositions, and compare the results from both approaches. The reported results confirm that metal–silicate equilibration produces significant 34S-depletion in silicates, with a magnitude of 0.65 ± 0.28‰ at 1673 K, in agreement with previous experimental work. This fractionation is parametrized as a function of temperature to account for Earth’s mantle composition following 1000 ∗ ln α M e t . - S i l . ≈ a / T 2 = 1.819 ± 0.784 × 10 6 K - 2 . This fractionation can explain most depleted mantle estimates; however, additional processes such as the effect of high-pressure equilibrium, sulfide–melt equilibria, or long-term mantle recycling may contribute to the observed Earth’s mantle regional variations.

title: Recycling of terrestrial mercury in modern subduction zones: constraints from Hg-Sr-Nd-B isotope systematics
description: Publication date: Available online 2 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Dian-Bing Wang, Ping-Ping Liu, Runsheng Yin
abstract: Mercury (Hg) isotopes, particularly mass-independent fractionation (MIF; expressed as Δ199Hg), serve as a powerful tracer for tracking the recycling of surficial materials into Earth’s deep interior. However, the contribution of terrestrial Hg to modern subduction zones remains poorly understood. Here we present new Hg–B–Sr–Nd isotopic data for volcanic rocks from eight stratovolcanoes and the Toba super-sized volcanic system, all located along the Sumatra segment of the Sunda arc. Sumatra volcanic rocks have negative Δ199Hg values (from −0.19 to −0.02‰), indicating an input of terrestrial Hg. Their mass-dependent fractionation (MDF; expressed as δ202Hg) ranges from −2.08 to −1.07‰, lower than that of the Mesozoic basement on Sumatra (−0.05‰). Together with Sr-Nd isotope constraints indicating minor crustal contamination, these observations rule out a crustal origin for the negative Δ199Hg anomalies and instead reflect a mantle source modified by recycled terrestrial Hg. The near-zero Δ199Hg values of the Nicobar Fan sediments (−0.01 to 0.03‰) indicate that the recycled terrestrial Hg in the mantle source is unlikely to originate from the Nicobar Fan but more likely reflects locally derived Sumatran terrigenous sediments. Three-endmember mixing models coupling Δ199Hg with Sr–Nd isotopes further indicate that the subducted sediment contribution was dominated by Nicobar Fan sediments but included a smaller proportion of Sumatra terrigenous component carrying the negative Hg-MIF signature, with total sediment additions of <5 wt% beneath the Sumatra stratovolcanoes and ∼5–10 wt% beneath the Toba volcanic system. Boron isotopes indicate slab-derived fluid additions of ∼0.01–1.0 wt% and ∼0.01–0.05 wt% beneath Sumatra stratovolcanoes and Toba volcanic systems, respectively. Mass-balance calculations show that fluids containing ∼20 ppb to 3.3 ppm Hg could reproduce the average Δ199Hg value of the Sumatra volcanic rocks, indicating that slab-derived dehydration fluids are potential carriers transferring terrestrial Hg into the mantle wedge. Near the slab tear zone, sediment melts generated during the diapiric ascent and partial melting of subducted sediments result in the enriched Sr-Nd isotopic compositions of the Toba volcanic rocks. Our results demonstrate that Hg isotopes, when integrated with Sr-Nd-B isotope systematics, serve as a sensitive tracer for distinguishing recycling of various components in subduction zones.

title: The effect of pressure and temperature on the fluid/melt partitioning of porphyry ore metals
description: Publication date: Available online 2 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Ivano Gennaro, Alexandra Tsay, Zoltán Zajacz
abstract: A major fraction of the total Cu, Mo, and Au mined worldwide is derived from porphyry ore deposits, with Ag representing an abundant by-product from the exploitation of these deposits. The relative endowment of these metals is linked to deposit depth, with Au-rich deposits forming in the shallowest levels of the crust while Mo-rich deposits form deeper. These deposits are fed by magmatic-hydrothermal fluids derived from magma chambers which likely sit 5–15 km below the surface, but attainment of fluid saturation at greater depths has also been proposed. These deposits display a general depth-dependent metal endowment. To determine the effect of pressure (P) and temperature (T) on the ability of the fluid phase to extract these metals from the melt, experiments were conducted in cold-seal pressure vessels and a piston cylinder apparatus covering a range of P (150–700 MPa) and T (760–950 °C) conditions at which fluid exsolution is most likely to occur in crustal magma reservoir systems. Experimental capsules were composed of a Au-Ag-Cu alloy as the source of metals and contained a synthetic rhyolite glass, fluid of 1 or 12 mol Cl/kg H2O, and natural quartz chip for the entrapment of synthetic fluid inclusions. Metal solubilities in the melt and fluid phases increase roughly linearly with increasing T; Cl concentration only affects the solubility of metals in the fluid phase. Fluid/melt partition coefficients of Cu, Ag, and Au decrease monotonically with increasing T and are generally unaffected by P at a fixed fluid salinity. Chlorine and Mo partitioning into the fluid increase by a factor of 4 with P increasing from 150 to 500 MPa at low fluid salinities but decrease slightly at high fluid salinities. Empirical functions were fit which describe the solubility, fluid/melt partitioning, and metal/Na exchange of Cl, Cu, Ag, Au, and Mo as functions of T and P. A simplified magma degassing model based on these equations reveals that ore metal extraction from magmas is the most effective at upper crustal emplacement depths and relatively high initial water concentrations.

title: Time-resolved Mo isotopes track source evolution from recycled slab components to a coherent OIB-type mantle source
description: Publication date: Available online 25 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Dongjing Xu, Xiu-Zheng Zhang, Yue Qi, Jie Li, Bing Chen, Pei-Na Guo, Tao Du, Qiang Wang
abstract: Subduction returns surface lithologies to the mantle and helps generate enriched domains sampled by ocean-island basalts (OIB). Many studies identify recycled components in OIB sources, but few resolve how these components mature into coherent, melt-fertile mantle domains. We examine this transition using Miocene and late Middle Pleistocene alkaline lavas that record temporally distinct sampling of a regional slab-modified asthenosphere above stagnant Tethyan slab material in southeastern Yunnan. New major- and trace-element, Sr–Nd–Pb and Mo isotope data for ca. 0.25–0.22 Ma Pingbian basanites are compared with published ca. 13–11 Ma Maguan basalts. The Pingbian lavas form a compact, silica-undersaturated, high-Nb suite. Relative to Maguan, Pingbian has narrower ranges of source-sensitive trace-element ratios and Sr–Nd–Pb isotope compositions and a clearer enriched mantle 1 (EM1)-like signature, characterized by low 206Pb/204Pb and 143Nd/144Nd and intermediate 87Sr/86Sr. These features define a more focused melt-producing domain, whereas δ 98/95Mo spans −0.41‰ to +0.04‰.
