Integrated δ 98/95Mo–Ce/Mo, trace-element and Sr–Nd–Pb relationships are consistent with similar recycled component classes in both suites but different effective weighting, with weaker expression of eclogitized oceanic crust and sediment-derived material and stronger expression of hydrated slab mantle in Pingbian. The resolved Mo isotope excursions indicate that component-scale heterogeneity persisted within this focused source. We define OIB-source maturation as source focusing and component reweighting within an inherited recycled slab inventory, rather than replacement by a new reservoir. More broadly, this paired record suggests that EM1-like OIB-type sources above stagnant slabs can develop through such reorganization, while Mo isotopes may retain component-level memory despite the narrowing of trace-element and Sr–Nd–Pb signatures.

title: Mercury isotopes in coral skeletons as proxies for marine Hg cycling: assessing fidelity and fractionation during biomineralization
description: Publication date: Available online 23 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Fei Cao, Yongquan Zhang, Ruoyu Sun, Larissa Schneider, Songjing Li, Rui Zhang, Pengfei Li, Wang Zheng, Jiubin Chen, Yi Liu
abstract: Stable mercury (Hg) isotopes provide powerful tools for tracing marine Hg sources and transformations. However, suitable geological archives that record long-term changes in seawater Hg isotopes remain scarce, limiting reconstructions of past marine Hg cycling. Here, we evaluate the potential of coral skeletons as archives of seawater Hg isotope compositions and assess the mechanisms controlling Hg incorporation during coral calcification. We systematically investigate the effectiveness and isotopic impacts of chemical cleaning protocols designed to isolate aragonite-bound Hg in coral skeletons. Sequential leaching and oxidative soaking experiments demonstrate that a substantial fraction of Hg in untreated coral skeletons is associated with non-aragonitic phases, primarily organic matter, and can be efficiently removed by optimized oxidative cleaning. These treatments result in large decreases in Hg concentrations and systematic changes in mass-dependent fractionation (MDF; δ202Hg), while mass-independent fractionation (MIF; Δ199Hg and Δ200Hg) signatures remain invariant. This indicates that cleaning selectively affects MDF without altering source-diagnostic MIF signals. Applying the optimized cleaning protocol, we analyze Hg concentrations and isotope compositions in coral skeletons collected from nearshore and offshore environments in the South China Sea. Coral skeletons preserve distinct regional differences in Hg MIF, which are consistent with published regional seawater values, reflecting contrasting contributions from atmospheric and terrestrial Hg sources. In contrast, δ202Hg values are consistently more negative than seawater by approximately 1 ‰, indicating systematic MDF during skeletal incorporation, likely driven by biologically mediated kinetic effects associated with calcification. Our results suggest that coral skeletons generally preserve seawater Hg MIF signatures while exhibiting predictable MDF during biomineralization. These findings establish coral skeletons as promising archives for reconstructing long-term changes in marine Hg cycling in response to natural variability and anthropogenic perturbations.

title: Hydrothermal experiments reveal methanol, ammonia, and methylamines as tracers of pH and temperature with potential application to Enceladus, Europa, and other icy ocean worlds
description: Publication date: Available online 13 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Kirtland J. Robinson, Everett L. Shock, Sean P. Sylva, Jeffrey S. Seewald
abstract: Icy ocean worlds in our solar system are prime targets in the search for extraterrestrial life. Enceladus and Europa are icy moons with evidence of global subsurface oceans in contact with rocky interiors, which may provide habitable environments for chemotrophic life. However, the interaction between water and rock and any changes in fluid chemistry are poorly constrained because the icy shells of these moons inhibit direct sampling of subsurface aqueous environments. Characterization of subseafloor processes may depend on chemical signatures in materials that are transported to accessible sampling locations near the surfaces of these icy ocean worlds. Here we present a theoretical framework where organic compounds likely to be present at icy ocean worlds can be utilized as tracers of geochemistry if they approach metastable equilibrium abundances, which we test with laboratory experiments. We use thermodynamic calculations of aqueous solutions to demonstrate that abundances of methanol, ammonia, and methylamines (compounds selected based on Enceladus’ plume data) should approach steady state ratios based on reversible substitution reactions that are systematically controlled by pH and temperature. We test these calculations by performing laboratory hydrothermal experiments ranging in temperature (175-325℃) and pH (∼3.5–7.0), demonstrating that chemical concentration measurements alone can be used in predictive models to accurately constrain the different conditions across experimental systems. As examples, with experiments conducted at 250℃, we demonstrate that the chemical tracers in a pH ∼ 3.5 solution predict a pH ≤ ∼5.0 and a temperature of ∼ 225-250℃, while the tracers in a solution at pH ∼ 7.0 predict a pH of ∼ 6.0–7.5 and a temperature of ∼ 200-275℃. Notably, all of our high-temperature experiments are cooled to room temperature prior to analysis, indicating that the hydrothermal signal (i.e., the ratio of chemical species) is preserved due to the slowing of reaction kinetics at lower temperatures, which may be analogous to hydrothermal fluids that vent into icy oceans. Similarly, we also performed a partial-cooling experiment that shows a tracer signal produced at 325℃ remains largely preserved for a year after the experiment was cooled to 175℃. We compare experimental results from gold reaction vessels to experiments previously conducted in glass vessels to assess the effects of experimental vessel type and find only minor differences in product distributions over time. Overall, our findings provide additional motivation to target small organic molecules for analysis on future missions to icy ocean worlds in order to constrain subsurface geochemical parameters critical to habitability

title: The importance of deep reactions between ascending komatiite and pre-existing protocratonic lithosphere for the chemistry of Archaean peridotites and greenstone belt volcanics: insights from reaction experiments
description: Publication date: Available online 9 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Rodrigo Freitas Rodrigues, Balz S. Kamber, Gregory M. Yaxley, Emma L. Tomlinson, Sandra Piazolo, Nathan R. Daczko
abstract: The cratonic lithospheric mantle is the buoyant 200–250 km deep root that enabled ancient continents (cratons) to survive for billions of years. The root stabilised due to extensive melting, erupting magnesian magmas at surface. However, peridotite xenolith samples from the cratonic mantle exhibit far more variable olivine/orthopyroxene and MgO/SiO2 ratios than expected from residues after melting of fertile mantle, exemplified by enigmatic dunites and orthopyroxene-rich harzburgites. Similarly, Archaean ultramafic lavas (komatiites) also show wider MgO/SiO2 variability than could be expected from shallow olivine fractionation. In addition, many komatiites have unexpectedly complex radiogenic isotope systematics, inconsistent with high-degree melting of refractory mantle. Thermodynamic modelling has suggested that these complexities could arise during deep (2–5 GPa) melt-solid reactions. Here, we present high-pressure layered experiments (3 GPa) involving the reaction between komatiite juxtaposed against harzburgite. The melt-bearing reactions yielded layered charges, wherein the initial komatiite layer (original, unreacted composition) was transformed into orthopyroxene-rich harzburgite following the reaction, and the original harzburgite layer resulted in the formation of dunite, with mineral modes and Mg-number depending on temperature. The solid residues of the reacted layers (orthopyroxene-rich and olivine-rich) are compositionally and mineralogically analogous to natural cratonic harzburgites and dunites, respectively. Thermodynamic modelling indicates that the MgO/SiO2 variability of the residues could be further increased by reacting the komatiite with fertile lherzolite instead of harzburgite. Solid-melt reactions markedly altered the composition of the incoming komatiite melt, with basaltic komatiite and komatiitic basalt formed at lower temperatures and modified high-Mg komatiites at higher temperatures. The melts exhibit the very wide range of MgO/SiO2 seen in ultramafic lavas in Archaean greenstone belts. Consideration of rare earth element and Hf partitioning suggests that assimilation of protocratonic ancient harzburgite into invading komatiite will be much more strongly seen in radiogenic Hf than Nd (or Ce) isotope ratios. Although both the original solid (harzburgite) and the incoming melt (komatiite) are ultramafic, their chemical contrast is sufficient to drive metasomatic reaction, likely partly due to the presence of a percolating melt. The reactions require higher temperatures than attained in the post-Archaean mantle, explaining both the sharp demise of komatiites after 2.5 Ga and the highly refractory nature of Archaean harzburgites and dunites. Ancient proto-cratonic mantle is one plausible candidate harbouring radiogenic signatures of Hadean silicate differentiation. The reason why these signatures are most commonly found in Archaean mafic and ultramafic igneous rocks may relate to the secular drop in maximum plume temperature, which has compromised the capacity of younger melts to sample this reservoir via assimilation

title: Context-dependent effects of microplastics on soil available phosphorus: An AP-centered multilevel meta-analysis
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Jianlong Li, Yuhan Zhang, Junyang Sun, Xiaoling Shan, Ling Ding, Xinran Qiu, Bin Zhang, Xian Li, Xujun Liang, Xuetao Guo
abstract: Microplastics are increasingly recognized as modifiers of soil nutrient availability, but their effects on soil available phosphorus (AP) remain difficult to generalize across soil–plastic contexts. Building on broader P syntheses, this AP-centered multilevel meta-analysis addressed within-study dependence, missing variance information, and AP-specific heterogeneity. The full dataset contained 597 paired observations from 79 studies, with 546 complete-SD effect sizes from 75 studies used for primary inference. Microplastic exposure was associated with an average 11.8% decrease in soil AP (lnRR = −0.126, 95% CI: −0.199 to −0.053), and this negative mean effect remained stable across complementary robustness analyses. However, the wide prediction interval showed that AP depletion was not universal. Reported background pH, particle size, and polymer identity were the clearest heterogeneity axes. Depletion was strongest in acidic soils and under exposure to particles ≤ 100 μm, while polymer identity significantly structured AP responses and the binary biodegradability classification did not. Exposure-duration class and soil sampling location showed limited explanatory power. The evidence base was concentrated in Asia, especially China, and AP extraction methods were poorly reported. Overall, microplastics shifted average AP toward depletion, but this response is best interpreted as context dependent rather than universal.

title: Amphipods ( Hyalella azteca ) and zooplankton as sentinels of rare earth elements, uranium and thorium in a northern mining region contaminated with arsenic
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Justine Labelle, Dominic E. Ponton, Holly Marginson, Claude Fortin, Maikel Rosabal, Marc Amyot
abstract: Growing demand for green energy and new technologies is driving rare earth elements (REEs) mining, with implications on the bioavailability and accumulation of REEs and co-occurring radionuclides (U, Th) in aquatic organisms. We evaluated the amphipod Hyalella azteca and zooplankton as potential biomonitors for REEs, U, Th, and arsenic by sampling ten lakes in the historically arsenic-contaminated region of Yellowknife (NWT), near the Nechalacho REE mine. Lanthanum (La) concentrations were among the lowest reported in Canadian fresh waters (0.01–0.07 nmol L⁻¹). In zooplankton, La bioaccumulation was negatively influenced by protein-like dissolved organic matter and phosphate, U free ion concentrations best predicted U accumulation, and dissolved organic carbon was found to reduce Th accumulation. In H. azteca, littoral sediment La, U, and Th concentrations strongly predicted bioaccumulation, and aqueous carbonate complexation likely reduced U accumulation. Arsenate (As(V)) in surface water was an important predictor of La, U, and Th amphipod bioaccumulation. Even after EDTA washing, Fe strongly predicted La accumulation, suggesting an association beyond their surface adsorption. Key processes controlling the bioaccumulation pathways of La, U, Th, and As in this arsenic-contaminated region were summarized in a conceptual model, providing a risk assessment framework for REE mining in northern Canada.

title: Crystal facet engineering of Mn 3 O 4 supported Ru catalysts for boosted photothermal propane oxidation: Synergy between metallic Ru 0 and oxygen vacancies
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Erhao Gao, Jiaqian Xue, Liang Zhou, Nan Xu, Jing Li, Jiali Zhu, Wei Wang, Shuiliang Yao, Zuliang Wu
abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) abatement remains a significant challenge, particularly for the deep oxidation of inert short-chain alkanes like propane. Herein, we report a facet-engineered Ru/Mn3O4 catalyst where the exposure of Mn3O4 {010} facets triggers a remarkable activity inversion compared to {110} facets upon light irradiation. Comprehensive analyses reveal a distinct facet-dependent metal-support interaction. On the {010} facet, pronounced interfacial charge transfer stabilizes a high proportion of metallic Ru0 and reduces the oxygen vacancy formation energy to 1.84 eV. The resulting electronically coupled Ru/Mn3O4{010} interface thus combines electron-rich Ru0 domains with a high density of oxygen vacancies; their synergy facilitates the cleavage of C–H bonds and accelerates the conversion from carboxylate intermediates to CO2 by generating reactive ·O2 – species. Consequently, the Ru/Mn3O4-D catalyst achieves a 90% propane conversion at 169 °C under full-spectrum irradiation, corresponding to a significantly lowered activation energy of 17.4 kJ/mol. Conversely, the {110} facet tends to anchor oxidized Ru species, leading to severe intermediate accumulation and inferior performance. This work not only elucidates the microscopic origin of facet-dependent influence in photothermal catalysis but also provides a feasible strategy for designing catalysts with optimized interfacial electronic structures.

title: Phthalate and non-phthalate plasticizers co-occur in soils and reshape microbial carbon metabolism
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Meng Gao, Yu Wang, Yiting Ge, Qi Su, Siyuan Li, Yingying Wen, Zixiao Zhao, Mohan Ma, Hongkai Zhu, Hongwen Sun
abstract: Phthalate esters (PAEs) are widely used plasticizers with well-documented ecological effects. The increasing use of non-phthalate plasticizers (NPAEs) as alternatives to PAEs has resulted in their co-occurrence in the environment, yet their co-contamination and microbial impacts in soils influenced by plastic production remain poorly understood. Here, a field survey around a plastic industrial area revealed that concentrations of PAEs (306–10,718 ng g−1) and NPAEs (20.3–380 ng g−1) in factory soils were an order of magnitude higher than those in nearby farmlands and villages. Di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP, 17.6–9280 ng g−1) and acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC, 1.19–233 ng g−1) were the dominant PAE and NPAE compounds, respectively. A 28-day microcosm experiment examined their combined effects on soil bacterial communities and functions. DEHP contamination individually enriched aromatic degradation pathways (i.e., benzoate/styrene degradation), whereas DEHP-ATBC co-contamination inhibited the aromatic degradation pathway, potentially associated with altered microbial carbon-utilization preferences, with Sphingomonas as a key functional taxon. Co-contamination also suppressed core carbon metabolism (i.e., citrate cycle), and enriched the ribosome pathway, indicating a shift toward fast‑growing, metabolically streamlined taxa. These findings provide the first evidence that PAE-NPAE co-contamination reshapes microbial carbon metabolism and impairs aromatic compound degradation, underscoring the need for mixture-based risk assessment for plasticizers.

title: Molecular mechanisms underlying the modulation of Co(II)-catalase interactions by polystyrene nanoplastics
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Wendi Bi, Xiaoyang Wang, Shuqi Guo, Xiangxiang Li, Yuntao Qi, Jinhu Wang, Rutao Liu
abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) can interact with heavy metals and alter metal-protein interactions. However, their effects on Co(II)-catalase (CAT) interactions remain unclear. We integrated enzyme activity assays, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), multispectroscopic analyses, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to compare Co(II) alone with the PS-NPs–Co(II) system. Co(II) increased background-corrected apparent CAT activity at 0.5–0.8 mM, whereas PS-NPs generally attenuated this increase, significantly at 0.6 and 0.8 mM (p = 0.024 and 0.009). ITC yielded distinct apparent responses for Co(II) into CAT titration (fitted ΔH = −335 kJ mol–1) and titration of the filtrate from a directly prepared PS-NPs–Co(II) mixture into CAT (−14.9 kJ mol–1). These values reflect different titrants in 20 mM HEPES and do not isolate a single binding event. Spectroscopy showed changes in CAT secondary structure, aromatic-residue environments, and heme Soret responses, with a distinct heme response in the combined system. Simulations indicated fewer direct CAT-Co(II) contacts and greater heme-pocket solvent exposure in the PS-containing model. These findings suggest that PS-NPs may modify the local CAT-Co(II) environment and contribute to the observed activity differences under these cell-free conditions.

title: Flow-through filter divided electrolytic cell enables highly efficient water purification via spatiotemporal alteration in electrocatalytic ozonation processes
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Runze Liu, Xingyu Fan, Mengying Yan, Hongbin Xu, Long Huang, Yingke Fang, Yuan Li, Huiying Yang, Guoqiang Li
abstract: Emerging contaminants with contrasting electronic structures respond differently to molecular ozone (O3) and hydroxyl radicals (•OH), yet conventional electro-peroxone systems mainly exploit cathodic O3 activation while leaving the acidic anodic chamber underutilized. Here, a hydrophilic carbon-fiber-membrane-divided, single-pass flow-through GF/EP reactor was developed to convert the anodic chamber into an active O3-preserving oxidation zone and regulate oxidant exposure by reversing the influent direction. In the cathode-to-anode (C-A) configuration, upstream H2O2/HO2 --mediated O3 activation increased the apparent •OH exposure to 0.59 × 10−10 M s, achieving 96.0% ibuprofen (electron-deficient contaminant) removal with a kobs of 0.101 min−1, compared with 82.3% and 0.076 min−1 in A-C. Conversely, the upstream acidic anodic region in A-C preserved molecular O3 and promoted selective electrophilic oxidation of electron-rich contaminants, yielding 99% benzotriazole removal with a kobs of 0.103 min−1. Product identification and DFT calculations revealed configuration-dependent pathways and toxicity evolution. Matching influent direction with contaminant reactivity reduced the specific energy consumption for ibuprofen mineralization to 0.16 kWh g−1. The system also maintained over 80% ibuprofen removal and achieved 47% COD removal in secondary effluent. These results establish flow-direction-regulated oxidant sequencing as a simple and energy-efficient strategy for treating chemically diverse contaminants.

title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal inoculation as a potential approach for enhancing pollutant removal from tailwater in Acorus calamus constructed wetlands
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zhi-Hao Song, Xiang-Long He, Qi-Hang Zhang, Jing-Wen Li, Liang-Cheng Lin, Yi-Hao Li, Jun-Feng Wang
abstract: The residual organic matter, nitrogen, phosphorus, and heavy metals (HMs) in the effluent from wastewater treatment plants pose persistent risks to the ecological environment. To enhance advanced treatment of synthetic tailwater, this study used CWs based on the symbiosis of Acorus calamus and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and investigated its pollutant removal efficiency and underlying mechanisms. The results showed that AMF inoculation significantly increased the removal rates of organic matter and total nitrogen by 11.35% and 16.62%, respectively, while TP removal showed a non-significant increasing trend (7.65%), respectively; reduced N₂O flux and peak emissions by 39.34% and 21.96%. Compared with the control group, AMF symbiotic treatment showed more positive changes: AMF–plant symbiosis significantly increased plant biomass and significantly enhanced plant HM content and accumulation (Cr, Ni, Pb, and Zn). Meanwhile, changes in microbial diversity and the relative abundance of microbial communities related to nitrogen and phosphorus cycling indirectly enhanced the removal of organic matter, nitrogen, and phosphorus in CWs. In addition, changes in the abundance of functional genes related to carbon metabolism and nitrogen transformation/reduction were consistent with organic matter and nitrogen removal and reduced N₂O/TN emissions. In summary, this study proposes that the AMF-plant symbiosis may coordinately enhance the advanced treatment performance of CWs for synthetic tailwater through plant-microbial community-functional gene interactions, thereby providing new insights for the application of plant–microbe symbiotic technology in advanced tailwater treatment.

title: Reactive diffusion of selenium anions into clay-rocks: A sorption in batch and through-diffusion investigation
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Sébastien Savoye, Serge Lefevre, Emilie Thory, Benoît Madé, Romain V.H. Dagnelie
abstract: Selenium-79 is a critical radionuclide in the safety assessment of high-level radioactive waste in deep geological repositories in clay-rich formations, due to its long half-life and speciation. It exhibits three relevant oxidation states in anionic forms: selenate(+VI), selenite(+IV), and selenide(−II) whose mobility through clay-rocks needs to be evaluated. To this end, batch and diffusion experiments were performed in the French Callovo-oxfordian clay-rocks under anoxic conditions and at ultra-trace concentrations, using the 75Se isotope. Our findings reveal that selenate is weakly retained and diffuses similarly to the inert anionic tracer 36Cl−. In contrast, selenite exhibits strong retention in diffusion experiments conducted with and without the addition of hydrazine. The steep 75Se rock profile and the 75Se(+IV) activity evolution in solution were modeled using high distribution ratio values (1000 −3300 L kg−1). The oxidation of selenide, HSe− species, into the precipitate Se(0)(s) was strongly delayed by its polymerization into polyselenides (Sen 2−), with no 75Se(0)(s) observed after 100 days of diffusion. Adding hydrazine to one of the diffusion cells slowed the polymerization rate of selenide, thus allowing more selenide to diffuse into the solid. Based on a simplified model, we proposed that the selenide diffusion would be similar to that of selenate and 36Cl−.

title: Geochemical controls on the fate and mobility of coal combustion product-derived elements in a dolomitic aquifer
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Shifat J. Monami, Ann S. Ojeda, Ming-Kuo Lee
abstract: Coal combustion products (CCPs) can release elements of concern into groundwater, posing risks to drinking water and ecosystems, yet their behavior in carbonate aquifers remains poorly understood. This study investigated the fate and mobility of seven elements (As, B, Cd, Cu, Cr, Mo, Ni) at a CCP disposal site overlying a dolomitic aquifer in the southeastern United States. CCP-impacted wells showed Ca-Mg-SO4 type waters with elevated sulfate concentrations (460–635 mg/L) compared to background Ca-Mg-HCO3 waters. Boron (0.13–4.5 mg/L) and Mo (0.10–2.9 mg/L) were the most mobile elements and exceeded groundwater protection standards. Sequential extraction showed that ∼76% of leachable Mo was associated with water-soluble and amorphous oxide fractions, indicating weak sorption. In contrast As, Cd, Cr, Cu, and Ni were predominantly associated with aquifer solids and occurred as low dissolved concentrations. Geochemical speciation models predicted HAsO4 2-, B(OH)3, and MoO4 2- as the dominant aqueous species under the site’s alkaline and oxidizing conditions. However, SEM-EDS identified As-Ca-Mg-O associations and sequential extraction showed that ∼95% of the leachable As was associated with carbonate-dominated fractions, indicating that As attenuation occurs through adsorption and/or structural incorporation onto carbonate minerals, rather than Fe-oxide attenuation pathways. Chromium was predominantly associated with resistant residual fractions, consistent with precipitation/co-precipitation of Cr(III) oxide or spinel phases. Cadmium, Cu, and Ni showed no plume enrichment and were interpreted as predominantly geogenic. Overall, the empirical and modeling results suggest B and Mo are the major CCP-derived hazards in this carbonate aquifer, whereas As is likely immobilized by carbonate adsorption and/or structural incorporation.

title: 137 Cs and natural radionuclides in Antarctic soil-vegetation systems on King George Island: Contrasting patterns in penguin-influenced and reference habitats
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Michał Saniewski, Katarzyna Fudala, Robert Bialik, Piotr Paneth, Dominika Saniewska
abstract: Fallout radionuclides are useful tracers of contaminant retention and redistribution in polar soil-vegetation systems. This study examined activities of 137Cs, 40K, total 210Pb, 226Ra, and 228Ac, together with δ15N and δ13C, in soil, penguin guano, lichens, mosses, and vascular plants collected during four campaigns over two austral spring-summer periods on King George Island. Relatively high 137Cs activities were observed in soil and Deschampsia antarctica in the penguin-influenced area, whereas Usnea antarctica showed low 137Cs activity in both areas. Fresh penguin guano contained low 137Cs activity (∼1 Bq kg−1 d.w.) and was not a direct high-activity source at sampling. D. antarctica showed consistently higher 137Cs activity in the penguin-influenced area than at the reference site across matched campaigns, together with a higher median soil-to-vegetation transfer factor, providing the clearest site-related 137Cs contrast among the analysed vegetation groups. U. antarctica showed the highest total 210Pb activity, while 7Be was detected in three lichen samples, a pattern compatible with atmospheric particle interception. Lower δ15N in U. antarctica was consistent with weaker ornithogenic nitrogen influence. Together, the contrasting radionuclide profiles indicated a stronger substrate-associated 137Cs signal in D. antarctica, whereas the U. antarctica profile was more compatible with atmospheric particle interception.

title: Empowered electron transfer behavior mediated by iron/sulfur cycling drives synergistic transformation of nitrogen and PFOA in constructed wetlands: Overlooked abiotic and biotic mechanisms
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xiuwen Qian, Juan Huang, Jin Xu, Yiren Gao, Shiyu Shan, Zhishui Liang, Yuanyan Zhang
abstract: In this study, enhanced dynamic ammonium, nitrate (NO3 --N), and total nitrogen (TN) removal reaching 85.87–99.35%, 61.31–99.45%, and 74.61–98.48% were observed in biochar-pyrite (BCP) amended constructed wetland. Among them NO3 --N and TN were significantly higher than both control and individual biochar (BC) group. Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) removal efficiency was 74.05–92.58% by BCP amendment, with higher defluorination rate and lower short-chain products accumulation. Increased activity of nitrate/nitrite reductase caused improved denitrification process in BCP system, which could result from enrichment of autotrophic denitrifying bacteria (like Pseudomonas, Thiobacillus, and Gallionella) and promotion of most genes involved in nitrogen/iron/sulfur metabolism. Facilitated redox cycles of iron/sulfur increased electron transfer system activity by 14.03–261.60% and 9.06–93.53% compared to control and single BC system, with higher activity of enzymes related to electron transport chain and encoding genes. Meanwhile, 1.72–3.79 folds enrichment of electroactive bacteria in BCP layer increased extracellular electron transfer (EET) efficiency. In mechanism, both reactive oxygen species mediated degradation and accelerated EET might enhance PFOA mineralization. This work offered a promising technique for synergic removal of nitrogen and PFOA in secondary effluent of WWTPs, which supplied novel insights on abiotic/biotic PFOA degradation mechanisms mediated by iron/sulfur cycling.

title: Interpretable QSPR modeling of PFAS endpoints via transformer-driven SMILES-to-molecular descriptor learning
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): ChanHyeok Jeong, SangYoun Kim, TaeYong Woo, NaYeong Jeon, SeonJu Kim, ChangKyoo Yoo, SungKu Heo
abstract: A data-centric and interpretable Quantitative structure–property relationship (QSPR) framework was developed for four Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) endpoints (i.e., LC50, log BCF, log KOA, and log KOW) with molecular- and descriptor-level interpretation of prediction behavior. First, PFAS endpoint datasets were collected while molecular descriptors and tokenized SMILES sequences were integrated for descriptor imputation. Descriptor redundancy was then reduced through statistical feature selection, and MissTransformer reconstructed missing descriptor values from latent structural information encoded in SMILES. Finally, explainable AI (XAI) analysis was applied to interpret chemical descriptor contributions to PFAS endpoint prediction. As a result, MissTransformer increased the number of descriptor-complete compounds available for QSPR modeling by 133.71% for log BCF data. Among the endpoint prediction models, the data-centric XGB model showed the best performance for log KOW prediction, with R2 and Q2 LMO values of 0.976 and 0.775, respectively. Interpretation results showed that hydrophobicity-related descriptors and fluorine atoms strongly contributed to log KOW prediction, whereas global structural descriptors related to molecular size and steric effects were important for log BCF prediction. The proposed framework can be used to prioritize data-poor PFAS compounds for further testing, monitoring, and risk-based environmental management.

title: Concentration-dependent impacts of ofloxacin on the mobilization-immobilization dynamics of geogenic arsenic in groundwater environment
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Qianyong Liang, Junna Ning, Kunfu Pi, Xianjun Xie, Philippe Van Cappellen, Yue’e Peng, Yanxin Wang
abstract: Arsenic (As) behaviors in aquifers can be altered by exogenetic antibiotics and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), which modifies evolution of originally geogenic As-contaminated groundwater while increasing environmental risk of ARGs. The roles of introduced antibiotics in As biogeochemical cycle in groundwater environments however remain elusive mechanistically. Using Shewanella oneidensis (S. oneidensis) as a model, this research elucidates the impacts of varying levels of antibiotic (e.g., ofloxacin) exposure on As fate during microbially-mediated reductive dissolution of host goethite. Under low-level ofloxacin exposure (≤1 μg/L), S. oneidensis restored secretion of riboflavin after a short period of stress adaptation. Conversely, high ofloxacin exposure (≥10 μg/L) consistently depleted aqueous riboflavin and weakened mineral-biomolecule interactions, restricting electron transfer and inhibiting goethite bioreduction. Contrasting changes in the abundances of ARGs (e.g., qnrA) and As efflux gene (e.g., arsB) indicate concentration-dependent reorganization of resistance-associated genetic potential under ofloxacin and As co-exposure, while aqueous As(III) accumulated despite declining arsB abundance. Therefore, the molecular mechanism underlying As migration differs depending upon antibiotic exposure levels. These findings provide novel insights into underestimated effects of concomitant antibiotics on As re-mobilization in geogenic contaminated groundwater.

title: Spatial prediction of the soil−wheat cadmium bioconcentration factor with a knowledge-guided learning model
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Siqi Liu, Yanling Li, Yang Yang, Huading Shi, Yao Zhang, Pu Dong, Meie Wang, Weiping Chen
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) readily transfers from contaminated soils into wheat grain, posing dietary risks; however, predicting the spatial distribution of the bioconcentration factor (BCF) remains challenging due to interacting direct and indirect pathways. We developed a knowledge-guided learning model using structural equation modeling to quantify relationships governing BCF. These mechanistic insights guided Random Forest coupled with high-accuracy surface modeling for spatial prediction and informed management strategy evaluation through scenario simulations. The results showed that the BCF was jointly governed by direct soil buffering and Zn–Cd competitive uptake, and indirectly by industrial emissions and wind that degraded soil properties and increased soil Zn concentrations. Validated against a large field dataset from northern China, the model achieved R2 of 0.44–0.84. Spatial predictions revealed a partial mismatch between soil Cd and BCF hotspots, with high-BCF zones occurring where neutral pH, moderate organic matter, and industrial emission-related deposition converged. Scenario simulations suggested that a combined strategy of source control and zinc fertilization could reduce the high-BCF area from 22.7% to 3.9% by 2050. We proposed a spatially differentiated zoning framework for targeted wheat production management. This knowledge-guided learning model provides a transferable methodology for precise control in heavy metal-contaminated agricultural regions.

title: Arsenic induces hepatic lipid accumulation associated with DNA methylation alterations and oxidative stress in marine medaka ( Oryzias melastigma )
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Ting Zhang, Yang Liu, Sen Du, Li Zhang
abstract: Arsenic (As) contamination is a global environmental concern, but its toxicity and mechanisms on marine organisms remain largely unknown. In this study, marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma) were exposed to dietary arsenate (AsV) at 0, 100, and 1000 μg/g for 28 days, and primary hepatocyte cultures were established to investigate the underlying mechanisms. The results showed that AsV induced significant and dose‑dependent lipid accumulation both in vivo and in vitro, following the internal arsenic burden. The transcription of lipogenic genes was upregulated, and the transcription of lipolytic genes was downregulated after AsV exposure. AsV reduced the level of SAM, suppressed transcription of dnmt1 and tet3, and induced hypomethylation of the ppargc1b promoter. Correspondingly, AsV upregulated the transcription of ppargc1b, which might modulate downstream genes of the PPAR signaling pathway and impaired lipid metabolism. In addition, the redox cycle of arsenic triggered oxidative stress and endoplasmic reticulum stress. The ROS scavengers GSH and NAC significantly alleviated arsenic‑induced lipid accumulation and aberrant gene expression, whereas the ER stress PBA inhibitor showed no protective effect. Our results demonstrated that AsV induced lipid accumulation associated with DNA methylation alterations and oxidative stress, providing insights into arsenic lipotoxicity and ecological risk assessment in marine environments.

title: Biocomposite based on alginate hydrosphere immobilized with Pseudomonas psychrotolerans for highly selective recovery of Ce-group rare earth elements from mine wastewater
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Chenxin Zhang, Tingting Wei, Qiang Wang, Honghai Yan, Zhibiao Chen, Zuliang Chen
abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) recovery from secondary resources urgently requires green and highly selective biosorbents to address supply shortages and mining pollution. Herein, a novel biocomposite PP/ALG was constructed by immobilizing the indigenous bacterium Pseudomonas psychrotolerans within alginate hydrospheres, enabling a specific adsorption preference for Ce-group REEs in mine wastewater, with adsorption efficiencies up to 90.37% and distribution coefficients (Kd) up to 9312.5 mL·g−1, outperforming many other adsorbents. As well, the separation factor (SF) of Ce-group REEs for Tb and Yb groups were significantly higher than that between other groups, drastically exceeding 27. The REEs selectivity originates from three synergistic effects: (1) the larger ionic radius and lower charge density of Ce-group REEs favor stronger coordination with surface functional groups, (2) microbial extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) are crucial in facilitating the adsorption process, and (3) metabolic-derived C-N and carboxyl/phosphate groups provide highly specific chelating sites for Ce-group. Overall, this work establishes a green, sustainable, and highly selective biorecovery strategy for REEs from hazardous mine wastewater, highlighting the critical role of indigenous bacteria and EPS in REEs separation.

title: Divergent evolution of trace elements in groundwater-dependent lakes: Insights from multi-isotopic tracers, DOM molecular characteristics, and microbial evidence
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xu Yang, Siyu Liu, Shen Qu, Xiangwei Li, Heyang Sun, Zhongli Wang, Limin Duan, Xiaomin Liu, Ruihong Yu
abstract: Groundwater-dependent lakes are highly vulnerable to trace element (TE) accumulation, yet the mechanisms controlling TE occurrence in coupled lake–groundwater systems remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the occurrence, transport, and controlling mechanisms of TEs in a representative groundwater-dependent lake system. Concentrations are reported as mean ± standard deviation (SD; LW, n = 6; GW, n = 44). Lake water (LW) and groundwater (GW) exhibited distinct TE occurrence patterns, with significantly higher concentrations of V (89.50 ± 69.00 μg L⁻¹), Mo (32.40 ± 24.30 μg L⁻¹), and U (25.60 ± 20.60 μg L⁻¹) in LW, whereas Sc (3.78 ± 0.93 μg L⁻¹), Zn (11.95 ± 38.54 μg L⁻¹), and Ba (193.04 ± 94.58 μg L⁻¹) were significantly higher in GW (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05). Hydrochemical and isotopic evidence (δ¹¹B and ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr) suggested that water–rock interactions and mineral dissolution contributed to lithogenic TE enrichment in GW, whereas alkaline and saline conditions (TDS = 7798 mg L⁻¹; pH = 9.4) were associated with elevated TE concentrations in LW. Furthermore, lignin-rich dissolved organic matter (DOM) and fungal communities were closely associated with lithogenic TE patterns in GW, whereas the more compositionally diverse DOM pool and bacterial communities showed distinct associations with TEs in LW, suggesting contrasting biogeochemical linkages between the two water bodies. The radon-222 (222Rn) mass balance model estimated a mean lacustrine groundwater discharge rate of 22.2 mm d⁻¹ , demonstrating substantial groundwater inputs to the lakes and highlighting groundwater as an important hydrological pathway for the transport of dissolved TEs. These findings provide a mechanistic understanding of TE evolution in groundwater-dependent lakes and improve predictions of TE accumulation and ecological risks under arid conditions.

title: Heavy metal content of plastic waste in agricultural ditches: Distinction and relation between exogenously adsorbed and endogenously added
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Pengling You, Xiaofeng Wen, Yingxing Liu, Yi Hong, Qiao Liu, Zhilin Zhou, Chuneng Gan, Yuannan Long, Changbo Jiang, Lingshi Yin
abstract: Plastic waste in agricultural environments can act as a sink and a source of heavy metal contaminants. However, the relationship between plastic waste and heavy metals under actual environment conditions remains poorly understood. In this study, sediments and plastic waste were collected from two agricultural ditches in the Dongting Lake basin, China. Pb, Cd, Cr, Cu, and Zn concentrations were determined in ditch sediments, and surface-associated and intrinsic metal concentrations in plastic waste were investigated. Zn exhibited the highest concentration in exogenous plastic waste (231.76 ± 75.94 mg/kg), endogenous plastic waste (119.31 ± 56.04 mg/kg), and sediments (96.71 ± 25.25 mg/kg). This finding reflects the combined influence of environmental accumulation and metal additives within plastics. Overall, endogenous Pb, Cr, and Cu concentrations were 5.0, 13.9, and 4.8 times higher, respectively, than exogenous concentrations, suggesting that the potential release of these additive-derived metals warrants future monitoring and assessment. PE showed relatively higher endogenous metal concentrations. Correlation analysis indicated that the relationships between exogenous and endogenous metals varied across environmental conditions and polymer type, indicating that these factors affected the exogenous adsorption and endogenous release of heavy metals in plastics. This study provides field-based evidence from actual agricultural ditches and highlights the need for greater attention to interactions between plastic waste and heavy metals. It thus offers empirical support for managing combined plastic-heavy metal pollution in agricultural environments.

title: HumanToxPredict: An interpretable data-driven framework for human oral TDLo prediction and toxicity assessment of pharmaceuticals and bioactive compounds
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Shubha Das, Probir Kumar Ojha
abstract: Predicting the human toxic dose low (TDLo) is critically important for pharmaceutical safety assessment and regulatory toxicology. A global computational toxicology framework that integrates toxicity data for children, infants, men, and women was developed using indicator-variable-based demographic encoding. Initially, Partial Least Squares (PLS)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) and quantitative read-across structure-activity relationship (q-RASAR) models were developed using interpretable molecular descriptors and similarity-based descriptors. A structure-level group-wise partitioning strategy was adopted. The q-RASAR model demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with the corresponding QSAR model. Additionally, Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models were explored to investigate non-linear relationships. To further improve practical applicability, classification models were also developed, with RF showing the strongest overall performance among the evaluated models based on multi-metric analysis. Model interpretation suggests that pTDLo values are influenced by substituted nitrogen environments, topological arrangements, and similarity-driven toxicological information. The final model was further applied to 3660 investigational drugs, with most compounds falling within the applicability domain. We also developed a user-friendly software tool, HumanToxPredict, to enable rapid toxicity prediction. Overall, the present study introduces an interpretable, population-integrated human toxicity prediction framework that integrates q-RASAR, machine learning, and large-scale chemical screening.

title: Mechanism of in-situ calcium sulfate in the synergistic sulfidation–carbothermal reduction for efficient recovery of Cu, Pb, and Zn from copper smelting flue coated materials
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Kai Fan, Haipei Zhang, Bo Li, Shichao Wu, Yonggang Wei, Hua Wang
abstract: Flue coated materials from copper smelting are hazardous wastes rich in Cu, Pb, and Zn, containing intrinsic CaSO4. Unlike processes relying mainly on externally added sulfur sources, this study evaluates whether intrinsic CaSO4 can serve as an in-situ sulfur donor and slag-forming flux during sulfidation-carbothermal reduction. Thermodynamic calculations, in-situ XRD, and TG-MS were combined to investigate phase evolution and metal partitioning. CaSO4 remained stable below about 900 ℃, was reduced to CaS mainly at 900–1050 °C, and participated in CaO formation and SO2 release above about 1050 °C. Significant CO, CO2, SO2 release occurred above 1000 ℃, defining a reaction-active window of 1050–1200 °C. The CaSO4/C ratio strongly influenced oxygen-sulfur potential. insufficient carbon left CaSO4 undecomposed, an appropriate ratio favored Cu2S and FeS, and excess carbon promoted metallic alloying. The overall mechanism is supplying sulfur at low T, making slag at high T, and regulating oxygen-sulfur potential in the middle stage, which enables selective separation and recycling of Cu from Pb and Zn into matte and volatile phases, with efficiencies of 95.1 ± 0.9%, 92.2 ± 1.1%, and 90.1 ± 1.3%. The volatile Pb/Zn species and SO2 generated require downstream capture and off-gas treatment, but the capture efficiency was not evaluated in this study.

title: Pesticide leaching in sandy and loamy soil—contrasting impact of polyethylene microplastic pollution and freeze–thaw events
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Siqi Wu, Alexander Böhme, Andreas Schäffer, Zhongli Chen, Annika Jahnke
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) can alter pesticide migration in soils by modifying soil structure and influencing pesticide sorption and transport. Freeze–thaw cycles (FTCs), which are common in temperate regions, naturally change soil structure and may influence the environmental fate of both MPs and pesticides. We investigated a mixture of 20 pesticides with a broad range of physical-chemical properties in a factorial column experiment combining sandy and loamy soils, room-temperature and FTC treatments, and the presence or absence of 1% (w/w) polyethylene (PE) particles (63–100 μm). Transport was characterized by the pore volumes required to reach 5% and 50% of the nominal influent concentration (BV5 and BV50). FTCs reduced mean breakthrough volumes by approximately 15–35% in sandy soil and 40–85% in loamy soil, whereas PE addition generally increased breakthrough volumes by approximately 7–17% across treatments. Loamy soil showed greater pesticide retention at room temperature and a 1–2.5-fold stronger response to FTCs than sandy soil. Associations with organic-carbon partition coefficients (K OC) and water solubility (S w) indicated compound-dependent transport. Changes in soil physical properties and complementary experiments with selected triazines suggested possible physical and partitioning-related contributions, particularly in loamy soil, consistent with FTC-induced changes in soil structure and flow pathways.

title: Environmental effects of biodegradable microplastics in cadmium-contaminated soil and their regulation on cadmium bioavailability
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xu Qin, Qingqing Huang, Lijie Zhao, Yuebing Sun
abstract: Biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) residues in soil are becoming increasingly prevalent; however, their effects on cadmium (Cd) bioavailability and toxicity in contaminated soils remain poorly understood. A pot experiment was conducted to investigate the effects of four typical BMPs—polylactic acid (PLA), poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), polybutylene succinate (PBS), and polycaprolactone (PCL) on soil physicochemical properties, Cd speciation, pak choi growth, antioxidant responses, and rhizobacterial community structure in Cd-contaminated acidic soil. Results demonstrated that BMPs regulated Cd behavior through dual abiotic (pH, zeta potential, electrical conductivity) and biotic (microbial community restructuring) pathways, with effects highly dependent on BMPs type. PBAT elevated soil pH, increased negative zeta potential, reduced shoot Cd accumulation, alleviated oxidative stress, and enhanced bacterial diversity with enrichment of Cd-immobilising taxa. Conversely, PLA, PBS, and PCL decreased soil pH, increased Cd availability and plant Cd uptake, aggravated lipid peroxidation and leaf tissue damage, and inhibited antioxidant enzyme activity. PLA broadly suppressed soil enzyme activity, whereas PCL reduced bacterial richness and enriched Cd-mobilising taxa. These findings demonstrate that BMPs exert species-specific regulation on Cd fate through combined modifications of soil physicochemical properties and reshaping of functional microbial communities, highlighting the need for risk differentiation when introducing biodegradable plastics into metal-contaminated farmlands.

title: Oxidant-free aqueous arsenic removal over few-layer Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene via coupled As(III) photooxidation and As(V) adsorption
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Shuhe Chen, Weijian Yu, Tao Liu, Yi Liu, Zuotao Liu, Siyuan Yang, Xin Cai, Qiongzhi Gao, Qingyou Liu, Zhigang Chen, Shengsen Zhang
abstract: Coupling arsenite oxidation with arsenate capture may reduce the need for separately dosed oxidants in water treatment, but the roles of the active phase and adsorption sites require careful evaluation. Here, Ti3C2Tx-based nanosheets were prepared by NH4F-assisted electrochemical etching and tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH)-mediated delamination without directly adding HF. The material exhibited a BET surface area of 80.37 m2/g and expanded basal spacing. Batch experiments under simulated solar irradiation showed light-dependent arsenic transformation and As(V) uptake without an added chemical oxidant. Under simulated solar irradiation, the material achieved efficient oxidant-free arsenic removal through coupled As(III) photooxidation and As(V) adsorption, enabling nearly complete oxidation of 10 mg/L As(III) within 3 h and a high maximum As(V) adsorption capacity of 349.1 mg/g. The system also showed good environmental adaptability and reusability, maintaining over 85% arsenic removal efficiency across pH 3–9 in the presence of common coexisting ions, with negligible performance decay after four regeneration cycles. Mechanistic analysis reveals that the enlarged interlayer spacing and exposed terminal groups provide abundant binding sites for As(V), while the ultrathin Few-Layer structure and favorable interfacial charge transfer promote As(III) photooxidation. This work demonstrates an oxidant-free MXene-based strategy for efficient remediation of arsenic-contaminated water.

title: Combined exposure to polyethylene microplastics, copper, and Di(2-Ethylhexyl) phthalate reconfigures component-specific internal exposure profiles and triggers cross-level biological responses in earthworms
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Lei Chen, Kangjun Zeng, Ting Li, Yining Wu, He Wang
abstract: Microplastics, metals, and plastic additives commonly coexist in soils, but how their interactions reconfigure internal exposure and relate to biological responses across multiple levels We exposed Eisenia fetida to polyethylene microplastics (PE), copper (Cu), and di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) singly and in binary and ternary combinations, integrating internal exposure, organismal phenotypes, redox biomarkers, histopathology, gut microbiota, and untargeted metabolomics. Combined exposure reconfigured rather than uniformly increased internal exposure: under ternary exposure, whole-body Cu decreased from 17.96 to 10.34 mg kg⁻¹ , whereas DEHP increased from 2735.76 to 8523.19 μg kg⁻¹ , while gut-retained PE varied among mixtures. Ternary exposure produced the strongest organismal effects, with mortality reaching 34%, body-weight loss 18.16%, reproductive and locomotor impairment, and ROS increasing 4.9-fold over the control. Gut bacterial responses were contaminant-specific: PE increased Chao1 richness from 1808 to 2579, while community composition differed among treatments (PERMANOVA, R² = 0.482, P = 0.001) and assembly shifted markedly under PE + DEHP and DEHP + Cu. Predicted microbial functions differed among treatments (R² = 0.525), with internal PE and Cu burdens significantly associated with KO profiles. Metabolomics identified 100, 66, and 124 candidate metabolites under PE, Cu, and DEHP, respectively, while Cu showed the clearest FDR-supported pathway enrichment. These findings reveal component-specific internal exposure linked to host, microbial, and metabolic responses.

title: Detection of degradation products of chemical warfare agents in Halabja soil: In vitro genotoxicity and effects in exposed humans
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hanna Hakulinen, Huiyuan Zheng, Anne Puustinen, Matti Kjellberg, Arja Valtanen, Paula Vanninen, Ulla Stenius, Johan Högberg, Aram Ghalali
abstract: The town of Halabja in Iraqi Kurdistan remains a symbol of the devastating impact of chemical weapons. Almost four decades after the attack, inhabitants continue to suffer from increased cancer rates and severe respiratory, neurological, and psychiatric disorders. While the acute effects of chemical warfare agents have been widely studied, their long-term environmental persistence and associated health impacts remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the presence of chemical warfare agent residues in the environment and assessed their potential genotoxic effects. Soil and water samples collected in Halabja in 2021 were analyzed for chemical warfare agents, including sulfur mustard, sarin, and their degradation products using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry with dual flame photometric detection and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry, selected for their sensitivity toward sulfur- and phosphorus-containing compounds. In soil samples, we detected thiodiglycolic acid and methylphosphonic acid, degradation products of sulfur mustard and organophosphorus nerve agents, respectively. To evaluate biological relevance, soil-derived extracts were tested in vitro using Western blotting to assess markers of DNA damage and inflammation, revealing elevated levels of both endpoints. Because some soil samples also contained the persistent organic pollutant p,p′-DDE, the observed genotoxic effects were interpreted as potentially reflecting contributions from both CWA-related degradation products and other environmental contaminants. To complement these findings, plasma and peripheral blood mononuclear cells from individuals exposed in 1988 were analyzed in 2025, by flow cytometry and ELISA, demonstrating increased levels of the same markers compared with controls. Together, these findings indicate long-term environmental persistence of chemical warfare agent degradation products and their genotoxic potential, while also highlighting that other environmental contaminants may contribute to the biological effects observed in complex soil extracts, alongside sustained biological effects in exposed individuals.

title: Synergistic enhancement of quinoline degradation and nitrogen removal in a coupling FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis and partial denitrification-anammox system: performance and mechanisms
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hao Shen, Chao Pang, Hong Mei, Yan Wang, Chunhua He, Wei Wang
abstract: Quinoline in coal chemical wastewater severely inhibits the performance of partial denitrification-anammox (PD/A) process. This study innovatively developed a FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis coupled PD/A system to simultaneously enhance quinoline degradation and nitrogen removal under quinoline stress. The coupled system achieved quinoline and nitrogen removal efficiencies of 92.0 ± 2.4% and 81.7 ± 1.7%, respectively, outperforming the control (32.8 ± 6.0% and 17.8 ± 9.5%), FeS (73.3 ± 6.8% and 53.8 ± 5.4%), and ZVI (75.3 ± 9.3% and 51.6 ± 5.6%) groups. Mechanistically, the FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis facilitated reactive species generation, thereby enhancing the abiotic removal of quinoline (30.0 ± 0.7%). Meanwhile, FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis maintained higher microbial electron transport and energy metabolism, with electron transport system activity, electron-donating capacity, and ATPase activity being 31.9–133.1%, 30.4–116.5%, and 104.1–771.3% higher, respectively, than those in the other groups. Crucially, quinoline degradation into chain compounds and the release of Fe2 +/S2- via FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis, enhanced heterotrophic and autotrophic partial denitrification, respectively, ultimately supporting anammox. Metagenomics analysis revealed enrichment of the electroactive bacteria (Pseudomonas), quinoline-degrading bacteria (Exiguobacterium), and genes involved in carbon (Ior A/B, PcaD, LigC), nitrogen (hdh, hzs, narB), and sulfur (Sox) metabolism. Therefore, the FeS-ZVI microelectrolysis-PD/A system achieved synergistic carbon and nitrogen removal under quinoline stress.

title: Ag-SnO 2 nanofibers with lattice oxygen activation for high performance triethylamine gas sensor
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Lihao Lv, Wei Cao, Kairui Liu, Chong Li, Jingfeng Wang, Lei Guo, Zhijun Ding, Peichang Shi, Chun Li, Puhong Wang, Lingmin Yu
abstract: TEA is a highly flammable and neurotoxic volatile organic compound; prolonged exposure can lead to emphysema and even immediate death, making the development of rapid, highly responsive TEA gas sensors an urgent priority. Although tin dioxide (SnO2)-based sensors have been extensively studied, they suffer from low sensitivity and high operating temperatures. In this study, silver-loaded tin dioxide nanofibers (Ag-SnO2 NFs) with a porous hollow structure were fabricated using electrospinning combined with in-situ reduction technology. The Schottky junction at the Ag-SnO2 interface triggers interfacial electron redistribution, thereby activating lattice oxygen (OL) in SnO2 and converting it into adsorbed oxygen species, which enhances the gas-sensing performance for TEA. At 200℃, the AS-2 sensor exhibited a response value of 2163.6 for 100 ppm of TEA, which is 79 times that of pure SnO2, and demonstrated fast response and recovery times (48 s/44 s). In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further elucidated this mechanism. This study provides a new mechanistic insight into how noble metal modification activates lattice oxygen and converts it into adsorbed oxygen to enhance gas sensing performance, offering rational design principles for advanced gas sensors targeting harmful volatile compounds.

title: Material-specific modulation of microplastic biotoxicity by chlorination: Mechanistic insights into ER stress and associated health risks
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Linxiang Lyu, Li Xiao, Zhikun Chen, Xiaohan Yang, Huifang Bi, He Peng, Shuyan Wan, Huaixiang Tian, Qian Tan, Chunjiang An
abstract: Chlorination, a widely used disinfection method in drinking water treatment plants, poses underexplored health risks through its interactions with microplastics (MPs). Here, we show that chlorination induces significant physicochemical changes in four common MPs—polyethylene (PE), polyurethane (PU), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA)—focusing on particles smaller than 30 µm. PU and PE MPs exhibit the most pronounced changes including significant surface degradation and oxidation, releasing various organic compounds. In vitro assays show that disinfected PU MPs significantly increased cytotoxicity, while disinfected PE MPs mitigated toxicity by modulating ER stress via the IRE1α/XBP1/BIP pathway. In vivo, 30-day exposure to pristine PE and disinfected PU MPs induce tissue damage, inflammation, and immune responses. Transcriptomic analysis of Liver revealed disrupted lipid, glutathione, and iron metabolism, activating DNA replication and proteasome pathways linked to ER stress. mRNA validation confirmed that disinfected MPs induces toxicity via the PERK/EIF2α/ATF4 pathway, with disinfected PU MPs causing severe damage, with significant CHOP upregulation indicating apoptosis. These findings underscore the biotoxicological impacts of disinfected MPs and provide insights for optimizing disinfection methods and mitigating the health risks of MPs in water treatment, particularly given the widespread use of chlorination worldwide.

title: Reconciling mass and number emissions through particle size: Implications for urban ultrafine particle modelling
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Soo-Jin Park, Lya Lugon, Youngseob Kim, Alexia Baudic, Amandine Rosso, Jeroen Kuenen, Marya el Malki, Karine Sartelet
abstract: Ultrafine particles (UFPs) contribute only a small fraction of particulate mass but dominate atmospheric particle number, making size-resolved particle-number (PN) emissions essential for urban exposure modelling. This study evaluates how methodologies for estimating size-resolved UFP emissions affect simulated PN concentrations over Greater Paris, from regional background to street level. Simulations were performed for summer 2021 with the WRF-CHIMERE/MUNICH/SSH-aerosol modelling framework. A mass- and number-conserving algorithm was implemented to consistently combine PM mass emissions with PN emission factors in a sectional aerosol model. Sensitivity scenarios examined traffic exhaust emissions constrained by COPERT or on-board-measurement PN factors, traffic non-exhaust emissions, and the sector related to industrial processes without combustion, which includes construction activities. The reference simulation, based on PM mass emissions and prescribed representative diameters by activity sector, reproduced total PN concentrations well at background and traffic stations, showing that a simple mass-based methodology can estimate total PN concentrations across scales. However, uncertainties remained in the simulated size distribution, particularly for particles around 10 nm. Non-exhaust traffic emissions had a limited but non-negligible influence, contributing to about a third of total traffic PN. More detailed size-resolved PN emission factors, including particles below 10 nm, are needed to improve UFP exposure modelling.

title: vToxiNet: An interpretable deep learning framework for hepatotoxicity prediction and mechanism exploration
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xuelian Jia, Tong Wang, Daniel P. Russo, Lauren M. Aleksunes, Shuo Xiao, Hao Zhu
abstract: Hepatotoxicity remains a leading cause of drug attrition and post-marketing withdrawal, resulting from diverse and complex toxicity mechanisms. Traditional in vitro models can only capture a limited subset of toxicity pathways, and animal studies face translational and ethical limitations. Regulatory agencies have therefore promoted new approach methodologies, including human-relevant assays, omics technologies, and computational models to improve predictive toxicology and support evidence-based decision-making. However, most machine learning models for hepatotoxicity either rely solely on chemical structure or operate as black boxes, limiting mechanistic interpretability and broader applicability. Here, we introduce the virtual toxicity network (vToxiNet), a biologically constrained deep learning framework that embeds systems toxicology knowledge directly into neural network architecture for interpretable hepatotoxicity prediction. vToxiNet integrates chemical descriptors, high-throughput assay responses, transcriptomic signatures, and Reactome pathway hierarchy to construct a virtual adverse outcome pathway network. Across cross-validation and external validation, vToxiNet demonstrates promising predictive performance. Importantly, interpretation of vToxiNet enables gene and pathway-level attribution, supporting mechanism-informed hazard characterization and chemical prioritization. By integrating multimodal data and biological hierarchy as architectural constraints, this study provides a framework that combines prediction with mechanistic interpretation and supports further development of mechanism-informed approaches for chemical hazard assessment.

title: An overlooked source of inhalational and dermal exposure to bisphenol A and its chlorinated derivatives in disposable face masks
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Ying Li, Xiaoxuan Han, Li Gao, Fangdong Jiao, Yong Tian, Jia Lv, Ya Jiao, Wei Gao, Xiangyu Liu, Yijing Chu, Shuo Gao, Yongfeng Lin
abstract: The presence of emerging and toxic chlorinated bisphenol A derivatives (ClxBPA) in disposable face masks (DFMs) remains unconfirmed. A total of 123 DFMs of various types, sourced primarily from China with additional samples from other Asian regions, North America, and Europe were analyzed. The results illustrated bisphenol A (BPA) was detected in all samples, while 3-monochloro bisphenol A (MCBPA) and 3,3’,5,5’-tetrachloro-bisphenol A (TCBPA) were found in over 65% of DFMs. BPA exhibited the highest concentrations (geometric mean: 11.6 ng g–1), followed by TCBPA (0.0446 ng g–1), MCBPA (0.0234 ng g–1), 3,3’-dichlorobisphenol A (DCBPA-1, 0.0179 ng g⁻¹), 3,3’,5-trichloro-bisphenol A (TriCBPA, 0.0169 ng g–1), and 3,5-dichloro bisphenol A (DCBPA-2, 0.0142 ng g–1). Notably, the proportion of DFM samples in which at least one ClxBPA congener was detected reached 92.7%, indicating the widespread occurrence of ClxBPA in DFMs. The concentration levels of BPA and ClxBPA varied by mask material but not between adult and toddler masks or across production regions. Exposure assessment indicated that occupational users and toddlers face higher BPA and ClxBPA exposure risks, particularly when using N95 and disposable activated carbon masks. Given the reported toxicological effects of ClxBPA, the health risks posed by these emerging contaminants deserve further attention.

title: Capturing the dual organic-metal hazard of fire smoke: Material-dependent passive sampling of PAHs and battery-derived metals
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Md. Touhidul Islam, Md. Jalal Uddin Rumi, Md. Jakir Hossain, Mazyar Etemadzadeh, Yulin Wu, Mengying Zhang, Rui Li, Guowen Song
abstract: Wildland-urban interface and battery-involved fires emit chemically complex smoke containing carcinogenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and metal-rich aerosols. However, the comparative performance of passive sampler materials under these conditions remains poorly defined. This study evaluated six chemically and structurally distinct materials: silicone wristband (SWB), polyurethane foam (PUF), activated carbon felt (ACF), thermoplastic polyurethane nanofiber (TPU), cotton fabric (CF), and cotton ball (CB) under controlled smoke from pine, pine + polystyrene (PS), and pine + battery scenarios. The 16 priority PAHs listed by the United States Environmental Protection Agency, along with battery-derived elements, were quantified and benchmarked against active sampling. Active sampling showed clear source-dependent profiles: total PAHs increased from 10.2 µg m⁻³ in pine smoke to 167.8 µg m⁻³ in pine + PS smoke, while pine + battery smoke was dominated by metal-rich aerosol, especially nickel (∼840 µg m⁻³). Passive uptake was strongly material dependent. Under the high-PAH pine + PS scenario, PUF retained the highest total PAHs (∼1.50 µg cm⁻²), followed by TPU (∼1.24 µg cm⁻²) and SWB (∼1.11 µg cm⁻²). ACF showed selective naphthalene enrichment, whereas SWB retained the highest battery-derived metal loading (∼46 µg cm⁻²), followed by PUF (∼38 µg cm⁻²) and TPU (∼30 µg cm⁻²). Scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy indicated that PAH uptake was governed mainly by sorption and partitioning, while metal retention reflected particle deposition and surface adhesion. These findings highlight the need for complementary, multi-material sampling strategies matched to the target exposure metric.

title: Atmospheric deposition as a substantial source of lead in wheat grain: Between-year variation and uptake-pathway contributions
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hailong Liu, Chao Zhu, Hui Yang, Yuansong Ding, Haowei Zhu, Jun Zhou, Xiaozhi Wang, Min Li
abstract: Atmospheric deposition is a critical pathway for lead (Pb) entry into agroecosystems; however, the patterns of its between-year accumulation and the contributions of foliar and root uptake to Pb levels in crops remain unclear. In this study, we combined a two-year factorial field exposure with a foliar-exposure trial in wheat to elucidate these mechanisms. Pb concentrations in wheat varied in accordance with the interannual deposition flux of Pb, decreasing synchronously as the flux declined from the first to the second year, demonstrating that crop Pb levels tracked annual atmospheric inputs. Extending soil exposure to atmospheric deposition from one to two years did not increase Pb concentrations in soil solution or wheat tissues. This suggested that, under the conditions of this study, newly deposited Pb during the current growing season—rather than Pb previously deposited in the soil—may be the primary source of Pb in wheat, as its bioavailability decreased markedly with soil aging. Quantitative pathway partitioning further revealed a sustained high contribution from foliar uptake to grain Pb accumulation (24.7%–68.8%), highlighting aboveground exposure as the key target for intervention. Collectively, these findings challenge conventional soil-centric management frameworks and emphasize the importance of reducing atmospheric Pb deposition and regulating foliar uptake to ensure the safe production of crops.

title: Oxidative conversion of HEDP to phosphate in charged water microdroplets
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zijun Yu, Yu Xia, Maojun Yu, Jiayang Li, Yong Liang, Jianbo Shi
abstract: Organophosphonates are persistent anthropogenic phosphorus compounds because of their stable carbon–phosphorus bonds. Whether such compounds can be oxidatively converted to inorganic phosphate at dynamic air–water interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, using 1-hydroxyethylidene-1,1-diphosphonic acid (HEDP) as a model organophosphonate, we show its stepwise oxidation in charged water microdroplets under mild conditions. Online mass spectrometry revealed a marked decrease in the deprotonated HEDP signal and the appearance of H2PO4 - at m/z 96.9685, while ion chromatography and CO2 analysis independently confirmed phosphate formation and carbon oxidation. Charge measurements and high-speed imaging showed atomization-induced charge separation, and simulations indicated possible local electric-field enhancement between oppositely charged droplets. Electron paramagnetic resonance, melatonin oxidation, H2 18O labeling, and tert-butyl alcohol scavenging experiments further showed that water-derived hydroxyl radicals are generated during atomization and participate in HEDP oxidation. Time-resolved product profiles identified transient phosphorus-containing intermediates and small organic acids, followed by the accumulation of phosphate and CO2. Detected carbon and phosphorus recoveries further constrained the elemental redistribution during the reaction. These results establish charged microdroplets as a model interfacial system for HEDP-to-phosphate conversion and support a mechanism involving water-derived hydroxyl radicals, with possible contributions from localized electric fields and oxygen-involved radical chemistry.

title: Precursor-dependent reconstruction of iron-carbon interface for high-efficiency removal of Cr(VI)
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Jinna Gu, Xiaoguang Liu, Xiaohu Dai
abstract: Using kitchen waste digestate as the feedstock, we assessed the impacts of precursor carbonization degree on modified chars’ characterization, compared their Cr(VI) removal behavior, and clarified the high-efficiency Cr(VI) removal mechanisms. K2FeO4 promoted pore development, surface oxygen-containing group enrichment, and in-situ anchoring of iron species in torrefied chars and hydrochars, whereas it mainly introduced iron-based active sites in pyrolysis chars. K2FeO4 modification effectively improved the Cr(VI) removal performance of the chars. The equilibrium adsorption capacity increased by 83.8–100.8% from 39.46 to 54.29 mg·g−1 to 79.24–100.20 mg·g−1 . Isotherm results suggested monolayer adsorption for modified torrified char and heterogeneous multilayer adsorption for modified pyrolysis char and hydrochar. The maximum adsorption capacity of modified torrified char increased from 90.91 to 96.91 mg·g−1, whereas the Freundlich adsorption coefficient of modified pyrolysis char and hydrochar increased markedly by 467% and 39%, respectively. The thermodynamic driving force, heat‑absorbing property, and randomness at solid‑liquid interface of Cr(VI) removal were evidently promoted. Cr(VI) was removed by K2FeO4-modified chars via several mechanisms, including surface electrostatic accumulation, inner-layer complexation capture, reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III), and Fe/Cr co-precipitation. These findings lay a solid scientific foundation for optimizing the preparation and usage of the K2FeO4 modified chars for Cr(VI) removal.

title: Functional complementarity in a heavy oil-degrading consortium through cross-feeding, detoxification, pH stability, and transcriptional relief
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): José Aparecido de Sousa Bernardino Leite, Júlia Firme Freitas, Patrícia Vieira de Araújo, Douglas Felipe de Lima Silva, Lucymara Fassarella Agnez Lima
abstract: Heavy oil bioremediation is challenged by hydrocarbon recalcitrance and toxicity, requiring synergistic microbial consortia. This study formulated a tripartite biodegradation microbial consortium (BMC) comprising Micrococcus luteus BD1, Acinetobacter baumannii subsp. oleum ficedula BD54, and Ochrobactrum oleinvorans BD61, guided by genomic screening and Flux Balance Analysis (FBA). In microcosms, the BMC achieved 77% degradation of heavy oil (16° API) in 15 days, significantly outperforming monocultures. Initially, all strains attack aliphatic fractions, with BD1 operating via monooxygenases and adh, while BD54 and BD61 secrete biosurfactants (80% emulsification). In late stages, as BD54 and BD61 shift to complex aromatic cleavage (benD and pcaH), BD1 transitions into a detoxifying "metabolic sink" supporting pH stability. FBA and Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) provided a testable hypothesis of proton-associated metabolism. In vitro assays validated that the consortium maintains neutral pH, mitigates toxic phenol accumulation, and displays bidirectional exudate cross-feeding. This detoxification prevents enzyme inhibition and triggers systemic transcriptional relief, as evidenced by RT-qPCR and total oil and grease (TOG) analysis. Social coordination is supported by quorum sensing networks (LuxI/LuxR and RiPP-like). Integrating in silico modeling with in vitro validation reveals functional complementarity through cross-feeding, detoxification, pH buffering, and bioavailability enhancement, sustaining continuous heavy oil mineralization.

title: Dual-functional Bacillus cereus X1 drives hydrocarbon biodegradation and carbon sequestration via glnQ -mediated metabolic rewiring
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Jiayu Song, Hui Lin, Qinghong Wang, Linxuan Zhang, Anming Xu, Ziyi Peng, Yakui Chen, Yaohui Bai, Xingchun Li, Wenzhong Tang, Hong Zhang
abstract: Petroleum hydrocarbon contamination poses dual environmental challenges: direct ecosystem pollution and indirect exacerbation of greenhouse gas emissions via microbial mineralization, while natural carbon fixation pathways (e.g., the RuBisCO-mediated Calvin cycle) are insufficient at offsetting CO₂ release due to RuBisCO’s inherent catalytic limitations. To address this, we engineered a dual-functional Bacillus cereus X1 strain capable of coupled hydrocarbon degradation and enhanced CO₂ fixation through optimization of a glnQ-centered metabolic network. Starting from oil-contaminated sludge, 40 carbon-fixing strains were isolated, with B. cereus X1 as the top performer, exhibiting the highest RuBisCO level (74.4 ± 2.8 U/g) together with confirmed n-alkane-degrading activity.
