Using Atmospheric Room-Temperature Plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis, we generated mutant derivatives (X1-Mut13/29) displaying a 1.29–1.34-fold elevation in RuBisCO level to the wild type that was stably inherited over ten serial passages. Whole-genome resequencing identified a shared nonsynonymous variant in glnQ (c.836 C>T; p.Ala279Val), encoding the ATP-binding subunit of a glutamine ABC transporter. Expression of the mutant glnQ A279V allele in wild-type X1 generated X1-glnQ, which exhibited 2.13 times the RuBisCO level of the empty-vector control and the lowest mean residual TPH concentration among the inoculated treatments in oily-residue microcosms (690 ± 62.23 mg kg−1 dry residue). Transcriptomics profiling revealed that glnQ overexpression upregulated key enzymes of the Calvin cycle (e.g., fbaA, glpX, tktA), glycolysis (gapA, pgk), and tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, thereby enhancing NADPH/ATP supply to support carbon fixation particularly for RuBP regeneration. Mechanistically, glnQ overexpression influenced cellular C/N status, redirecting glutamine-derived α-ketoglutarate to replenish TCA cycle intermediates and fuel anaplerotic CO₂ assimilation. Collectively, this study establishes a novel “degrade-and-sequester” biocatalyst that enables synergistic pollution remediation and carbon fixation, providing a blueprint for engineering microbial carbon loops in oil-contaminated ecosystems. Synopsis This study engineers a hydrocarbon-degrading Bacillus cereus X1 strain with enhanced CO₂ fixation capacity via glnQ-mediated metabolic reprogramming, offering a novel bioremediation strategy for petroleum-contaminated environments. By leveraging glnQ—a key regulator of nitrogen and carbon metabolism—as a metabolic hub, the strain is designed to couple hydrocarbon catabolism with CO₂ sequestration, addressing the dual challenges of environmental pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. These findings support partial CO₂ reassimilation as a potential route to improve carbon-use efficiency during bioremediation, advancing sustainable solutions for contaminated ecosystem restoration.

title: Thiamphenicol decouples acidogenesis from methanogenesis and redirects carbon flux toward volatile fatty acids in sludge anaerobic digestion
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Shumeng Yang, Yuting Luo, Xiang Zou, Wei Zhang, Yinglong Su, Jingyang Luo, Feng Wang
abstract: Antibiotic residues in waste activated sludge (WAS) may disrupt anaerobic carbon conversion, yet how phenicol antibiotics redistribute carbon between acidogenesis and methanogenesis remains unclear. At 10 mg/g TSS, methane production decreased by 63.2% while VFAs reached 131-fold the control. This functional decoupling was underpinned by microbial fates: hydrolytic-acidogenic bacteria were largely retained or enriched, whereas methanogenic archaea and syntrophic bacteria were severely depleted. Concurrently, bacteria–archaea ecological networks underwent reorganization, with positive correlations partially rebounding at moderate TAP exposure. The network collapsed at high TAP, with substantial loss of connector taxa mediating inter-module metabolite exchange. Metagenomic evidence further revealed a functional asymmetry: genes involved in substrate transport and amino acid metabolism were maintained or showed increased relative abundance, while methanogenic genes and AI-2-associated communication genes exhibited decreased relative abundance. PLS-PM revealed that TAP was positively associated with the acidogenic bacterial community (β = 0.960) but negatively with methanogenic potential (β = −0.998). Accordingly, the methane share dropped from 98.7% to 18.1%, while VFAs increased to 81.9% of the COD-equivalent product pool. This work advances the understanding of antibiotic-driven functional imbalance and carbon flux redirection in sludge anaerobic digestion, providing a mechanistic basis for managing antibiotic-laden sludge prior to energy recovery.

title: Simultaneous valorization of nitrate and formaldehyde waste streams to hexamethylenetetramine via photo-electro-thermo-catalysis
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yan Sun, Lijun Yang, Lei Zhang
abstract: To remediate nitrate (NO3 –) pollution and recover resources from formaldehyde wastewater, this work presents a waste valorization strategy integrating photoelectrocatalytic nitrate reduction (PEC NO3RR) to ammonia (NH3) with downstream chemical upgrading. Herein, a hollow MoO2@CuFe2O4@MnFe2O4 Z-scheme-Schottky dual heterojunction nanoreactor array is developed to spatially separate proton and nitrate adsorption sites. The MoO2@CuFe2O4@MnFe2O4 improves photogenerated charge separation and retaining robust redox capability, while the oxygen vacancy-rich MoO2 layer exhibits favorable photothermal features to extend light harvesting, accelerate carrier migration and produce localized heating through localized surface plasmon resonance for reduced reaction energy barriers. Interfacial built-in electric field combined with spatial confinement jointly promote nitrate capture and enrichment. Fast hydrogen intercalation/deintercalation within MoO2 create a dynamically *H-enriched surface to boost NO3RR-to-NH3 conversion efficiency. This system resolves kinetic incompatibility between NO3 – reduction and hydrogen supply, effectively suppressing NO2 – accumulation and hydrogen evolution. It delivers an NH3 yield rate of 5.96 mM h–1 cm–2 at –0.6 V vs. RHE with high selectivity and stability over 24 h. The in-situ generated NH3 further transforms formaldehyde wastewater into high-value hexamethylenetetramine. This process enables simultaneous detoxification of two waste-streams and nitrogen/carbon feedstock upgradation, providing a closed-loop pathway for integrated pollution abatement and resource reclamation.

title: Phosphate rock drives greater arsenic accumulation in Pteris vittata than calcium carbonate by enhancing arsenic metabolism and reshaping rhizosphere microbiome
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Ruimin Jin, Qianyu Zhou, Songge Deng, Chunyan Hu, Qishang Zhou, Lena Ma
abstract: Poorly-soluble phosphate rock (PR) and CaCO3 can enhance arsenic accumulation in calcicolous As-hyperaccumulator Pteris vittata, but their mechanisms under soil conditions remain unclear. P. vittata was grown for two months in As-contaminated soil (100 mg kg–1) receiving 2.0 g kg–1 Ca as PR, CaCO3, or soluble CaCl2. Plant nutrients, rhizosphere chemistry and bacterial communities, and As-metabolism genes were examined. Compared with CaCO3, PR increased frond As and P by 35% and 28% to 3128 and 3158 mg kg–1, while CaCO3 produced slightly greater biomass and 10–15% higher rhizosphere available As and P. PR upregulated P-transporter PvPht1;3, arsenate reductase PvHAC2, and arsenite antiporters PvACR3 and PvACR3;3 by 2.0–2.3 fold, whereas CaCO3 induced PvPht1;3, PvPTB1;2, and PvACR3;1/3;2 by 1.7–3.3 fold relative to the soil control. PR retained a more diverse bacterial community (Shannon: 4.20) containing taxa associated with P cycling and As tolerance, whereas CaCO3 showed lower diversity (3.76) under elevated pH. These findings link superior As accumulation under PR to P acquisition, distinct As-metabolism transcriptional responses, and rhizosphere restructuring, providing a mechanistic basis for selecting PR to enhance As accumulation during phytoremediation of As-contaminated soils.

title: Facet-dependent activation of chlorine dioxide over Mn 2 O 3 for benzo[ a ]pyrene degradation
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Ailijiang Tuerdi, Fanyu Wang, Jiamin Zheng, Meng Zhang, Jun Wang, Fanbin Meng, Yuning Yang, Bing Qin, Xiao Liu
abstract: Benzo[a]pyrene (Bap) is a representative highly recalcitrant and extremely toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon. Although chlorine dioxide (ClO2) oxidation technology can be employed for Bap treatment, it often suffers from incomplete oxidation and the residual accumulation of highly toxic intermediate products. In this study, a series of Mn2O3 catalysts with different exposed facets are synthesized to regulate ClO2 activation pathways for deep Bap degradation. The cubic Mn2O3 exposing predominantly (001) facets possesses more oxygen vacancies and facilitates the adsorption of ClO2 species. These adsorbed ClO2 species subsequently undergo coupling disproportionation to generate singlet oxygen (1O2) and chlorine radical species (•ClO), while concurrently enabling the formation of transient high-valent MnV(O)+ species. The synergistic interaction between 1O2 and MnV(O)+ establishes a non-radical-dominated oxidation regime, leading to an efficient Bap degradation rate exceeding 97.6% and excellent stability. In contrast, Mn2O3 exposing (111) facets with fewer oxygen vacancies shows lower activity because Bap degradation proceeds mainly via hydroxyl radical (•OH)-dominated pathways. This work demonstrates that the facet engineering of Mn2O3 can be tuned to regulate the activation pathways of chlorine dioxide, providing fundamental mechanistic insight and a rational design strategy for the efficient and deep oxidation of persistent polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.

title: Emerging plastic additives in umbilical cord serum, metabolomic profiles, and fetal growth restriction: A case-control study
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Mengxuan Xie, Wei Qiu, Shuqin Tang, Xiaoqing He, Da Chen, Jun Zhang, Wei Huang, Yun Huang, for the Early Life Plan
abstract: Background Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with substantial perinatal and long-term health risks. As traditional plasticizers are being restricted, exposure to emerging plastic additives is increasing, yet their associations with FGR and related metabolic profiles remain poorly characterized. Methods This case-control study included 90 FGR cases and 100 controls from the “Early Life Plan” cohort. A total of 117 plastic additives were measured in umbilical cord serum, and untargeted metabolomics was performed using UHPLC-HRMS. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR), and quantile g-computation were used to evaluate the effects of single and mixed exposures of these chemicals on fetal growth outcomes. Meet-in-the-middle (MITM) analysis and pathway enrichment analysis were performed to identify associated metabolic features. Results UV-360 was positively associated with FGR (OR = 1.35, 95% CI: 1.11–1.64), while 2,6-DtBEP was negatively associated with FGR (OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.61–0.84). Neither BKMR nor quantile g-computation provided clear evidence of an overall association between the 21-chemical mixture and FGR. Exploratory class-specific BKMR analyses suggested positive and negative associations for UV stabilizers and antioxidants, respectively. Differential metabolites were mainly enriched in amino acid, lipid, and one-carbon metabolism. MITM analyses suggested that six metabolites, including Valine, Proline, Palmitoylcarnitine, Ornithine, Xanthine, and (25 R)-Delta(4)-dafachronic acid, may be involved in the associations of UV-360 and DiBA/DnBA with FGR. Conclusions Concentrations of selected plastic additives in umbilical cord serum were associated with FGR, with UV-360 being consistently associated with higher odds of FGR. Metabolomic findings suggest that amino acid and lipid metabolism may be involved in these associations, warranting further validation in future studies.

title: Chemical composition and toxicological properties of particulate emissions from lithium-ion battery fires
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Elizabeth DeFrance, Zisimos Toumasatos, Wonsik Woo, Xena Mansoura, Byoungchul Kwon, Vinay Premnath, Judith Jeevarajan, Ying-Hsuan Lin, Georgios Karavalakis
abstract: This study assessed the physical, chemical, and toxicological properties of particulate emissions produced from lithium-ion battery fires. Commercially-available nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) battery modules were overcharged to trigger thermal runaway. The first experiment allowed the battery modules to burn without engaging any suppression system, while two additional experiments were performed with water and a potassium-based aerosol to suppress the battery fires. Results showed the formation of large diameter particles with geometric mean diameters of ∼360 nm, with their majority be below 1 μm. Depending on the experimental conditions, particle morphology revealed the generation of more spherical complex particles, while particle composition showed a mix of organic and inorganic agglomerates. Particle metallic composition was dominated by Li, Ni, Mn, Co, O, and Al, consistent with the chemistry of the battery modules. Medium and high molecular weight polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) showed higher concentrations than lighter PAHs. Small-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) dominated the particle emissions, with the presence of legacy PFAS suggesting that these compounds are still used in the manufacturing of lithium-ion batteries. All particle samples induced elevated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and correlation analysis identified relationships between particle composition and toxicological outcomes.

title: PM 2.5 exposure and retinal neurovascular dysfunction: Clinical and mechanistic evidence for complement C3/C3aR pathway involvement
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yi Tian, Yixiang Zhu, Xinyao Yu, Ji Zhou, Haidong Kan, Xinghuai Sun, Yuan Lei
abstract: PM2.5 is a pervasive environmental toxicant associated with retinal neurodegeneration, yet the mechanisms remain unclear. This study combined clinical, animal, and cellular approaches to investigate whether C3/C3aR signaling mediates PM2.5‑induced retinal neurovascular damage. In retrospective longitudinal glaucoma cohort, a linear mixed‑effects model analyzed PM2.5 effects on inflammatory markers. In mice, we examined PM2.5 effects on retinal complement, microglia activation, neurovascular function, and vision. The protective effect of the C3aR blocker SB290157 was also evaluated. BV2 and retinal endothelial cells were used to study C3‑dependent microglial polarization and its vasoregulatory effects. In clinical experiment, we identified a significant association between short-term PM2.5 exposure and systemic complement dysregulation, characterized by a decrease in serum C3c. In mice, PM2.5 exposure induced marked retinal C3 activation. This change was characterized by microglial activation, vascular dysfunction, and retinal structural and functional impairment. In vitro, PM2.5 directly induced C3/C3aR-dependent microglial M1 polarization and stimulated endothelial vasoconstrictor secretion via microglial crosstalk. Treatment with C3aR inhibitor attenuated the vicious cycle, preserving retinal structure and visual function. In conclusion, C3/C3aR axis serves as a key mechanistic link between PM2.5 exposure and retinal neurodegeneration. Targeting this pathway may offer a therapeutic strategy for mitigating pollution-related retinal damage.

title: Threshold-like transitions of microbial community states and functional reorganization in petroleum hydrocarbon-contaminated soils
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yuqian Li, Shumai Zhang, Beidou Xi, Caihong Huang
abstract: Petroleum hydrocarbon (PH) contamination alters soil microbial communities, yet whether microbial responses to PH contamination occur gradually or exhibit threshold-like transitions remains poorly understood. Here, soils collected along a PH contamination gradient surrounding an oil well were analyzed to identify microbial community states and their associations with environmental factors, community assembly, interactions, and functional potential. Bacterial communities exhibited a bimodal distribution, indicating two distinct states: State A was predominantly associated with higher PH contamination, whereas State B was associated with lower contamination. Random forest analysis identified PH contamination, particularly n-alkanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), together with inorganic nitrogen (N), as the environmental factors most strongly associated with state differentiation. Potential landscape analysis identified intermediate contamination ranges where both states occurred (2.50 ≤lg(n-alkanes)≤ 3.21; 1.61 ≤lg(PAHs)≤ 1.69), indicating threshold-like differentiation. State A exhibited lower diversity, stronger deterministic assembly, more modular co-occurrence networks, enrichment of hydrocarbon-degrading taxa, and greater predicted functional potential for hydrocarbon activation, aromatic ring cleavage, denitrification, and N assimilation. State B showed greater network connectivity and stronger predicted potential for downstream carbon assimilation, nitrification, and more balanced N transformation. These findings demonstrate that PH contamination is associated with nonlinear reorganization of microbial community structure and functional potential across different community states.

title: A study on the characteristics of soil heavy metal pollution and risk assessment resulting from particulate matter erupted during thermal runaway of ternary lithium-ion batteries
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yanni Zhang, Xinyi Mi, Hua Yang, Luoxin Huang, Yuchen Zhang, Yunchao Hou
abstract: Ternary lithium-ion batteries can release heavy-metal-containing particulate matter during thermal runaway, posing potential risks to soil after deposition. In this study, overcharge-induced thermal runaway tests were conducted on a 117 Ah NCM811 prismatic battery at 100% SOC in a sealed chamber. Particulate matter was collected by particle size and characterised using SEM, EDS and ICP-MS. The results showed clear particle-size-dependent characteristics. As particle size decreased, particle morphology changed from fused spherical agglomerates to loose, porous and flake-like structures, while the contents of Cr, Mn, Ni and Co and the proportions of exchangeable and carbonate-bound forms generally increased. A quantitative indicator system integrating particle migration, pollutant load and chemical speciation was established to assess potential soil heavy metal pollution risk. The comprehensive pollution index increased with decreasing particle size, and the 200–500 μm fraction exhibited the highest risk. These results identify 200–500 μm particles as the key fraction requiring priority attention and provide a quantitative basis for pollution risk assessment and control following battery thermal runaway.

title: VOC evolution during petrochemical abnormal operations and vertical characteristics during shutdown: Evidence from ground and tower observations
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xiaoya Dou, Guiying You, Hefan Liu, Lanni Luo, Jing Wang, Yan Chen, Yuanhang Zhang
abstract: Petrochemical shutdown, maintenance, and start-up operations emit substantial amounts of reactive volatile organic compounds (VOCs). However, the vertical distribution of these emissions within the lower boundary layer remains poorly characterized. This study combined full-cycle online monitoring with shutdown-stage multi-height tower sampling (10, 50 and 90 m) and receptor-site observations to investigate VOC evolution, vertical profiles, and spatial transport in a large petrochemical park. After meteorological normalization, mean TVOC concentrations during shutdown, maintenance, and start-up were 97.59, 106.62 and 85.36 ppbv, respectively. VOC composition showed more pronounced stage-dependent changes. Alkenes increased by 53.69% during maintenance, with ethene reaching 32.13 ppbv. Propylene and 1,3-butadiene increased markedly during start-up. During shutdown, TVOC showed a non-monotonic vertical profile and peaked at 146.29 ppbv at 50 m, 1.52 times that at 10 m. The difference between 10 and 50 m was significant (p < 0.001). VOC-derived OH reactivity (L OH) and ozone formation potential (OFP) also peaked at 50 m, reaching 32.07 s⁻1 and 1160.73 μg m⁻3, respectively. After normalization, L OH/TVOC was similar at 10 and 50 m, while OFP/TVOC increased with height. Near-ground observations within the park and at the tower during the shutdown stage showed reduced VOC concentration fluctuations during transport, accompanied by a shift from alkane- and alkene-dominated composition toward greater OVOC contributions. Combined near-ground and multi-height tower observations during shutdown highlighted the potential limitations of single-height near-ground monitoring in characterizing vertical variations in elevated plumes. These measurements support the value of height-resolved observations for characterizing reactive VOCs during petrochemical shutdown.

title: Comparative fate and risk of microplastics in sanitary landfills versus open dumping sites: A multidimensional assessment framework
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Jiaoming Pan, Peiyan Yuan, Erkai He, Xinde Cao, Ling Zhao, Xiaoyun Xu, Hao Qiu
abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) landfills are critical terrestrial reservoirs of microplastics (MPs), yet how disposal methodology governs MP fate remains poorly constrained, hindering accurate risk assessment and management. Here, we systematically compared MP pollution between an engineered sanitary landfill (SL) and an open dumping site (OD) in East China through field investigation and laboratory simulation. We analyzed spatial distribution, physicochemical characteristics, and release potential of MPs, and developed a novel Index (MDAI) that integrates soil species sensitivity distribution (SSD), abundance, size, shape, and polymer hazard to assess ecological risk. Results revealed that MP abundance in SL (5340–12,670 particles/kg soil) markedly exceeded that in OD (2100–5620 particles/kg soil), with SL exhibiting a distinct vertical accumulation gradient absent in OD. MP abundance on plastic waste were substantially higher, reaching 29,740 particles/kg plastic on deeply buried SL plastics. MPs in SL were predominantly small-sized fragments and films dominated by polypropylene, whereas OD contained more fibers and medium-sized fragments dominated by polyethylene. Surrounding soils of the OD showed higher MP levels and extremely high potential ecological risk (PERI), whereas those of the SL exhibited only Level III risk. Plastic waste from both sites demonstrated ongoing MP release potential, most pronounced for deeply buried SL waste. The MDAI indicated a higher comprehensive risk within SL (Level III) versus moderate but spatially dispersed risk around OD (Level II). This spatial disparity highlights distinct management priorities: for SL, ensuring long-term containment to prevent release of internally accumulated MPs; for OD, implementing immediate source control and migration barriers to limit off-site dispersion. This study provides a critical, multidimensional framework for assessing and managing MP pollution from these predominant waste disposal pathways.

title: Influence of root morphology and salinity on PFAS uptake by ten Australian wetland plant species
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hugo Carvalhal Silva, John Awad, Divina Navarro, Baden Myers, Albert Juhasz
abstract: Constructed Floating Wetlands (CFWs) show promise as nature-based technology for attenuating per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in surface water. However, few studies have investigated plant morphological and physiological characteristics that promote PFAS uptake. This study assessed ten wetland plant species exposed to PFAS-spiked stormwater (PFBS, PFPeA, PFHxS, PFOA, PFOS, 30 µg/L each), for 28 days, under two salinity conditions (200 and 1000 mg/L). At low salinity, all species accumulated PFAS, with variation according to species. T. triandra, P. labillardieri, and S. validus were most effective for short-chain compounds (5740–6610 ng PFBS, and 4330–5290 ng PFPeA), whereas E. acuta, C. fascicularis, P. labillardieri, and B. caldwellii accumulated more long-chain compounds (2040–2390 ng PFHxS, 6100–6590 ng PFOS, and 2320–2830 ng PFOA). Plants with thin, branched roots showed greater PFAS accumulation. Bioaccumulation data highlighted that PFAS carbon chain length influenced PFAS partitioning, with PFOS showing limited shoot translocation compared with PFBS and PFPeA (translocation factors: 0.2–2.8 vs 0.4–34.0 vs 0.5–24.6). Elevated salinity significantly suppressed the uptake and translocation of short-chain PFAS (particularly PFPeA), while long-chain compounds were less affected. Results suggest that species selection for CFW must consider plant morphology and site-specific water parameters for optimum removal of complex PFAS mixtures.

title: Redistribution of continuous airway exposure risk in polluted environments with high- to ultra-high-density dust particles: From nostrils to terminal bronchioles
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xianhang Yang, Haiming Yu, Ding Yuan, Xinyu Zhang, Wenping Wu, Qinghai Li
abstract: Dust particles are typical environmental pollutants. However, the characteristics of airway transportation and deposition of high/ultra-high-density dust remain understudied. In this study, a high-fidelity continuous airway model was constructed from the nostrils to the fine bronchiole ends based on real medical images. The deposition evolution and exposure risk redistribution of high- to ultra-high-density particles of various sizes were then investigated. The results demonstrated that: Particle size determined the spatial deposition pattern, while the deposition center migrated upward with increasing density. Particle deposition results from the coupling of mechanisms such as traditional inertial collision, secondary flow inertial effects, turbulent diffusion transport, and gravitational settling. Ultra-high density had different influences on the interception effect in different regions, and also differentially modulated the risk of bronchioles to particles of different sizes, especially the abnormal increase of PM2.5. These findings reveal the characteristics of deposition redistribution after inhaling high/ultra-high-density harmful dusts, helping clarify and control their risks to human health and the environment. They also provide a basis for further exploring associations between airway lesion locations and exposure preferences for specific particle sizes.

title: Molecular transformation of dissolved black carbon during photobleaching and its enhanced role in goethite-mediated 17α-ethinylestradiol anaerobic biotransformation
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Feiyuan Liu, Weiqing Ma, Zhicheng Liao, Chaochao Lai, Xiunan Cai, Huan He, Bin Huang, Xuejun Pan
abstract: Dissolved black carbon (DBC) is an important component of dissolved organic matter, which undergoes continuous photobleaching in the sunlit surface water. The resulting photobleached DBC (P-DBC) can subsequently be transported across the sediment-water interface into sediments rich in minerals and microbes, thereby regulating the transformation of organic contaminants. This study investigated photobleaching-induced molecular transformation of DBC and the mechanism of P-DBC in goethite-mediated 17α-ethinylestradiol (EE2) anaerobic biotransformation. The results showed that photobleaching promoted the oxidation and decarbonization of DBC, driving its molecular composition toward a higher oxidation state and lower energy density. Intensity and H content were the key molecular features governing the photochemical reactivity of DBC. P-DBC was enriched in oxygen-containing functional groups that could enhance electron transfer with goethite. Additionally, the higher bioavailability of P‑DBC enriched aromatic‑degrading bacteria. Species associated with iron reduction and organic matter transformation in the presence of goethite were increased. As a result, P-DBC combined with goethite significantly promoted the anaerobic biotransformation of EE2, achieving a removal efficiency of 73.0%. EE2 transformation involved de-ethynylation and decarboxylation to yield more oxygenated products, contrasting with co‑metabolism alone. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into the natural attenuation of estrogens in iron-rich aquatic environments.

title: Solar-hydrodynamic energy coupling enables round-the-clock algal inactivation in natural waters
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Wenjie Liu, Yunlu Jia, Guofei Dai, Yaogang Chen, Ziwen Yang, Xiaonan Sun, Jie Liu, Hui Yun, Haijian Luo, Xiyu Wei, Ningyan Peng, Ping Yang, Peng Yao, Zhixue Zou, Yanqin Li, Yinghe Zhang, Lu Lu, Lei Yang
abstract: Sustainable mitigation of harmful algal blooms in natural waters remains constrained by intermittent energy supply, quenching of reactive species (RS) in complex matrices, and limited recoverability of conventional nanocatalysts. Here, we report a piezo-photocatalytic strategy integrating ambient solar and hydrodynamic energy harvesting with floating catalyst deployment and selective RS regulation, enabling round-the-clock in situ algal control under realistic aquatic conditions. A Bi4O5I2/Bi2O2S (6BIS) heterojunction couples light and mechanical energy harvesting, extending catalytic activity across illuminated and dark conditions when the corresponding energy input is available. In the dark, weak mechanical agitation yields ∼50% algal inactivation within 4.5 h via limited piezoelectric activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS), increasing to 90% under ultrasonic stimulation. Under combined ultrasound and low-intensity visible light, complete algal inactivation is achieved within 2.5 h. Microcystin-LR (0.5 mg L−1) is degraded within 5 min. Mechanistic investigations reveal that PMS adsorption at Bi sites selectively promotes superoxide radicals and singlet oxygen, mitigating quenching by humic substances. Field tests using a floating-supported catalyst achieved 55% algal inactivation within 8 h under natural sunlight and ambient hydrodynamic conditions. This work provides a strategy for improving the temporal continuity of environmental remediation by coupling ambient renewable energy harvesting with selective RS regulation.

title: Paenibacillus polymyxa L62 synergistically regulates Pb 2+ speciation and reconstructs soil microecological networks via surface complexation and PbS mineralization
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zongsheng Yuan, Sifan Wang, Xiaoling Wang, Xun Dong, Fang Liu
abstract: The adsorption activity of Paenibacillus polymyxa L62 toward Pb2+ was evaluated in aqueous systems. Strain L62 achieved a Pb2+ removal efficiency of 95.97%. Its cell surface was enriched with functional groups such as –OH and –COO⁻, which promoted Pb2+ adsorption via complexation and ion exchange. In aqueous systems, XRD, FTIR, and EDS analyses suggested the possible formation of stable PbS crystalline precipitates on the cell surface. In soil incubation experiments, strain L62 was inoculated into Pb-contaminated soil at 1% (L1) and 3% (L3). Both treatments significantly promoted Pb transformation among different fractions, with L3 showing greater efficacy. Compared with the control, L3 increased soil cation exchange capacity and soil organic matter by 55.24% and 5.26%, respectively. Microbial community analysis showed that L1 and L3 enriched key bacterial genera, including Marinobacterium and Photobacterium, and significantly enhanced soil acid phosphatase, urease, and dehydrogenase activities. Collectively, P. polymyxa L62 removed Pb2+ in aqueous systems mainly through surface complexation and possible PbS mineralization. In soil, L62 promoted Pb transformation toward more stable fractions and reshaped the microbial community and enzyme activities.

title: Accumulation mechanisms and source-specific risks of PAHs across indoor and outdoor environments in a typical petrochemical industrial park
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Shun Li, Jing Wang, Xiaoxiao Han, Xiangshuai Bi, Zhunan Xiong, Hans Chr. Bruun Hansen, Lingqing Wang, Tao Liang
abstract: Prolonged petrochemical activities severely exacerbate polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) contamination in surrounding areas; however, the differential accumulation mechanisms and source-specific risks of these pollutants across off-site indoor and outdoor environments remain poorly understood. This study systematically investigated PAH occurrence and risks in soil, road dust, and indoor dust surrounding a typical petrochemical industrial park to elucidate their divergent multimedia accumulation pathways. The mean concentrations of ∑16PAHs (μg/kg) in soil, road dust, and indoor dust within the study area were 5.94 × 102, 4.66 × 103, and 5.28 × 103, respectively, with a mixed combustion-related source identified as the largest contributor to regional PAH contamination. An integrated analysis combining gradient boosting decision trees (GBDT) and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) indicated that multimedia PAH accumulation was shaped by the complex interplay between intrinsic matrix properties and external inputs. Specifically, total organic carbon (TOC) may directly influence PAH retention across the three matrices, while petrochemical sources and wind direction may indirectly affect PAH accumulation through matrix carbon content; traffic emissions likely intensify PAH loading in roadside environments. Additionally, source-specific assessments showed that road and indoor dust had higher PAH pollution and greater health risks than soil, with petrochemical-associated sources contributing most to both. This study advances understanding of PAH accumulation and distribution across multimedia environments under intensive industrial activities, providing a scientific basis for targeted PAH mitigation in industrial areas.

title: Multi-biomarker forensic assessment of petroleum pollution in a tropical riverine ecosystem using hopanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons with a wet-dry season comparison
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Sadeq Abdullah Abdo Alkhadher, Nor Kartini Abu Bakar, Mohammad Sherjeel Javed Khan, Najat Masood, Sami M. Magam, Konstantinos Tsamoutsoglou
abstract: This study presents a wet-dry seasonal comparison of hopanes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) as molecular markers for the forensic tracing of petroleum pollution in the sediments of the Selangor River, Malaysia. Sediment samples were collected from 13 stations during wet and dry seasons to determine concentrations, sources, and distribution patterns. Hopane concentrations exhibited variation between wet and dry seasons, ranging from 208 to 1492 ng g⁻¹ in the wet season and from 145 to 1737 ng g⁻¹ in the dry season. Complementarily, total PAHs (Ʃ25PAHs) ranged from 215 to 964 ng g⁻¹ (wet) and 203–665 ng g⁻¹ (dry), with notably higher loads observed during the wet season. Diagnostic ratio analysis for hopanes identified Middle East crude oil (MECO) and used crankcase oil as the predominant sources. In contrast, PAH isomeric ratios indicated a dominant contribution from pyrogenic sources (combustion of fossil fuels and biomass), alongside petrogenic inputs. This divergence reveals the river's mixed pollution from direct petroleum and combustion sources. Grain size analysis revealed sediments were predominantly sandy, and total organic carbon (TOC) showed no significant correlation with hopane or PAH concentrations, indicating distribution is governed by chronic anthropogenic input and hydrodynamic seasonal forcing rather than sedimentological processes. Ecological risk assessment using sediment quality guidelines (ERL, ERM, TEL, PEL), toxic equivalent concentrations (TEQ: 15.3–89.7 ng TEQ g⁻¹), and mean ERM quotients (M-ERM-Q: 0.016–0.045) indicated low probability of adverse biological effects. The results provide critical baseline data and demonstrate that single-timepoint assessments underestimate pollution dynamics. This study underscores the necessity of continuous monitoring and provides actionable insights for targeted mitigation strategies, establishing a combined hopane-PAH fingerprint as an essential tool for forensic tracking in tropical riverine environments.

title: Integrated post-closure safety assessment of radioactive waste containing hazardous chemicals: A screening framework for radiological–chemical risk
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): In Gyu Chang, Ji Su Kang, Jae Hak Cheong
abstract: Disposal of radioactive waste containing hazardous chemicals can generate post-closure radiological cancer risks, chemical cancer risks, and chemical non-cancer hazards. Existing assessments often treat radiological and chemical endpoints separately. This study develops an integrated post-closure assessment and screening framework that combines United States Environmental Protection Agency risk methods with AMBER dynamic compartment modeling, using the International Atomic Energy Agency Trench Case as a reference disposal system. A normalized generic assessment of selected metallic elements was used to compare radiological and chemical risk behavior and derive two endpoint-specific screening metrics: a critical radioactivity concentration for identifying when chemical cancer risk is small relative to radiological cancer risk, and a preliminary non-cancer trigger based on maximum leachate concentration relative to the drinking-water standard. A case-study application using documented mixed-waste inventory data from nuclear facilities evaluated complex waste types with associated radionuclides under normal-evolution and human-intrusion scenarios. Several cases triggered total cancer risk screening criteria under human intrusion, indicating the need for detailed assessment. The results are reference-scenario screening outcomes, not site-specific predictions. The framework supports prioritization of radioactive mixed waste for constituent-specific, pathway-specific, and site-specific assessment. This structure links time-dependent transport outputs with endpoint-specific decisions for waste management and regulation.

title: Mineral-contaminant interactions in the presence of polystyrene microplastics: Implications for contaminant adsorption in aqueous environments
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Abhishek Mandal, Arpan Sarkar, Jay Karmakar, Sangeetha Thykandi, Gopala Krishna Darbha
abstract: Microplastics (MPs), particularly polystyrene microplastics (PSMPs), are emerging contaminants of global concern that can alter contaminant dynamics in aquatic systems. This study investigates how Polystyrene MPs influence the adsorption behaviour of three representative environmental contaminants-Cd(II), Cr(VI), and tetracycline (TC) onto natural clay and mineral substrates (goethite, kaolin, and bentonite). Batch adsorption experiments showed that all three minerals effectively adsorb these contaminants. However, the presence of PSMPs reduced their overall adsorption capacities by ∼13–45% for Cd(II), ∼7–11% for Cr(VI), and ∼9–12% for TC, depending on the mineral system. Kinetic modelings revealed distinct behaviours between pollutant classes. The adsorption of Cd(II) and Cr(VI) followed a mixed kinetic control governed by both surface reaction and intraparticle diffusion. In contrast, tetracycline uptake was best described by a revised pseudo-second-order mechanism sensitive to both solute and surface site availability. Markedly, the addition of PSMPs altered apparent adsorption rates in a highly system-specific manner, inducing, either suppression or minimal variation through a complex interplay between steric hindrance arising from site masking and a concurrent transition toward rapidly forming outer-sphere complexes. The XPS analyses suggested that, while contaminant binding in MP-free systems involved a greater contribution from inner-sphere complexation, PSMP-amended systems exhibited an increased contribution from weaker outer-sphere interactions. Although PSMP-only controls showed negligible direct contaminant uptake under the tested conditions, the presence of PSMPs altered mineral surface reactivity and aggregate structure, thereby reducing mineral-mediated contaminant retention. These findings demonstrate that PSMPs can modify contaminant partitioning and mobility in aquatic environments and highlight the importance of incorporating MP-mineral interactions into contaminant transport and environmental risk assessment frameworks.

title: Low-dose triclosan induces neurotoxicity in zebrafish via gut microbiota disruption
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xiangguang Chen, Xiaoli Zhao, Junyue Zheng, Jiazhen Jiang, Fengchang Wu
abstract: Triclosan (TCS), a broad-spectrum antibacterial agent, is widely detected in environmental and human samples, yet its neurotoxic risks and mechanisms following long-term environmental exposure remain unclear—particularly the role of gut microbiota. Using germ-free zebrafish and fecal microbiota transplantation, we established a causal link between TCS-induced gut dysbiosis and neurotoxicity. Integrating transcriptomics, 16S rRNA sequencing, and gut-derived metabolite transplantation, we elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms. Three-month exposure to environmentally relevant TCS concentrations significantly enriched gut Proteobacteria, increasing lipopolysaccharide (LPS) levels. LPS subsequently crossed the damaged blood–brain barrier via the gut–brain axis, triggering neuroinflammation and behavioral abnormalities in female zebrafish. Notably, TCS exhibited dose-dependent neurotoxicity: low doses (0.4 and 4.0 μg/L) acted primarily through gut microbiota disruption, while high-dose (40 μg/L) effects involved both microbiota-dependent and independent pathways. This study provides new insights into the neurotoxic mechanisms of TCS and highlights the critical role of gut microbiota in mediating its effects. However, this study was conducted exclusively in female zebrafish, and further investigations in males are warranted to assess potential sex differences.

title: Rhizospheric phosphorus activation drives microbial degradation of tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Longfei Jiang, Jiali Xu, Jibing Li, Chunling Luo, Yuhong Wang
abstract: Organophosphate esters (OPEs), such as tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate (TCEP), undergo accelerated microbial degradation in the rhizosphere, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Given their structural similarity to natural organophosphorus compounds, we hypothesized that rhizospheric phosphorus cycling contributes to OPE degradation. Using DNA-stable isotope probing, we identified active TCEP degraders and linked them to soil phosphate fractions. Plant cultivation reshaped degrader communities, increasing their relative abundance by 80.7% and predicted functional gene content by 20.8%, while reducing interactions between degraders and non-degraders. Rhizospheric TCEP degraders exhibited a lower average phylogenetic distance than those in non-rhizosphere soils (0.58 vs. 0.64). This contrasts with the greater phylogenetic breadth observed for rhizospheric PAH and PCB degraders. The reduced phylogenetic breadth suggests that TCEP degradation may be more functionally conserved and dominated by specialized taxa, potentially reflecting phosphatase-mediated processes rather than cooperative, multi-taxon degradation networks. TCEP degradation correlated negatively with total phosphorus but positively with bioavailable phosphorus, indicating a key role of plant-mediated phosphorus solubilization in regulating degrader composition and activity. Increased alkaline phosphatase activity further supported this interpretation. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism by which rhizospheric nutrient cycling regulates TCEP degradation, advancing our understanding of phosphorus-microbe interactions in pollutant biotransformation within plant-soil systems. Synopsis Plant-mediated phosphorus cycling in the rhizosphere selectively enriches TCEP-degrading microbes, uncovering a novel link between nutrient availability and pollutant biotransformation in soil ecosystems.

title: Weathering chemistry shapes the gut microbiome–metabolome–transcriptome response of adult zebrafish to aged polyethylene microplastics
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Carl Angelo Medriano, Kin Wei Chow, Jae Young Oh, Sungwoo Bae
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in aquatic environments undergo continuous weathering, yet most toxicological studies still rely on pristine commercial particles, leaving biological consequences of distinct aging chemistries poorly resolved. Here, polyethylene (PE) MPs were aged through oxidative and hydrolytic pathways (UV+H₂O, H₂SO₄, HNO₃, and NaOH), characterized by FTIR (Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy) and SEM (Scanning Electron Microscopy), and administered to zebrafish to link surface chemistry with the multilayered gut microbiome, metabolome, and host transcriptome responses. Weathering chemistry governed surface oxidation and morphological damage, with strong-acid treatment (H₂SO₄ ≫ HNO₃) causing the most severe fragmentation. These surface differences propagated into chemistry-specific effects: an abundance-driven restructuring of the gut microbiota, including suppression of the core commensal Cetobacterium under alkaline aging and expansion of stress-tolerant environmental taxa; weathering-specific remodeling of the metabolome (NAD⁺/nicotinamide and glycosphingolipid); and low but treatment-specific transcriptional changes (6–13 DEGs per treatment, including a shared ∼800-fold induction of lhfpl5b under NaOH and UV+H₂O). Multi-omics integration resolved into three chemistry-specific cross-omics axes, with the metabolome and transcriptome showing the strongest cross-layer concordance (Procrustes 1-M2 = 0.38, p < 0.01). Weathered MPs from different degradation pathways cannot be aggregated into a single "aged-MP" category, as their hazards are chemistry-specific at every molecular layer.

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomic profiling reveals cell type–specific responses of the soybean root tip to aluminum stress
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Qiuping Liu, Shuwei Wang, Ruiyuan Yan, Kedong Xu, Yi Zhang, Yunmin Wei
abstract: Aluminum (Al) toxicity resulting from soil acidification poses a major constraint on crop productivity. Although the root apex serves as the primary site for Al perception and adaptive remodeling, cell type–resolved responses to prolonged Al exposure remain poorly characterized. Here, we employed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to generate a cell type–resolved transcriptomic atlas of the soybean (Glycine max) root tip under Al stress. We profiled a total of 79,201 high-quality nuclei and identified nine major root cell types. Our results reveal that Al stress elicits shared transcriptional responses across cell types while reshaping root cell type composition. Notably, the proportion of nuclei increased in the epidermal cell layer (from 34.16% to 70.41%). In contrast, a significant reduction in nuclear number was detected within the cortical cells (from 40.70% to 8.53%). Interestingly, microscopic examination further indicated a pronounced expansion of regions exhibiting patterns inconsistent with the decrease in cortical nuclei. Cell type–specific analyses identified a total of 20,544 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and showed that epidermal cells primarily responded to Al stress by activating transcriptional programs associated with transport, cell wall reinforcement, and defense, accompanied by enhanced fatty acid biosynthesis and cuticle–related pathways. In contrast, cortical cells exhibited repression of cell cycle–related transcriptional programs, consistent with their reduced cell abundance and indicating that limitations in cell division are closely associated with cortical cell loss. Furthermore, untargeted metabolomic profiling supported an important role of lipid metabolism in the response to Al stress. Collectively, our study reveals cell type–specific response patterns of the soybean root tip to long-term Al stress at single-nucleus resolution and provides new insights into the cellular mechanisms underlying aluminum tolerance in crop roots.

title: Crystallographic phase engineering of MnO 2 for efficient peracetic acid activation: Unraveling the critical role of surface manganese oxidation state
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Si Sun, Shurun Yang, Ruoxin Li, Chuan-Shu He, Bo Lai
abstract: This study systematically investigates the influence of MnO2 crystallographic phase on the activation efficiency of peracetic acid (PAA). Firstly, α-, β-, γ-, and δ-MnO2 were synthesized through tailored methods. The oxidative activity of these catalysts was evaluated based on the degradation kinetics of naproxen (NAP), revealing the following catalytic activity order: α-MnO2 > δ-MnO2 > γ-MnO2 > β-MnO2. Further analysis revealed that NAP oxidation in the different crystallographic phases MnO2/PAA process mainly depends on RO• and 1O2. Comprehensive characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to elucidate the surface chemistry, intrinsic redox properties, structural stability, crystal features, and Mn-O bonding interactions. The results demonstrated an inverse correlation between the average oxidation state of surface manganese sites and the activation efficiency of PAA, thereby elucidating the fundamental origin of the high activity observed in specific crystalline phases of MnO2. The surface-localized chemical environment, rather than bulk characteristics, serves as the dominant factor governing the catalytic performance. Surfaces featuring lower average oxidation states exhibit enhanced reducibility of manganese species, which facilitates more rapid initiation of the catalytic reaction. These insights offer valuable guidance for the rational design of efficient and cost-effective MnO2-based catalysts for advanced water treatment applications.

title: Fluorine mass balance, precursor transformability, and screening-level inhalation prioritization of PFAS-containing firefighting foam concentrates
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Jeonghoon Park, Myoungho Lee, Soobin Choi, Taeyeon Kim, Seungwoon Sohn, Kyung-Duk Zoh
abstract: Ten PFAS-containing firefighting foam concentrates from South Korea were characterized by LC–MS/MS target analysis, IMS–HRMS suspect screening with CCS-supported confidence assignment, the total oxidizable precursor (TOP) assay, total organofluorine (TOF) analysis, and screening-level inhalation prioritization. PFOS and PFOA were not detected, whereas C6 fluorotelomer-derived PFAS dominated all eight AFFF-related products. 6:2 FTAB accounted for 97.5–98.6% of quantified PFAS in five products and 6:2 FTS for 92.3–96.3% in the remaining three. Suspect screening identified 16 PFAS classes, including four candidate classes previously unreported in firefighting foams. TOP results indicated unknown oxidizable PFCA precursor pools. Apparent target-plus-suspect fluorine recovery averaged 45 ± 52% across all ten products, including LOQ-bound estimates for two SS products without directly quantifiable TOF, indicating unresolved organofluorine. Under a conservative indoor scenario without self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) protection, the toxicity reference value (TRV)-normalized hazard index (HI) was dominated by 6:2 FTS and reached 18.1 for H-AFFF at 450 L/min. Although 6:2 FTAB had the largest target-PFAS burden, it was excluded from the main HI because only an exploratory 28-day oral provisional TRV was available; therefore, the HI should be interpreted as a screening-level prioritization metric rather than a definitive inhalation risk estimate.

title: Photodegradation of Naproxen augment the photosensitization and phototoxicity with attenuated COX-2 binding under ambient UVA and UVB exposure
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Madhu Bala, Mohd Danish Kamar, Joel Saji, Tanmayee Basu, Atul Kumar Upadhyay, Garima Sagar, Ashish Dwivedi, Ratan Singh Ray
abstract: Naproxen (NPX) is a widely prescribed non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with analgesic, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory effects. Owing to its structure, NPX is susceptible to photodegradation, a factor of particular concern for topical formulations where exposure to solar UV radiation is inevitable. In this study, we systematically investigated the photodegradation and phototoxic potential of NPX under environmentally relevant UVA and UVB irradiation. NPX underwent faster photodegradation under UVA than UVB. UHPLC and LC-QToF-MS/MS identified two major photoproducts, P1 (1-(6-methoxynaphthalen-2-yl)ethanol) and P2 (2-acetyl-6-methoxynaphthalene), with P1 comprising approximately 90% of the photoproduct profile in both UVA and UVB. Spectroscopic analyses using FTIR and Raman spectroscopy revealed characteristic structural alterations, while LC-QToF-MS, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and 2D NMR elucidated the photodegradation pathway, dominated by side-chain cleavage and decarboxylation reactions. Computational studies, including molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations with the COX-2 enzyme, indicated diminished binding efficacy of NPX photoproducts. Further, we checked the COX-2 inhibitory activity, with PGE₂ abundance increasing by 15.6% and 37.4% with degraded NPX (Deg-NPX) relative to NPX at 10 and 50 µg/mL, respectively. Cytotoxicity assays in HaCaT cells demonstrated that NPX is phototoxic but Deg-NPX is both cytotoxic and phototoxic and also induced greater intracellular ROS accumulation, membrane damage, apoptosis, and dsDNA breaks. Collectively, these results highlight that NPX photodegradation generates photoproducts with greater basal cytotoxicity and enhanced phototoxicity and diminished pharmacological activity. The study provides mechanistic insights into their role in cutaneous adverse effects and highlights the importance of evaluating phototoxic risks in the clinical management of NSAID-based topical therapies.

title: Machine learning-driven high-throughput prediction of Hg 0 capture in MOFs and decipherment of structure-property relationships
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zhen Zhang, Li Jia, Peng Cheng, Ya–wen Wu, Zi–kuo Li, Zong–bao Li, Chu–hao Fan, Yue Yu
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show potential for Hg0 adsorption via tunable pore structures and chemical functionalities. However, efficient screening of MOF adsorbents remains challenging due to vast material space and unclear structure-property relationships. Herein, a Hg0 adsorption database of 6528 MOF samples was established, and machine learning models were developed for predicting adsorption performance. Among tested models, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) exhibited the best prediction on the independent test set, achieving a coefficient of determination (R 2) of 0.893. SHAP analysis revealed that energy descriptors, including logarithmic Henry coefficient (log(K H)) and adsorption enthalpy (ΔH ads), dominated Hg0 adsorption, while structural descriptors further regulated adsorption behavior. Combined model interpretation revealed a condition-dependent interaction between adsorption affinity and pore characteristics. High-throughput screening revealed characteristic descriptor intervals for high-performing MOFs, including log(K H)=−3.62 to −2.61, ΔH ads = −34.60 to −25.21 kJ·mol−1, and VF = 0.67–0.78. MOFid-based structural analysis identified significant enrichment of Cr, Fe, Co nodes and nbo topology, alongside preferred acs and tbo topologies, as well as nitrogen-containing aromatic conjugated heterocyclic ligands in high-performing MOFs. These findings clarify the roles of metal nodes, topology, and ligand chemistry in Hg0 adsorption and provide a machine learning-driven strategy for rational design of MOF-based mercury removal adsorbents.

title: Urine metabolomics analysis of construction painters with complex chemical exposures
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Chani Sahabandu Hewa Sahabanduge, Pengyuan Liu, Kushal Biswas, Paridhiben Patel, Anila Bello, Dhimiter Bello
abstract: Construction painters involved in metal structure coating experience complex chemical exposures, including epoxy resins, amine cross-linkers, isocyanates, organic solvents and flame retardants. These exposures induce oxidative stress and downstream metabolic perturbations, yet integrative metabolomic evidence in this workforce remains scarce. This study aimed to characterize urinary metabolomic alterations associated with distinct construction-related exposure scenarios including painting workers applying epoxy-based mid-coat and isocyanate-based top-coat. Untargeted urinary metabolomics was performed using liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) in pre- and post-shift samples collected from professional construction painting workers. Daily exposure effects were assessed using pre- versus post-shift urinary metabolomic comparisons, while exposure biomarker-associated metabolomic alterations were evaluated using tertile exposure stratification based on established urinary exposure biomarkers. The association of metabolic responses related to heat stress/dehydration was assessed using urinary specific gravity values. Statistical analyses included Student’s t-testing, pathway enrichment analysis, and correlation analysis. Solvent-related metabolites, including hippuric and methylhippuric acids, were markedly elevated among coating workers. Both exposure groups showed significant alteration of amino acid metabolism and glutathione metabolism. In addition, mid-coat workers showed exposure effects on vitamin B6 metabolism, riboflavin metabolism, and catecholamine biosynthesis specifically. Top-coat workers demonstrated the exposure effects of nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism. These findings demonstrate that distinct coating-related exposures mixtures could yield unique metabolic signatures, despite complex mixtures exposures with overlapping chemical signatures.

title: Cometabolic and nutrient-driven defluorination and transformation of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances by metabolically versatile bacteria
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Jinha Kim, Jiaju Fu, Jennifer A. Field, Kung-Hui Chu
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are emerging contaminants of great concern. Yet, current knowledge of PFAS-degrading microorganisms is limited. Here, we report novel bacterial strains, Cupriavidus sp. CuC1, Pseudomonas sp. PsB, and Variovorax sp. VaC1, capable of defluorinating diverse C1-C6 fluorinated PFAS and using nitrogen (N)- and sulfur (S)-containing PFAS as nutrients. These bacteria exhibited broad metabolic versatility toward various sugar, carboxylates, alcohols, alkanes, aromatic, hydrocarbon surfactants, and organic solvents. In particular, 1-butanol (BuOH)-grown CuC1 effectively defluorinated C1-C6 fluorinated PFAS. Strain PsB significantly removed 6:2 fluorotelomer sulfonamidoalkyl betaine (FtSaB) and N-ethyl perfluorooctane sulfonamide as sole N-sources. All three strains removed 6:2 fluorotelomer sulfonate (FtS) as a sole S-source and accumulated various PFAS (suspect) metabolites when grown from selective carbon source types. Strains CuC1 (ethylene glycol-, BuOH-, or octanoate-grown) and VaC1 (glucose-grown) achieved > 95% 6:2 FtS removal. Strain VaC1 uniquely accumulated a novel metabolite, α-OH 6:2 FtS, that corresponded with higher accumulation of 6:2 fluorotelomer unsaturated carboxylic acid. Furthermore, CuC1 demonstrated 6:2 FtS removal when grown on sodium octyl sulfate under S-rich conditions and showed potential removal in 6:2 FtSaB and undecafluoro-2-methyl-3-oxahexanoic acid (commercial name GenX) under S-limited conditions. These findings significantly expand the portfolio of PFAS degraders and provide new mechanistic insights into nutrient-driven PFAS biotransformation.

title: Overlooked Pb–(Sn)–(Sb)–(As) oxide particles in incineration bottom ash: Particle-scale occurrence, alteration and potential relevance to antimony and arsenic mobility
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Quentin Wehrung, Ginevra Mango, Giulia Pia Servetto, Davide Bernasconi, Nadia Curetti, Enrico Destefanis, Caterina Caviglia, Andrea Pani, Florian Audoye, Fabien Michel, Ruggero Vigliaturo, Alessandro Pavese, Linda Pastero
abstract: Antimony (Sb) is a critical metal and an emerging hazardous pollutant, chemically akin to arsenic (As), and is widely used as antimonial lead in Pb–(Sn)–Sb–(As) alloys. A substantial fraction of the Sb fed to municipal solid waste (MSW) incinerators remains in incineration bottom ash (IBA), where Sb leaching, together with that of As, restricts IBA reuse. We document, at the particle scale, the occurrence of Pb–(Sn)–(Sb)–(As) oxide particles in the 0.25–2 mm fractions of IBA from several facilities in France. Seven particles were characterized in detail by optical microscopy, SEM–BSE–XEDS, PXRD, and S/TEM–XEDS with dual-range EELS. The particles span a continuum of apparent alteration states, from Pb–(Sn)–(Sb) metallic cores with incipient oxide crusts to hollow, fully oxidized, brittle polycrystalline shells with distinctive yellow to brown-reddish colours. EELS features are consistent with Sb(III) and higher Sb oxidation states and XEDS phase maps show that As is concentrated together with Sb in Ca-bearing Pb–Sb–As oxide domains of the alteration rims. The assemblages constitute an overlooked, dense host of Sb and As in IBA that complement the calcium-antimonate framework; Because these particles are much denser than the silicate-carbonate ash matrix, density-based separation of IBA fines is a natural candidate for their removal.

title: Nitrogen cycling regulates arsenic mobilization in alluvial-lacustrine aquifer systems: DOM molecular signatures and thermodynamic constraints
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Qingfeng Chen, Yijun Yang, Chenhao Dong, Qixiang Wang, Shiyao Liu, Yao Du, Huaming Guo, Yanxin Wang
abstract: High arsenic (As) groundwater commonly co-occurs with elevated ammonium (NH4 +) in aquifers worldwide. However, the underlying nitrogen cycling processes regulating As mobilization in groundwater remain elusive. Here, hydrochemistry, stable isotopes, FT-ICR MS, and thermodynamic modelling were integrated to investigate the NH4 + production pathways and their impacts on As mobility within the alluvial-lacustrine aquifer. Hydrochemical and isotopic data indicated that groundwater NH4 + was primarily produced through OM mineralization and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), and both processes contributed to As enrichment which reached up to 1603 μg/L. FT-ICR MS analysis revealed that OM mineralization depleted CHON2 and highly unsaturated compounds, while DNRA preferentially consumed labile aliphatic compounds. Thermodynamic potential factors (FT) further evidenced that OM mineralization faced thermodynamic constraints (0.26 0.97). Notably, thermodynamically favorable organic compounds such as highly unsaturated compounds and N-containing OM could promote OM mineralization, during which NH4 + is produced and the reductive dissolution of Fe(III) oxides is simultaneously facilitated, thereby releasing As into groundwater. These findings could provide novel insights into the role of coupled C-N-Fe cycling in As mobilization within alluvial-lacustrine aquifer systems.

title: MOF-on-MOF-derived Co 3 O 4 @ZnO@Hemin peroxidase-like nanozyme for ultrasensitive detection of organophosphorus pesticides in vegetables and lake water
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zhaoyun Ma, Siran Du, Ben Dong, Qingwei Wang, Zhenmin Xu, Yong Chen, Xiqing Cheng, Qin Kuang
abstract: To address threats of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) residues to food safety and environmental health, this study developed a core-shell-shell nanozyme (Co3O4@ZnO@Hemin) for sensitive OPs detection in multiple real samples. The nanozyme integrates nanocatalyst electronic effects with biomimetic hydrophobic microenvironment functionality, fabricated by pyrolyzing a ZIF-67@ZIF-8 metal-organic framework (MOF)-on-MOF precursor, followed by Hemin loading. Remarkably, this nanozyme exhibits specific peroxidase-like activity, attributed to the mesoporous Co3O4@ZnO structure that promotes electron transfer and provides bimetallic mixed-valence active sites. Meanwhile, Hemin incorporation further increases oxygen vacancies through electronic regulation and enhances hydrophobicity, synergistically boosting catalytic performance. Therefore, this nanozyme sensor platform achieved ultrasensitive acetylcholinesterase (AChE) detection with a detection limit (LOD) of 0.07 mU mL⁻¹ and quantitative trichlorfon detection (1–5 ng·mL−1, LOD 0.10 ng·mL−1), successfully applied to detect trichlorfon in lettuce, cucumber, bok choy, and lake water, with 90.21–105.91% recoveries and RSDs below 4.62%. This study provides a bioinspired nanozyme strategy for sensing.

title: A multi‑target adverse outcome pathway network for sub-chronic ketamine‑induced cognitive impairment in adult zebrafish
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Binjie Wang, Haoying Zhang, Yihui Zhao, Tongyao Gao, Ruonan Zheng, Song Chian, Jiye Wang, Fang Wei
abstract: Ketamine (KET), an emerging contaminant, is increasingly detected in aquatic environments, yet its sub-chronic neurocognitive effects at environmentally relevant concentrations remain largely unknown. We exposed adult zebrafish to KET for 40 days and integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, behavioral assays, and molecular simulations to investigate these effects. Sub-chronic KET exposure impaired spatial learning and memory at 0.4 μg/L, while anxiety‑like and social behavior were altered only at 40 μg/L. Intersecting transcriptomics with network toxicology yielded 9 candidate genes and 15 shared KEGG pathways, which were mainly associated with neurocognitive function. SHAP prioritized hmox1, camkk2, and trem2 and molecular simulations predicted stable binding of KET to these proteins, supporting their role as candidate molecular initiating events. Gene expression changes correlated with altered glutamate, and GABA levels. Based on these multi‑level findings, we constructed a proposed adverse outcome pathway (AOP) network in which KET is predicted to bind to HMOX1, CAMKK2, and TREM2, which may contribute to oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and synaptic dysfunction converging on cognitive decline. This study provides evidence in adult zebrafish that sub-chronic exposure to environmentally relevant KET impairs cognition and proposes a multi‑target AOP network based on zebrafish data, supporting ecological risk assessment of KET as an emerging contaminant.

title: Reaction kinetics and mass transfer synergistically enhanced the electrochemical oxidation performance of porous SiC/Ta/BDD electrodes in a flow-through reactor
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xiang Wang, Jinjie Dou, Zejun Deng, Kechao Zhou, Qiuping Wei, Li Ma
abstract: Integrating superior interfacial kinetics with enhanced mass transfer is crucial for advancing electrochemical advanced oxidation processes. However, porous boron-doped diamond (BDD) electrodes often suffer from high inherent interfacial resistance on ceramic substrates continuously. Herein, we report a highly efficient flow-through oxidation system utilizing a novel 3D porous p-SiC/Ta/BDD electrode. By introducing a sputtered Ta conductive interlayer, the charge transfer barrier is significantly diminished, yielding an enlarged electrochemically active area and accelerated ·OH generation kinetics. To fully harness this intrinsic kinetic gain, a flow-through reactor configuration was utilized. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) confirms that the directed flow structurally induces a > 3-fold increase in turbulent kinetic energy and vorticity within the porous framework, activating previously dormant deep catalytic sites and boosting the ·OH-pollutant collision probability. Benefiting from this kinetics-mass transfer synergy, the flow-through p-SiC/Ta/BDD system delivers a 98.7% rapid removal of metronidazole. Impressively, it exhibits a reaction rate constant of 0.074 min−1, 2.24 times that of traditional p-SiC/BDD batch systems, at an ultra-low energy consumption of 1.59 kWh m−3 order−1. Furthermore, the electrode demonstrates remarkable universal applicability toward multi-class organic pollutants (tetracycline, acid orange G), outstanding chemical resistance against complex inorganic anions, and long-term durability. This work provides an innovative interfacial engineering and hydrodynamic integration strategy for sustainable refractory wastewater treatment.

title: Viral regulation of N 2 O emissions depends on soil acidity
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hailin Zhang, Rui Yan, Jiao Wang, Linfa Fang, Xinrong Huang, Teng Wen, Yiyue Zhang, Longfei Yu, Kai Yang, Yuting Zhang, Zhenwu Tang, Prakash Lakshmanan, Jinbo Zhang, Baozhan Wang, Yunpeng Qiu, Xinping Chen, Xiaojun Shi, Xiaoxuan Su
abstract: Acidification generally enhances N2O emissions from soils. Yet, the adaptive responses of denitrifiers and the regulatory roles of soil viruses in denitrifier-mediated N2O emissions under persistent acidity remain poorly understood. Here, we combined D2O-labeled single-cell Raman spectroscopy, 15N tracing, metagenomics, machine learning, and virus-addition experiments to examine virus-denitrifier interactions across soils with contrasting long-term acidity conditions maintained for > 17 years. Acidic soils showed the highest N2O emissions despite the lowest potential denitrification rate and highest microbial anabolic activity. Denitrifiers and viral populations in acidic soils exhibited reduced microdiversity, stronger purifying selection, and distinct functional specialization, while viruses showed a lower virulent-to-temperate ratio and greater genetic potential for host interaction and persistence. Host antiviral defense capacity was the strongest genomic predictor of abundance responses to active virus. In acidic soils, active viruses increased N2O reductase level by 33.2% without altering nosZ abundance and reduced N2O accumulation by up to 62.5%, indicating an efficiency-optimized response. Neutral soils showed a quantity-driven response, whereas alkaline soils showed no significant reduction in N2O accumulation. These findings reveal acidity-dependent viral regulation of N2O emissions, strongest in long-term acidic soils.

title: Enhanced phytoremediation of Cd- phenanthrene co-contaminated soil through the combined application of electric field and chemical additives
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Lizhu Yuan, Xinzhuo Qian, Weijin Zheng, Xu Chen, Boxi Lv, Xuemei Zhong, Jonathan W.C. Wong
abstract: Electric fields and chemical additives can enhance phytoremediation, but their synergistic mechanisms in cadmium (Cd)–phenanthrene (PHE) co-contaminated soils remain unclear. Here, a greenhouse pot experiment was conducted to investigate the combined effects of a direct‑current electric field and chemical additives (citric acid + ammonium nitrate) on the phytoremediation of Cd-PHE co‑contaminated soil using marigold (Tagetes patula L.). The combined treatment (Phy‑CN‑EK) achieved the highest PHE removal (82.3%) and total shoot Cd uptake (41.443 μg pot−1), and simultaneously increased the relative abundance of potential PHE-degrading functional bacteria such as Pseudomonas and Saccharimonadaceae. The results suggested that the chemical additives accelerated the initial oxidative degradation of PHE, while the electric field subsequently promoted the complete mineralization of its intermediates. For Cd uptake, the chemical additives directly enhanced phytoextraction but indirectly suppressed it via a shift toward Pseudomonas dominance; conversely, the electric field promoted Cd uptake by enhancing plant biomass and facilitating intermediate mineralization, thereby counteracting the microbial-driven suppression. Their integration achieved synergistic enhancement of both PHE degradation and Cd phytoextraction. These findings deepen the understanding of the combined enhancement mechanisms in phytoremediation of Cd-PAH co-contaminated soils and provide a mechanistic basis for future field-scale validation and optimization.

title: Spatiotemporally adaptive optimization of groundwater remediation: Well-network system design and multi-stage operation
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yiran Chen, Yaqiang Wei, Xinde Cao, Zi Zhan, Jialun Xie, Haobo Niu, Jian Chen, Hui Li
abstract: Groundwater remediation under stringent resource and time constraints requires coordinated decisions on where extraction infrastructure is deployed and how pumping is operated over time. Conventional pump-and-treat optimization often addresses strategic well-network design and dynamic pumping operation separately, limiting the coordinated use of evolving hydraulic and concentration fields in heterogeneous aquifers. Here, we developed an optimization framework incorporating mixed-variable well-network design and multi-stage pumping optimization under concentration and hydraulic-head constraints. Mixed-variable NSGA-II identifies Pareto-optimal combinations of well number, location, pumping rate and remediation duration, after which the selected solution is refined by reallocating pumping between stages according to simulated plume evolution. The framework was evaluated using two-dimensional and three-dimensional heterogeneous aquifer models and applied to a chromium-contaminated field site initialized from monitoring data. In the three-dimensional case, multi-stage operation reduced estimated pumping energy cost by 35.3% relative to the selected single-stage solution. At the field site, multi-objective optimization reduced cumulative pumping by 27.3% using existing wells, and multi-stage operation achieved a further 2.8% reduction while maintaining modeled contaminant mass removal within 1.6% of the single-stage solution. This work shifts groundwater management from experience-led heuristic designs toward model-driven, precision decision-making, providing a resource-efficient approach for pump-and-treat remediation of groundwater contamination.

title: Substrate-dependent attenuation of antibiotic and metal resistance genes during acidogenic fermentation of titanium-flocculated sludge
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Beibei Liu, Jinming Du, Na Pan, Chunyi Sun, Weiying Xu, Liangguo Yan, Tao Yan, Xuguang Li, Yu Du, Qinghui Zuo, Yanxia Zhao, Baoyu Gao
abstract: Titanium-based coagulation enables efficient wastewater purification and sludge recovery, yet the fate of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and metal resistance genes (MRGs) during downstream sludge valorization remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated how food waste-derived substrates affected fermentation performance and ARGs/MRGs profiles during 7-day acidogenic co-fermentation of Ti-flocculated sludge. Substrate composition resulted in distinct fermentation characteristics and resistome responses. Compared with refractory fiber-rich substrates, readily hydrolysable starch promoted organic solubilization and acidogenesis, producing the highest soluble chemical oxygen demand and volatile fatty acid (VFA) concentrations. These fermentation characteristics were accompanied by the enrichment of polysaccharide-degrading and VFA-producing microorganisms, together with an increased representation of genes associated with glycolysis and carbohydrate-active enzymes. Concurrently, the relative abundance of mobile genetic element-associated genes decreased, accompanied by a reduction in total ARG abundance after fermentation. Protein-rich substrates showed distinct microbial and functional profiles, with higher relative representation of genes associated with proteolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and VFA-related metabolism. This treatment also markedly decreased the relative abundance of transposase-related genes, suggesting reduced mobility-associated potential of resistance genes. This study lays the foundation for evaluating resistance gene dynamics during co-fermentation of Ti-flocculated sludge.

title: Mechanisms of biochar derived from chicken manure or rice straw that effectively immobilizes cadmium do not apply to sewage-sludge biochar
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Fei Huang, Kai-Ming Liang, Jun-Chun Li, Zhi-Wen Hu, Long-Yong Lin, Yi-Rong Deng
abstract: In order to explore immobilization characteristic and its possible mechanism of various feedstocks-based biochars, deriving from chicken manure (CMB), rice straw (RSB) and sewage sludge (SSB), the effect of three biochars on speciation transformation of Cd in soil was compared, and soil properties, microbial community diversity were also examined. The treatment of CMB and RSB reduced significantly the content of acid-extractable Cd by 53.62% and 41.18%, respectively, but this available fraction was increased by 23.44% after SSB treatment.
