title: Synergistic effects of interdecadal oscillations in dual ocean basins trigger pronounced annual runoff variability in cell-based reconstructions during the late 20th century, and the impact of runoff changes on the ecological and agro-pastoral
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Ziyue Zhang, Long Ma, Bolin Sun, Jiamei Yuan, Xing Huang, Tingxi Liu, Qiang Zhang, Shengxiang Mao, Haimei Tian, Shuo Zhang
abstract: Study region For this study, the Taoer River basin located in mid-high latitude cold mountainous area was selected as the research object. Long-term runoff evolution of this watershed exerts profound impacts on regional ecological security and agro-pastoral economic development. Unraveling centennial runoff patterns and drivers is critical for cold-region water governance. Study focus This study innovatively reconstructs annual runoff using birch xylem cell wall thickness chronology for the first time in the mid-high latitude cold zone. We systematically disentangle runoff driving forces from three dimensions: external radiative forcing, ocean boundary signals, and cross dual-ocean basin ocean-atmosphere coupling oscillations, and further quantify the ecological and economic consequences of historical runoff fluctuations. The outcomes provide scientific support for water resource allocation, extreme hydrological risk early warning, and coordinated eco-agricultural sustainable development in analogous cold basins. New hydrological insights for the region Synergistic oscillations of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) and Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO) dominate amplified late-20th-century runoff variability in the Taoer Basin, the core innovation corresponding to this paper’s title. Our 328-year reconstruction identifies the 1843–1872 dry phase and two wet periods (1936–1961), with short-term runoff governed by ENSO (El Niño–Southern Oscillation). Runoff correlates negatively with solar radiation and positively with northwest Pacific SST. Snow-permafrost melt creates pre-2000 positive temperature-runoff linkage, reversed by modern evapotranspiration. Extreme wet runoff sharply cuts crop output but barely hurts livestock production.

title: Satellite-derived turbidity dynamics reveal sediment regulation by the Three Gorges Dam and large river-connected lakes in the Yangtze River
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Rui Deng, Fang Liu, Tianci Zhu, Yibo Li, Xiaosong Lin, Weiliang Pan
abstract: Study Region The Yangtze River is a large regulated river system with pronounced variations in hydrology, sediment transport, and river–lake interactions. This study focuses on the mainstem from Yibin to Shanghai, particularly reaches influenced by the Three Gorges Dam (TGD), Dongting Lake, and Poyang Lake. Study Focus An integrated satellite-driven framework was developed to reconstruct turbidity dynamics during 2016–2024. Landsat-8/9 imagery was combined with ensemble machine learning, causal inference, and GeoDetector analysis to characterize turbidity variability and identify environmental controls. The Voting Regressor achieved the best performance (R² = 0.934, RMSE = 5.221 NTU, MAE = 3.874 NTU, MAPE = 18.618%). New Hydrological Insights for the Region Basin-wide turbidity declined by 32.2% during 2016–2024, reaching a minimum in 2022 followed by a slight rebound in 2023–2024. Turbidity was generally higher during the low-water period than during the high-water period. Spatially, turbidity generally increased downstream but exhibited pronounced heterogeneity. A marked reduction occurred downstream of the TGD, whereas turbidity increased farther downstream in reaches influenced by Dongting Lake. Near the Yangtze–Poyang Lake confluence, turbidity showed a positive correlation with runoff (r = 0.54), contrasting with upstream reaches. Hydrological factors exerted the strongest influence, while meteorological and land-use factors mainly contributed through their interactions with hydrological conditions. These findings underscore the importance of considering reservoir regulation, river–lake interactions, and watershed environmental factors in understanding turbidity dynamics in large regulated rivers.

title: Beyond the Ca–HCO₃ facies: Multivariate identification of hydrogeochemical subsystems in a complex karst aquifer of northeastern Hungary
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Márta Czuppon-Lázár, József Kovács, Kinga Hips, Péter Dobosy, József Stieber, Lóránt Bíró, György Czuppon
abstract: Study region The Aggtelek Karst of northeastern Hungary, part of the transboundary Gömör–Torna Karst system, is one of the most important carbonate aquifers in Central Europe. Study focus This study investigates the hydrochemical and stable water isotope characteristics of 27 springs to identify hydrogeochemically coherent groundwater groups and evaluate the factors controlling groundwater variability. Combined Cluster and Discriminant Analysis was applied to major-ion and stable water isotope data and interpreted within the geological framework of the aquifer. New hydrological insights for the region Seven statistically robust hydrogeochemical groups were identified, demonstrating that the Aggtelek Karst is not a hydrochemically uniform carbonate aquifer despite the predominance of Ca–HCO₃ waters. The differences among the groups are associated with variations in carbonate lithology, particularly the relative influence of limestone and dolomitic units, variable contributions from non-carbonate and evaporite-bearing lithologies, and heterogeneity in hydrogeological setting and groundwater-flow conditions. Importantly, hydrochemical similarity is not determined primarily by geographical proximity: springs from different parts of the karst may belong to the same group, whereas geographically close springs may show distinct hydrogeochemical characteristics. The results demonstrate that conventional facies-based classifications may underestimate the internal hydrogeochemical complexity of carbonate aquifers. These findings improve the conceptual understanding of groundwater circulation in the Aggtelek Karst and demonstrate the value of integrating hydrochemical, stable water isotope, and multivariate statistical approaches in regional karst investigations.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns of cumulative and lagged drought effects on vegetation dynamics across China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yanan Li, Weiliang Chen, Jiakang Huang, Ying Hu, Nannan An, Chengpeng Ji, Tongchao Le, Xisheng Hu, Jian Li, Gongfu Ye
abstract: Study region China spans strong hydroclimatic gradients, from humid subtropical ecosystems in the southeast to arid and semi-arid ecosystems in the northwest and cold alpine ecosystems on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. We analyzed six major terrestrial ecological zones. Study focus A major challenge is to determine whether vegetation variability is more strongly associated with multimonth accumulated water balance or with antecedent monthly drought conditions across heterogeneous climates and vegetation types. We combined precipitation- and potential-evapotranspiration-derived SPEI at 1–12-month scales with MODIS NDVI, LAI, and GPP from 2001 to 2020. Pixel-wise Pearson correlations identified optimal cumulative and lagged timescales; ∆R max quantified their relative dominance, which was further evaluated across ecological zones, a continuous long-term mean SPEI_12 gradient, and major vegetation types. New hydrological insights for the region Lag-dominant associations covered 61–68% of vegetated China and were concentrated in northern and northwestern regions, whereas cumulative-dominant associations prevailed in humid southeastern China. Cumulative timescales showed an inverted-U relationship and lagged timescales showed a U-shaped response along the long-term mean SPEI_12 gradient, with the longest cumulative integration occurring at intermediate SPEI conditions. Shrublands were predominantly cumulative-dominant (78.3–97.7%), whereas grasslands and croplands were predominantly lag-dominant (67.3–85.7%). These results reveal that vegetation-water-balance coupling is strongly region- and vegetation-type dependent and provide region-specific timescale information for drought monitoring and ecohydrological modeling.

title: Impacts of coal mining subsidence on runoff generation under extreme precipitation: A case study of Xinzhi Coal Mine, Shanxi Province, China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Shengqing Zhang, Zhaoliang Wang, Xiaohui Sun, Li Tang, Ruiqing An, Fengwei Xu, Di Wang
abstract: Study region Xinzhi Coal Mine watershed, Shanxi Province, China, a region experiencing coal mining subsidence and increasingly frequent extreme precipitation events. Study focus This study investigates the disturbance mechanisms of mining-induced subsidence (goaf) on watershed hydrological processes. An integrated methodology was employed, combining physical similarity simulation experiments (1:200 scale) under the 100-year return-period rainfall intensity (94 mm/h), SBAS-InSAR deformation monitoring, and the development of a hybrid machine-learning hydrological model incorporating a time-varying Goaf Impact Factor (GIF flow ). New hydrological insights for the region Physical experiments revealed a three-stage evolution of runoff response post-subsidence: fracture-dominated reduction, gully-development amplification, and stabilized elevated flow. This pattern was formalized in a deformation–runoff coupling model (NSE = 0.942). At the watershed scale, the optimized GIF flow time series, derived from 21-year data, successfully captured this three-stage trajectory, improving reconstructed simulation NSE from 0.561 to 0.683. Because GIF flow is identified retrospectively from each year's observed discharge, this watershed-scale analysis is best regarded as a diagnostic reconstruction of goaf hydrological disturbance rather than an independent out-of-sample forecast. The results nonetheless indicate that goaf evolution dynamically re-routes hydrological pathways and can critically amplify flood peaks during gully-development stages, providing a mechanistic basis for assessing flood risks in similar mining-affected watersheds under extreme climate.

title: Hydrology-driven chemical weathering and CO 2 consumption in a mixed-lithology karst river system
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Keyi Wang, Benjamin Chetelat, Jun Zhong, Wang Zheng, Man Gao, Wengang Liu, Fen Huang, Hongming Cai, Wei Yuan, Ning Ma, Jiubin Chen
abstract: Study region The study region is the Maocun subterranean river catchment, a typical mixed‑lithology karst system in Guilin, Southwest China. The goal is to characterize chemical weathering in karst regions that may shape river chemistry and play a crucial role in the global carbon cycle. Study focus The complex hydrogeochemical processes involved in solute transport and dissolution-reprecipitation often obscure the original weathering signals, hampering accurate estimation of chemical weathering intensity, CO2 consumption rate, and their impact on the hydrochemistry. To address these, we quantify solute sources, evaluate secondary calcite precipitation impacts, and how seasonal hydrology modulates weathering rates and carbon sink dynamics. New hydrological insights for the region Our results, together with a Bayesian mixing model integrated with radiogenic Sr isotopes (87Sr/86Sr) and the cation-normalized ionic ratios reveal carbonate weathering dominates cationic load (~62%) across the catchment, while silicate weathering contributes 65% of cations only in the silicate-dominated headwater. Secondary calcite reprecipitation increased downstream, along with distinct spatial variations in hydrochemistry and isotopes. Interestingly, the highest carbonate (CWR) and silicate (SWR) weathering rates both occur during floods, confirming discharge co-regulates weathering intensity and CO2 consumption. Our findings demonstrate that rock chemical weathering is a major source of riverine solutes of this region, clarify the regulatory role of seasonal hydrology in chemical weathering, and emphasize the necessity of correcting for secondary carbonate precipitation to improve the accuracy of carbon sink estimation, especially in carbonate-oversaturated river systems.

title: Deep generative modeling of groundwater level dynamics using a conditional LSTM-WGAN-GP architecture
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Mohammad Nazeri Tahroudi
abstract: Study region This study focuses on the Doroud–Borujerd Plain aquifer in Lorestan Province, western Iran. Monthly groundwater level data from 25 monitoring wells were used for model development and evaluation. The region is characterized by increasing water demand, climate variability, and hydrogeological heterogeneity that have intensified pressure on the aquifer system. Study focus This study aims to develop and evaluate a novel deep learning framework, termed Conditional LSTM-WGAN-GP, that integrates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with a Conditional Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network using Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) for monthly groundwater level forecasting. The proposed architecture is designed to simultaneously capture temporal dynamics and probability distributions by conditioning the generator on historical observations. Predictive performance was assessed using four widely adopted hydrological indicators: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Coefficient of Determination (R²), Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE), and Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE). In addition to statistical metrics, time-series comparisons, scatter plots, and density distribution analyses were employed for comprehensive evaluation. New hydrological insights for the region During the independent testing period, the proposed model achieved a mean RMSE of 1.55 m, R² of 0.69, NSE of 0.47, and KGE of 0.70 across the 25 wells. The model demonstrated satisfactory performance in 13 out of 25 wells (NSE ≥ 0.50), although performance varied across locations due to local hydrogeological heterogeneity. The results demonstrated that the proposed model successfully reproduced the temporal dynamics and statistical distribution of groundwater levels across most wells. Stable convergence of the adversarial training process confirmed the effectiveness of the Gradient Penalty strategy in improving optimization stability, while the LSTM component effectively captured seasonal and long-term dependencies. The close agreement between observed and simulated groundwater levels indicates that integrating temporal sequence learning with adversarial distribution learning provides a robust framework for groundwater forecasting in the region.

title: Impact of drainage channel network on hydrologic and hydraulic responses over the entire basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Ryutaro Otsuka, Kengo Ohno, Yasuo Nihei
abstract: Study region The Ichinomiya River basin, Chiba Prefecture, Japan Study focus Flood disasters caused by heavy rainfall are becoming severe and frequent worldwide, making it essential to understand the hydrological dynamics across river basins. While drainage channel networks are important for constructing numerical models, research on the impact of channel configuration on river water level, discharge and basin water balance during large-scale flooding is lacking. This study aimed to determine the locations of multiple drainage channel networks, clarify how their configuration conditions affect the hydrological and hydraulic dynamics, and examine the network conditions required for numerical analysis. To achieve this, we conducted coupled rainfall–runoff, river flow, and inundation flow simulations for the basin using multiple drainage channel networks, targeting a large flood event. New hydrological insights for the region This study revealed that channels play a crucial role in basin water balance by promoting stormwater drainage and increasing river water volume and downstream cumulative discharge, demonstrating the importance of channel setting in basin hydrological and hydraulic dynamics. Furthermore, the upstream drainage area threshold A min for channel setting exhibited an appropriate range (0.1–0.2 km2) for the Ichinomiya River basin, based on channel-network reproducibility and water-level accuracy. This range is specific to the investigated basin and flood event, and its transferability requires further testing. The results demonstrate that channel setting considering basin topography can improve model performance.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of blue-green water in a humid basin: Covariation with ENSO and underlying drivers
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Junjie Liu, Cuishan Liu, Guoqing Wang, Qixiao Zhang, Peng Liu, Wenjie Liu
abstract: Study region The Xiangjiang River Basin, a typical humid basin. Study focus Blue-green water responses to climate anomalies and their underlying driving pathways remain insufficiently understood in humid basins. In this study, a jointly calibrated hydrological model and Bayesian ensemble algorithm were used to investigate spatiotemporal dynamics of blue-green water in the Xiangjiang River Basin from 1981 to 2020. On this basis, we assessed the covariation of blue-green water with ENSO, a key driver of climate anomalies. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied to further quantify the effects and pathways driving blue-green water variations. New hydrological insights for the region Abrupt changes in the seasonal and trend components of green water storage (GWS) and blue water (BW) largely coincided with the occurrence periods of typical ENSO events, whereas no credible changepoint was detected for green water flow (GWF). GWS and BW showed stronger positive responses to ENSO, with correlation coefficients of 0.52 and 0.60 (both p 0.6). Temperature indirectly affected blue-green water via vegetation dynamics and dry-wet conditions. These findings provide useful evidence for water resources management under anomalous climate conditions.

title: Approximating FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference evapotranspiration with a wind-augmented Hargreaves–Samani model across the Czech Republic
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Lukas Pospisil, Viktor Dubovsky, Dagmar Dlouha
abstract: Study Region: The Czech Republic, represented by 1301722 daily observations from 171 meteorological stations during 2000–2025. Study Focus: FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference evapotranspiration (FAO-PM) requires inputs that are often unavailable. We developed a four-parameter wind-augmented Hargreaves–Samani model (HS-WA) combining a calibrated temperature–radiation baseline with an additive temperature-derived demand term and a bounded, concave wind response. HS-WA was compared with the original and calibrated Hargreaves–Samani equations and a recalibrated Cobaner wind correction using full-data calibration, 100 random hold-outs, 11 rolling-origin temporal tests, 30 station-blocked tests, and station-level regional analyses. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: HS-WA achieved full-data RMSE, MAE, and correlation of 0.409 mm day − 1 , 0.299 mm day − 1 , and 0.965, outperforming the recalibrated Cobaner model ( 0.435 mm day − 1 , 0.312 mm day − 1 , and 0.960). It retained lower RMSE and MAE and higher correlation in every random, temporal, and station-blocked split, and reduced station-specific RMSE at 164 of 171 stations. Its normalized wind response closely reproduced the data-conditioned aerodynamic wind-response shape embedded in FAO-PM, whereas the linear Cobaner multiplier matched it less closely. Cobaner nevertheless often produced smaller absolute bias, revealing a criterion-dependent trade-off between daily accuracy and mean offset. HS-WA therefore provides a robust regional reduced-input surrogate for daily FAO-PM approximation where temperature and wind observations are available.

title: Three-dimensional semi-analytical solution of variably saturated flow due to recharge from ephemeral streams in arid regions
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Sima Tavakkoli, Hadi Jafari, Mohammad Mahdi Sedghi, Rahim Bagheri
abstract: Study Region Arid regions of Iran and other Middle East countries. Study Focus Ephemeral stream infiltration constitutes the principal process of aquifer recharge in arid regions, particularly in the Middle East. Despite recent advances in mathematical modeling, no analytical solutions exist for three-dimensional saturated-unsaturated flow in unconfined aquifers recharged by ephemeral streams of arbitrary geometry. This paper presents a new semi-analytical solution that couples the Richards equation with the saturated groundwater flow equation, considering the continuity of pressure and vertical flux at the water table. The solution for a point-source recharge was derived using Laplace and Fourier transforms, and then stream recharge was simulated by integrating the solution along the stream path and combining the results via the principle of superposition. New Hydrological Insights The proposed model showed that the thickness and constitutive exponent of the unsaturated zone significantly control the spatiotemporal evolution of groundwater recharge mounds. Increasing the thickness of the unsaturated zone reduces groundwater mounding and delays the mound peak, particularly when saturated vertical hydraulic conductivity is low. The complex effects of variations in the constitutive exponent of the unsaturated zone, along with the influence of saturated zone parameters on the development of groundwater recharge mounds, were also examined. Validation of the result against a previous solution confirmed the accuracy of the proposed approach. This research offers a robust tool for the sustainable management of groundwater resources in arid and semi-arid regions.

title: Disentangling the effects of Three Gorges Dam operation and post-dam channel evolution on flood stages along the middle and lower Yangtze River
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Ran Gu, Yang Xiao, Taotao Zhang, Chen Xu, Jiaming Liu, Carlo Gualtieri
abstract: Study region The middle and lower Yangtze River (MLYR), spanning ~1800 km from the Three Gorges Dam (TGD) outlet at Yichang to the East China Sea, China. Study focus Flood responses to large dams are spatially heterogeneous, while the contributions of short-term regulation and long-term channel evolution remain poorly quantified. Using the 2020 flood as a common reference, we attribute specific-gauge flood-stage change to TGD operation and channel-form evolution between the 2010 and 2020 surveys. A 2D Delft3D model with baseline, operation-only, channel-evolution-only, and combined scenarios separates the two effects and quantifies their non-additivity. New hydrological insights for the region For the 2020 flood and under a fixed-lumped-resistance assumption, the 2010–2020 channel-form change is the leading control on specific-gauge flood stages, lowering them by 0.03–1.85 m (an upper-bound, geometry-only estimate because bed coarsening is not modelled). The residual effect of TGD operation on the stage–discharge relationship is small (within 0.34 m), whereas the operation strongly reshapes the flood hydrograph: the peak discharge is reduced by up to 2.85 × 10⁴ m³ s⁻¹ and the peak stage by up to 5.29 m. The interaction term is generally small but is threshold-sensitive and is interpreted primarily as a non-additivity diagnostic. The framework, rather than the Yangtze-specific magnitudes, is transferable to other regulated rivers under comparable data and boundary-condition settings.

title: Evaluating inland flood mitigation capacity under extreme rainfall conditions
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yangguang Song, Shi Shen, Changqing Song, Lin Yue
abstract: Study Region Henan Province, central China, is a representative inland monsoon region in the Yellow River–Huai River transition zone, characterized by densely urbanized plains, agricultural lowlands, and vegetated western mountains. The region experienced severe pluvial flooding during the July 2021 Zhengzhou extreme rainfall event. Study Focus Pluvial flooding risks are increasing under climate change and urbanization, yet assessments of flood mitigation capacity (FMC) under extreme rainfall remain limited in inland regions. This study evaluates land-surface FMC, expressed as the runoff-retention ratio, under 24-h rainfall scenarios from 50 to 550 mm using a spatially explicit SCS-CN framework integrating land use, hydrological soil groups, and slope-adjusted curve numbers. Pixel-scale FMC degradation, spatial convergence under extreme rainfall, and urban core–fringe contrasts were analyzed. New Hydrological Insights for the Region FMC decreases nonlinearly with increasing rainfall. The strongest degradation occurs at 0–150 mm, followed by an operational saturation-transition interval at 150–300 mm. Spatial differences in runoff retention converge markedly beyond ~300 mm, reflecting saturation of finite land-surface storage in the SCS-CN framework. Under 0–300 mm rainfall, urban built-up areas showed roughly 0.20 lower R value than non-urban areas, while urban cores exhibited roughly 0.25 lower R value urban fringes. High-FMC areas were concentrated in mountainous, vegetated, and peri-urban regions, whereas low-FMC areas coincided with dense urban cores and low-lying river-adjacent zones.

title: Regional heterogeneity in winter wheat yield responses to compound agricultural drought in the Huai River Basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jiaying Liu, Yonghua Zhu, Haishen Lü, Robert Horton, Yinghao Fu, Yingying Xu, Tingxing Chen, Yiding Ding
abstract: Study region Huai River Basin. Study focus Agricultural drought is a major constraint on crop production and food security, yet its definition remains inconsistent and is often based solely on soil moisture deficits, which cannot fully represent the actual process of crop damage. This study defines agricultural drought as a propagated soil-vegetation drought chain, in which soil drought precedes and is temporally linked to subsequent vegetation drought. From the integrated perspective of occurrence, propagation, recovery, and yield response, we investigate the mechanisms through which compound agricultural drought affects winter wheat yield. New hydrological insights The findings indicate that precipitation is the dominant factor controlling drought recovery characteristics. The observed mean propagation time from soil drought to vegetation drought was approximately 31 days. Propagated compound agricultural drought showed stronger yield relevance than soil drought alone. Huaibei and Luohe showed yield loss probabilities above 20%, increasing by more than 10 %age points under higher C2 exposure. The exposure threshold for a 50% probability of yield reduction varied substantially among regions, with Huaibei and Suzhou showing high sensitivity. Longer and stronger recovery processes were associated with lower yield anomalies, whereas faster recovery was linked to better yield outcomes. These findings suggest that agricultural drought in the HRB should be identified as a propagated soil-vegetation drought chain rather than by soil moisture deficit alone.

title: Meteorological to agricultural drought propagation and vegetation response across China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Dong Liu, Zihan Ma, Liangliang Zhang, Nan Sun, Muhammad Abrar Faiz, Mo Li, Xiaochen Qi, Tianxiao Li, Song Cui, Zhaoqiang Zhou, Muhammad Imran Khan
abstract: Study region This study covers mainland China, spanning the Eastern Monsoon Region, the Northwest Arid and Semi-Arid Region, and the Qinghai-Tibet Alpine Region. Study focus Meteorological drought does not translate linearly into agricultural drought, and lagged vegetation responses remain poorly constrained. We combined Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), satellite solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), and drought diagnostics based on the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) and Standardized Soil Moisture Index (SSMI) to quantify meteorological-to-agricultural drought propagation, drought duration and severity, and vegetation response memory across China. We examined long-term trends and propagation lags, evaluated cumulative and delayed vegetation responses using correlation and wavelet coherence analyses, and used machine-learning attribution to identify the dominant controls on vegetation variability. New hydrological insights for the region Agricultural drought lasts longer and is more severe than the meteorological drought that triggers it, with a duration approximately one month longer, reflecting the drought amplification effect within the soil-vegetation system. Drought propagation time varies significantly across China, with a median lag of 3–5 months, and the longest lags occur in inland semi-arid regions. Vegetation exhibits a pronounced drought memory effect: NDVI and SIF responses lag approximately 5 months behind drought onset. Compared with NDVI, SIF is more sensitive to short-term water stress. In most parts of China, temperature and evapotranspiration dominate vegetation dynamics, while hydrological factors exert a stronger influence in the humid southeastern regions.

title: The influence of spring soil moisture on flood runoff in forest and grassland basins of the Haihe river mountainous region
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): WeiLi Tan, XiaoWei Yang, QingMing Wang, Yong Zhao, Yuan Liu, Shan Jiang, Fan He
abstract: Study region This study focuses on 10 typical basins in the Haihe River mountainous region, where runoff processes have undergone significant changes during the period of vegetation restoration. Study focus Based on hydrometeorological, vegetation, and soil moisture (SM) data from 1983 to 2020, this study analyzes runoff differences and their causes between forest and grassland basins under vegetation restoration. SEM combined with an LSTM was applied to identify the seasonal pathway among vegetation, SM, and runoff, and to quantify the hydrological sensitivity of flood season runoff to spring SM changes in the two basin types. New hydrological insights for the region Compared with the period before 2000, both annual and flood season runoff declined during the later stage of vegetation restoration, but at different rates, indicating a weakening of runoff seasonality. Grassland basins exhibited a larger discrepancy between flood season and annual runoff reductions, reflecting stronger seasonal sensitivity. The analysis indicates that spring SM depletion associated with vegetation restoration persists into the flood season through a SM carryover effect, and this is one of the key factors behind the different flood‑season runoff responses of forest and grassland basins. Compared with forest basins, grassland basins experienced larger spring SM declines and stronger impacts. Based on LSTM control experiments, a unit change in spring SM leads to an approximately 2.87% change in flood season runoff in grassland basins, which is 1.15 %age points higher than that in forest basins, indicating greater hydrological sensitivity.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and scale-dependent similarity of soil moisture on hillslopes in the Mu Us Sandy Land, China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Wande Gao, Xiong Feng, Zhongqiang Jin, Xiuhua Liu, Changchun Shi
abstract: Study region Mu Us Sandy Land, China Study focus This study investigated soil moisture similarity and scale-dependent dynamics on sandy hillslopes using hourly observations from windward and leeward slopes at multiple depths and slope positions. Spearman’s rank correlation was used to assess overall temporal similarity among soil layers. Wavelet coherency analysis was then applied to examine time- and scale-dependent relationships among soil moisture series and between soil moisture and rainfall or potential evapotranspiration. The results were evaluated using correlation coefficients, average wavelet coherence (AWC), percentage area of significant coherence (PASC), and phase relationships. New hydrological insights for the region Soil moisture similarity generally decreased with increasing depth interval. Spearman’s correlation coefficients ranged from 0.394 to 0.9 on the windward slope and from −0.011 to 0.775 on the leeward slope, indicating stronger vertical coupling on the windward slope. AWC and PASC further showed that coherency between surface and deeper layers weakened with depth. Rainfall controlled wet-season soil moisture variability across multiple scales, whereas potential evapotranspiration was more closely related to dry and freeze–thaw periods, especially at 12–24 h scales. Phase relationships indicated delayed vertical infiltration and lateral redistribution toward footslope positions during wet periods.

title: Copula-based joint distribution analysis of the compound drought-fire weather conditions during the 2025 spring large-scale wildfires in Japan
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Chenling Sun, Yoshiya Touge, Ke Shi, Kenji Tanaka
abstract: Study region Japan, focusing on five large-scale wildfires at four locations and representative cities across all prefectures. Study focus This study developed a daily-scale copula framework to characterize compound drought–fire weather conditions associated with five large-scale wildfires in Japan in 2025. Drought was represented by the 3-month Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI3) and soil moisture (SM), and fire weather by effective humidity (EH) and wind speed. The analysis evaluated dependence and compound severity for drought–fire weather variable pairs, quantified pre-fire changes in EH and SM using seven-day rolling slopes, and mapped compound severity at representative locations across all prefectures on key wildfire dates. New hydrological insights for the region Drought–fire weather pairs generally showed weak daily-scale dependence. Several combinations reached severe or extreme levels during both Ofunato wildfires and the Otsuki wildfire, reflecting moisture deficits coinciding with low EH or strong winds. Okayama and Imabari showed compound anomalies of varying severity and rapid prefire declines in EH and SM. On 26 February, severe compound conditions occurred at many representative locations along the Pacific side, indicating that geographically separated wildfires occurred within a broader regional background of concurrent moisture deficits and adverse fire weather conditions. Severe compound conditions during wildfire periods and rapid pre-fire drying may represent complementary aspects of the hydrometeorological conditions associated with large-scale wildfires in Japan.

title: Catchment-dependent runoff-partitioning uncertainty in the near-optimal parameter space: Insights from 62 catchments in Southeastern China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yi Nan, Yan Li, Fuqiang Tian, Jingan Lin, Yao Zhuang, Diego Avesani
abstract: Study region This study was conducted in 62 small- to medium-sized catchments in southeastern China. Study focus Parameter equifinality can be especially problematic when hydrological models are used not only to reproduce streamflow, but also to infer internal runoff-generation processes. We used the semi-distributed THREW model and 10,000 Latin-hypercube parameter sets per catchment to examine how equifinality affects surface-subsurface runoff partitioning. The contribution of subsurface runoff to total runoff was evaluated within the near-optimal parameter space defined by performance rank and by an absolute Kling-Gupta efficiency threshold, and the resulting uncertainty was compared across catchments and related to a parsimonious set of catchment descriptors. The analysis therefore quantifies parameter-conditioned uncertainty in THREW-estimated runoff partitioning under the fixed model structure, input data, and streamflow-evaluation framework. New hydrological insights for the region Near-optimal parameter sets that reproduce streamflow similarly can imply markedly different surface-subsurface runoff partitioning, and the magnitude of this uncertainty varies systematically among catchments in southeastern China. Among the selected first-order catchment descriptors examined, runoff ratio showed the most consistent association with this variability. Higher-QR catchments exhibited a narrower spread in subsurface runoff contribution among the highest-ranked parameter sets, but broader parameter support and greater partitioning variability under a fixed KGE tolerance. Thus, runoff-partitioning equifinality has a catchment-dependent regional structure, and its apparent magnitude depends on how the near-optimal parameter space is defined. These findings identify runoff ratio as a regional signature of where runoff-partitioning inference from streamflow alone is more or less constrained.

title: Quantification of flood-occurrence risks in the middle reaches of the Yellow River under climate and land-use changes
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Qianling Ci, Wenjing Wang, Chuyu Wu, Ying Han, Yuwei Wang, Xingda Chen, Yida Lu, Dan Li, Shuisen Chen, Jinxia Fu
abstract: Study region The study area is the Middle Reaches of the Yellow River (MRYR), China. Study focus Flood-occurrence risk under concurrent hydroclimatic and land-use change remains poorly quantified in the MRYR. We developed an AHP–FCE–GIS framework integrating 19 climatic, hydrological, topographic, and land-use indicators to reconstruct risk evolution during 1990–2020 and project 2050 conditions under SSP1–1.9, SSP2–4.5, and SSP5–8.5. The framework was evaluated using historical flood/non-flood reference locations, ROC–AUC, and spatial-block cross-validation. New hydrological insights for the region Historical FORI showed an overall increase, but the 1990–2000 reconstruction was weakly constrained. Between the better-validated 2001–2010 and 2011–2020 periods, mean FORI increased from 0.494 to 0.578 and the high-risk area from 26.7% to 46.6%. This shift coincided with a 20.2% increase in annual precipitation and a 111.09% expansion of urban land during 2000–2020. Future mean FORI reached 0.520, 0.551, and 0.603 under SSP119, SSP245, and SSP585, respectively. Under SSP585, 59.14% of the basin was classified as high or very high risk, compared with 28.57% under SSP119 and 28.30% under SSP245. Despite the largest annual precipitation increase under SSP119, its overall risk remained lowest, indicating that annual precipitation alone cannot explain future risk. The Yiluo and Wei basins remained persistent hotspots, while SSP585 extended severe risk toward the Fen River Basin and Yellow River mainstream. These findings support spatially differentiated, climate-adaptive basin management.

title: From deterministic to stochastic: A hybrid framework coupling machine learning with Bluecat for probabilistic satellite-based precipitation estimation over Greece
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Nikos Tepetidis, Theano Iliopoulou, Panayiotis Dimitriadis, Ioannis Benekos, Alberto Montanari, Demetris Koutsoyiannis
abstract: Study region: This study focuses on Greece, characterized by complex topography and strong spatial and temporal variability in precipitation variability, which challenge accurate rainfall estimation and hydrological applications. Reliable precipitation data are essential for hydrological modeling, water resource management and rainfall extremes assessment, while satellite products provide extensive spatial coverage but are subject to systematic biases relative to ground observations. Study focus: We develop a hybrid machine learning-stochastic framework for post-processing satellite-derived precipitation using ground-based observations. Daily gauge and Integrated Multi-Satellite Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (IMERG) data for the period 2000–2021 are used to evaluate independent machine learning algorithms and the proposed framework. The stochastic component provides uncertainty estimation, achieving 88.7% coverage at a 90% confidence level. We introduce a method for estimating the output distribution to generate intensity-time scale-return period (ombrian) curves using annual maximum daily rainfall from a denser station network. New hydrological insights for the region: The proposed framework substantially improves satellite precipitation estimates over Greece. The estimated output distribution achieves Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) and Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE) values of 0.99 and 0.96, respectively, compared with 0.78 and 0.65 for the original satellite product. The framework provides accurate precipitation estimates and reliable uncertainty quantification, supporting hydrological modeling, flood frequency analysis and robust Ombrian curve development in regions with complex terrain. By integrating post-processing techniques within the learning pipeline, the proposed method improves accuracy over conventional merging approaches.

title: A water-balance-guided hybrid machine-learning framework for quantifying recharge to assess groundwater depletion in the Southeastern USA
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Fatemeh Saedi, Mukesh Kumar, T. Prabhakar Clement
abstract: Study region Southeastern United States Study focus Groundwater recharge is an important hydrological flux; however, recharge estimation methods used in the literature estimate different types of recharge fluxes. The focus of the current study is to elucidate the distinction between two common recharge estimates, namely water-balance (WB) recharge, which represents water leaking below the root zone, and water-table fluctuation (WTF) recharge, which represents the net amount of recharge reaching the groundwater table. We developed a water-balance-guided hybrid machine-learning framework that first estimates WB recharge and uses it as a predictor to constrain net recharge predictions. Several machine-learning models were evaluated, and a multilayer perceptron (MLP) was selected to be the best-performing model. The new ML-model-derived data are mapped at the HUC12 scale across the Southeastern US. The modeled recharge was then used to quantify groundwater depletion (GWD) levels as the imbalance between recharge and total fresh groundwater withdrawals. New hydrological insights Results show that the net recharge for the region generally ranges from about 10–15% of average annual local rainfall for most of the catchments. Furthermore, estimated GWD levels exhibited noticeable spatiotemporal variability, with cumulative depletion reaching approximately 31 km³ during 2008–2020 with an average annual depletion rate of about 2.5 km³ /year. This study highlights the importance of distinguishing different types of recharge estimates and also demonstrates the need for using net recharge in GWD assessments.

title: A novel hybrid Elk-Eel and grouper optimizer coupled with machine learning for integrated irrigation water quality index prediction and Pareto-optimal monitoring cost reduction
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Mahmoud E. Abd-Elmaboud, Youssef M. Youssef, Mohamed Abdellatief, Mohamed Elkollaly, Mohsen Sherif, Ahmed El-Shafie, Ahmed M. Saqr
abstract: Study region Eastern Nile Delta aquifer, Egypt Study focus Groundwater quality across the Eastern Nile Delta is deteriorating under seawater intrusion and upward Miocene leakage. Irrigation sustainability is at risk. Comprehensive hydrochemical monitoring, however, remains prohibitively costly for many water authorities in the region. This study asks whether machine learning can improve prediction of the Integrated Irrigation Water Quality Index (IIWQI), and whether its input parameters can be safely reduced without loss of accuracy. A novel Hybrid Elk-Eel and Grouper Optimizer (HEEGO) tunes ten machine learning algorithms across 501 wells spanning three aquifer subsystems. A dependency-aware Cost-Weighted Feature Importance (CWFI) framework then ranks parameters for removal, accounting explicitly for those shared across several derived water-quality indices. New hydrological insights for the region IIWQI assessment reveals that 58.3% of sampled wells are unsuitable for irrigation, concentrated where Na⁺-Cl⁻ facies dominate the northern coastal zone. HEEGO improves prediction accuracy by a mean 12.9% in RMSE across the ten algorithms. The central contribution, however, is economic. The CWFI framework identifies a four-parameter monitoring subset, EC, Na⁺, Ca²⁺, and Mg²⁺, that preserves the full eighteen-parameter protocol's accuracy, R²= 0.9851 against 0.9853, with no loss in classification reliability. Per-sample analytical cost falls by 79.5%, saving an estimated $48,597 a year, or $485,970 over ten years, across the 501-well network. Substantial monitoring-cost reductions are therefore achievable without compromising water-quality assessment. For resource-constrained authorities in similarly salinity-affected agricultural aquifers, this offers a practical route toward more frequent and sustainable groundwater surveillance.

title: Stepwise-clustered downscaling of spatiotemporal variations in compound drought-heatwave extremes over the Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zhirui Yang, Ya Zhou, Guohe Huang, Yongping Li, Xiong Zhou, Jiayan Ren, Feng Wang, Yiting Wei, Xinyue Ren
abstract: Global warming is intensifying compound drought-heatwave events (CDHWs), yet coarse-resolution climate models cannot adequately resolve local variations across the complex terrain and monsoon climate of the Yangtze River Basin (YRB). This study developed a Stepwise Clustering Drought-Heatwave Downscaling (SCDHD) framework to downscale daily maximum temperature, precipitation, and potential evapotranspiration at the station scale and project CDHW variations across the YRB and its five climatic regions under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5. Historical evaluation showed that the framework reasonably reproduced the main climate variables and key drought and heatwave characteristics. Under SSP2–4.5, CDHW frequency increased by 0.116 events per decade, with increases of 129.73% and 96.23% in the Semi-Arid Plateau and Semi-Humid Basin, respectively, during 2061–2090 relative to 2031–2060. Under SSP5–8.5, frequency increased initially but declined overall by 0.167 events per decade during 2032–2089, mainly reflecting changes in the Humid Delta, Semi-Humid Plain, and Semi-Humid Hill. In contrast, maximum duration, mean duration, and mean event intensity increased significantly under both scenarios, at rates of 0.978–1.406 days decade⁻¹ , 0.707–1.268 days event⁻¹ decade⁻¹ , and 1.481–4.667 °C·day event⁻¹ decade⁻¹ , respectively, with larger increases under SSP5–8.5. The contrasting changes in frequency, duration, and intensity demonstrate the need for multiple complementary indicators when characterizing future CDHW hazards.

title: SWAT-based analysis of LULC change impacts on hydrology of the Subarnarekha River Basin, India
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Farhin Tabassum, Akhouri Pramod Krishna, Virendra Singh Rathore, C. Jeganathan
abstract: Study region Subarnarekha River Basin (SRB) is a predominantly rainfed, river basin of Eastern India, spanning parts of Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha. Study focus This study examined the impacts of historical and future land use and land cover (LULC) changes on the hydrology of the SRB. LULC maps for the year 2012, 2017, and 2022 were generated from 5.8 m IRS LISS-IV imagery using support vector machine (SVM) classifier. Future scenarios for 2030, 2040, and 2050 were simulated using a multi-layer perceptron-Markov chain (MLP-MC) model. These LULC datasets were integrated into the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) to evaluate hydrological responses. Model calibration and validation using streamflow observations from four gauging stations showed strong performance, with Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency values ranging from 0.72 to 0.90. New hydrological insights for the region Between 2012 and 2022, built-up land, barren land, and agricultural land increased by 79.39%, 14.81%, and 0.89%, respectively, while forest cover and water bodies declined by 5.54% and 17.45%. These changes increased surface runoff (2.56%) and water yield (1.07%) while reducing groundwater flow (1.29%), lateral flow (5.87%), and evapotranspiration (0.77%). Similar hydrological responses are projected under future LULC scenarios, with impacts becoming increasingly pronounced at the sub-watershed scale. These findings support sustainable watershed management in the SRB and provide a framework for assessing hydrological impacts of land-use change in similar monsoon-dominated river basins.

title: Rainfall structure controls soil water transport and recharge along a humid hillslope revealed by stable isotopes
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Haowen Liu, Junliang Jin, Li Guo, Aiming Huang, Ailin Zhan, Yufei Ma, Cuishan Liu, Guoqing Wang
abstract: Study region This study was conducted on a forested hillslope in a humid hilly catchment at the Chuzhou Hydrological Experimental Station, eastern China, where frequent rainfall, seasonal precipitation variability, and complex soil water redistribution occur. Study focus Rainfall temporal structure may influence hillslope soil water transport, mixing, and storage, but remains insufficiently quantified in humid hilly catchments. Event-scale stable isotope observations (δ²H and δ¹⁸O) and high-resolution soil moisture monitoring were combined to investigate soil water dynamics across upslope, midslope, and downslope positions under Uniform, Extreme, and Uneven rainfall patterns. Soil water response, event-water contribution, and active exchange depth were evaluated to clarify rainfall- and hillslope-position controls on infiltration and redistribution. New hydrological insights The active soil water exchange zone was mainly confined to 0–20 cm at the upslope and midslope, but extended to approximately 40 cm at the downslope. Uniform rainfall favored gradual infiltration and longer event-water retention, whereas uneven rainfall promoted rapid event-water transmission but limited storage. The two observed extreme events suggested activation of a larger soil profile and shorter response lags. Their contrasting responses further pointed to a possible influence of intra-event rainfall distribution on event-water retention under high rainfall input. The upslope was characterized by vertical infiltration, the midslope showed possible lateral redistribution, and the downslope exhibited responses consistent with convergence and earlier fill-and-spill behavior. These findings highlight rainfall-structure controls on hillslope soil water partitioning under variable precipitation regimes.

title: Future projections of cryosphere degradation and its hydrological impacts in the upper Bulgan River basin, Altai Mountains
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zehua Chang, Leilei Yong, Yahui Wang, Kang Wang, Batsuren Dorjsuren, Otgonbayar Demberel, Hongkai Gao
abstract: Study region The nested Baitag and Duchinjil catchments in the upper Bulgan River basin, Altai Mountains, western Mongolia, have small glacier coverage and widespread permafrost. Study focus FLEX-Cryo model was used to assess future cryosphere and runoff changes. The model was evaluated using runoff and cryospheric data. Bias corrected projections from 13 CMIP6 models were used separately to drive the model under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5. New hydrological insights for the region Ensemble mean annual runoff shows no significant trend during 2024–2100. Winter runoff increases, summer runoff decreases, and runoff timing advances in both catchments. Under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5 scenario, glaciers persist as remnants in Baitag at the end of the century but disappear in Duchinjil around 2060. At the Duchinjil station, annual maximum snow depth increases while snow cover duration decreases under both scenarios. Permafrost area decreases in Baitag under both scenarios. Mean active layer thickness increases from approximately 2.25 m to 2.95 m under SSP2–4.5 and 3.42 m under SSP5–8.5 by 2099. Summer runoff decreases approximately twice as fast in upstream Duchinjil as in Baitag. Under SSP5–8.5, peak runoff advances by 18 days in Baitag and 38 days in Duchinjil between 2030–2034 and 2090–2094. Hydrological assessments in similar cold and arid mountain catchments should emphasize seasonal runoff changes and runoff timing.

title: Multi-time scale analysis of loess landform evolution for Dongzhi tableland, southwestern Loess Plateau, China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Shuang Yuan, Qiang Xu, Wei Liu, Siming He, Kuanyao Zhao, Xuan Wang, Pinglang Kou, Qi Zhou
abstract: Study region Dongzhi tableland, southwestern Loess Plateau, eastern Gansu Province, China. Study focus The loess tableland has shrunk greatly over the past thousand years, and this trend is expected to continue. Predictions of loess tableland evolution can support the design and implementation of adequate mitigation measures. To address the limitations of generic Landscape Evolution Models (LEMs) in loess regions, this paper establishes a modified LEM tailored for loess landforms. The model incorporates water as an actual flowing medium in real-time computations, capturing the effects of soil creep, soil detachment, sediment transportation, and sedimentation on loess landscape evolution in a relatively simple and practical manner. Field observations validated that the stream incision law could be modified by adjusting the erosion incision index to make it more suitable for loess regions. The evolution processes of two watersheds with different scales were calculated and analyzed with the established loess geomorphic evolution model. New hydrological insights for the region The numerical results show that the loess geomorphic evolution model can effectively describe the process of erosion and expansion of loess gullies. In local areas, the model can also describe the evolution process from loess tableland to loess ridge to loess hill. When the erosion incision index m is less than 0.3, the model can better balance the proportions of lateral erosion and downcutting erosion in loess regions. The parameters that control the rate of erosion in the model were verified using archaeological evidence and data on similar landforms presented in the scientific literature. When the selected gully advance rate is 0.26 m/year, the time accuracy of the model can reach 95.4%. This model may be extended to other loess areas to assess the extent of landform evolution.

title: Quantifying water origin of a Mediterranean urban karst aquifer using storm event typology and high-frequency physicochemical signatures
Estimating multi-decadal groundwater levels using incomplete well records in confined and unconfined aquifers of the southern San Joaquin Valley, California (USA)
Hydrochemistry of confined aquifers in Friuli Venezia Giulia, Italy: Regional patterns, trends, and drivers
abstract: Abstract Confined aquifers are considered to be protected from surface contamination, yet intensive abstraction and long-term land-use pressures may alter their quality, especially in coastal areas. This study characterises the hydrochemistry of the multilayered confined aquifer system of the lower Friulian Plain (NE Italy), where groundwater is extensively exploited and locally affected by anthropogenic stressors. The study combines hydrochemical data from 1996 to 2025 from the monitoring activity of Regional Environmental Protection Agency of Friuli Venezia Giulia (ARPA FVG) and new samples collected in 2024–2025, compiling 1210 samples from 103 wells. The aim is to determine how recharge sources, residence time, and human activities control groundwater quality. Hydrochemical families were identified using major ions, redox-sensitive species, organic micropollutants, stable oxygen isotopes, and multivariate statistics. Three groundwater families were recognised: submodern waters, with hypoxic conditions, low to absent contaminant load and likely associated with recharge dating back to the late Würmian glacial period; modern-pristine waters, which are characterised by oxidising conditions, are SO 4 2− -rich, and show low to absent NO 3 − and pesticide concentrations; and modern-impacted waters, which are similar to the latter but display elevated NO 3 − concentrations, lower pH values, and detectable anthropogenic contaminants. Long-term trends indicate that although NO 3 − concentrations are overall stable or slightly decreasing in shallow aquifers, slowly increasing trends occur in deeper wells and near the margins of the NO 3 − plume, suggesting downward and lateral migration of impacted modern groundwater. Cl − concentrations show no increasing trends in coastal wells, indicating no evidence of active seawater intrusion.

title: Validating a numerical model for calco-carbonic reactive transport in a laboratory-scale fracture analog
abstract: Abstract Calco-carbonic reactive transport controls the dissolution of limestone by carbonic acid, a key process shaping the hydraulic and geochemical evolution of carbonate aquifers. Quantitative understanding of the coupling between flow, transport, and chemical reactions is essential for predicting karstification under variable hydraulic gradients, $$\text {CO}_{2}$$ CO 2 partial pressures, and pH. To support model validation, laboratory experiments were conducted in a 1 m $$^2$$ 2 vertical karst-fracture analog with variable aperture, representing a simplified hydrogeologic fracture domain. Numerical simulations reproduced these experiments under controlled discharge, $$\text {CO}_{2}$$ CO 2 concentration, and acidity. The coupled reactive transport models capture feedbacks between forced convection, diffusion, and density variations, linking reactive interface dynamics with evolving flow fields. Simulated and measured calcium and carbonate ion concentrations showed good agreement, indicating that diffusive transport at the water–limestone interface primarily limited dissolution. Insights from the combined modeling and experimental framework refine laboratory-scale design, improve interpretation of dissolution kinetics, and strengthen the basis for upscaling to field-scale carbonate aquifers. The results enhance prediction of permeability evolution, flow-path development, and $$\text {CO}_{2}$$ CO 2 - $$\text {H}_{2}\text {O}$$ H 2 O -rock interactions in karst systems.

title: Mechanical and chemical rehabilitation of groundwater abstraction wells clogged by iron and manganese precipitates in Finland
abstract: Résumé Le colmatage des puits de captage d'eau souterraine survient généralement lorsque le fer et le manganèse dissous dans l'eau précipitent sur les éléments du puits, entraînant une baisse du débit. En Finlande, ce phénomène est marqué car les sols sont riches en fer et en manganèse, et les aquifères sédimentaires quaternaires recouverts d'argile présentent généralement une carence en oxygène. Une nouvelle approche de réhabilitation des puits, combinant traitements mécaniques et chimiques, a été appliquée à quatre puits de captage d'eau souterraine situés dans des dépôts sédimentaires quaternaires postglaciaires non confinés en Finlande. D'après les analyses par fluorescence X (XRF), les précipités responsables du colmatage étaient composés de Fe₂O₃, SiO₂, MnO et P₂O₅. Les réhabilitations mécaniques et chimiques ont toutes deux permis d'augmenter considérablement les débits (de 68 à 6 692 %) ; même les puits totalement colmatés ont affiché une nette amélioration de leur débit après l'intervention. À l'issue de la réhabilitation mécanique, les crépines des puits présentaient un niveau de propreté modéré. La réhabilitation chimique a permis un nettoyage supplémentaire des crépines, libérant totalement les fentes et réduisant la turbidité. Le traitement chimique a entraîné une augmentation de la conductivité électrique, de la teneur en sulfates ainsi que des concentrations en fer et en manganèse (dissous et totaux) dans l'eau, en raison des réactifs utilisés et de la dissolution du fer et du manganèse contenus dans les précipités. Toutefois, la qualité de l'eau est revenue à ses niveaux initiaux après une journée de pompage suivant le traitement. Cette méthode de réhabilitation est applicable aux puits de captage situés dans des dépôts sédimentaires quaternaires postglaciaires non confinés, au sein d'aquifères constitués de sable et de gravier à forte conductivité hydraulique. Néanmoins, des études complémentaires sont nécessaires pour mieux comprendre le processus de colmatage ainsi que l'applicabilité de ces méthodes de réhabilitation dans des contextes hydrogéologiques et des environnements redox variés.

title: Sustainable groundwater management in coastal areas: Modelling saltwater intrusion dynamics in Muravera, Italy
abstract: Abstract The coastal alluvial aquifer of Muravera, in south-eastern Sardinia (Italy), is affected by intense saltwater intrusion that seriously threatens freshwater supply. As groundwater overexploitation is often the main process controlling saltwater intrusion dynamics, it can strongly exacerbate salinization, making sustainable groundwater management essential to safeguard these resources. Reliable hydrogeological models based on robust datasets are powerful tools to support decision-making. This work develops a variable-density groundwater flow and solute transport model to analyse saltwater intrusion into the coastal aquifer of Muravera. Four simulation scenarios were implemented. The first reconstructs the historical evolution of salinization over the period of 1999–2023, whereas the other three extend the simulations to 2050 to quantify the various effects of different groundwater abstraction practices and to test a mitigation scenario. Two modelling codes were coupled to support the analysis. Groundwater recharge was computed using the Soil–Water-Balance (SWB) code and subsequently used as input to the iMOD-WQ code, which simulates variable-density flow and salt transport using SEAWAT. This coupling explicitly captures temporal and spatial recharge variability, which is often oversimplified in other approaches. The results indicate that groundwater abstractions for rice-field irrigation exerts a stronger influence on salinization dynamics than drinking-water abstractions. The mitigation scenario attenuates groundwater salinization in the plain, providing useful insights for future groundwater-management strategies.

title: Groundwater modeling to evaluate saltwater intrusion and freshening processes identified from hydrochemistry in a coastal groundwater system in Vietnam

Advancing hydraulic conductivity estimation in the Permo-Triassic Sherwood Sandstone Group using borehole NMR logging
abstract: Abstract The Permo-Triassic Sherwood Sandstone Group is an important aquifer in the United Kingdom (UK) for groundwater and geothermal energy applications. Hydraulic conductivity ( K ) is essential for understanding groundwater movement, contaminant and heat transport in aquifers. Pumping test and borehole nuclear magnetic resonance logging (BNMR) were conducted in three boreholes drilled into the Sherwood Sandstone to determine K . BNMR provides information on the water-filled porosity and pore space geometry, and compared to conventional methods, it is an effective way to estimate K at a high vertical resolution. Schlumberger-Doll Research (SDR) and Timur-Coates (T-C) were used to estimate K using the standard empirical constants initially developed for petroleum reservoir applications. K SDR and K T-C were upscaled to the larger volume represented by K pumping for comparison. Both the standard SDR and T-C equations underestimated K by at least two orders of magnitude because of the limited transferability of their empirical constants to shallow groundwater systems, as they were derived for petroleum reservoir rocks rather than near-surface materials. The fits between the K SDR , K T-C and K pumping were optimised using a semi-constrained least-squares approach to obtain a set of site-specific parameters for the Sherwood Sandstone Group. The new K SDR and K T-C estimates, based on site-specific parameters, are within an order of magnitude of the K pumping . This study presents the first reported SDR and T-C constants for the Sherwood Sandstone Group, which may be used to estimate a more reliable NMR-derived high-resolution hydraulic conductivity in other locations where this formation is present.

title: Isotopic assessment of the origin of fresh and saline groundwater in the highly exploited, predominantly fossil Mekong Delta aquifer in Ca Mau, Vietnam
Estimating specific yield from GRACE-based storage change and groundwater levels across India
Mining-induced overburden fracture development and its control on preferential groundwater flow
Hydrochemical differences and origins of karst waters around the Jinan Pluton, North China
abstract: Abstract The periphery of the Jinan Pluton, North China, contains abundant cold-water and geothermal karst resources, constituting a natural observatory for investigating karst water origins and hydrogeochemical evolution. To advance the understanding of the occurrence pattern and origins of karst waters around the Jinan Pluton, a total of 36 samples of karst groundwater were collected and analyzed for hydrochemical constituents via ion chromatography (IC) and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES), and isotopic composition. The results are as follows: (1) Along the south-to-north regional groundwater flow path, cold-water and geothermal karst groundwaters around the Jinan Pluton exhibit significantly distinct hydrochemical types. From shallow cold-water karst (spring water) to deep geothermal karst systems, the hydrochemical types become progressively more complex, accompanied by a continuous increase in the extent of water–rock interaction. (2) Within the geothermal field north of the Yellow River, the observed gradual increase in total dissolved solids (TDS) of geothermal karst water from west to east can be attributed to two main factors. First, the geothermal karst water in the western segment of the geothermal field receives significant recharge from the Yellow River. Second, the karst water level in the eastern segment of Jinan is the lowest across the study area, making it the convergence center of regional karst groundwater flow, which results in a relatively isolated hydrogeological environment with respect to the surface. This study reveals karst water hydrochemical evolution near the Jinan Pluton to guide water resource utilization and protection.

Old water, rapid responses: Process-based hydrogeological domains reveal hydraulic–age decoupling and implications for recharge assessment in a complex aquifer system of the Heuningnes Catchment, South Africa
abstract: Abstract Groundwater-level fluctuations are commonly used as recharge indicators because groundwater-level rises are often assumed to represent additions of recently recharged water to aquifer storage. In heterogeneous, multilayer aquifer systems, this assumption remains uncertain because groundwater-level variations may also reflect hydraulic connectivity, pressure transmission, storage redistribution, and groundwater mixing. Misinterpretation of groundwater-level behavior may consequently bias recharge estimates and groundwater-resource assessments. This study evaluated relationships among groundwater-level behavior, groundwater residence times, and hydrogeological process domains within the Heuningnes Catchment, South Africa. Groundwater hydrographs, tritium-derived groundwater ages, and a domain-based conceptual framework were integrated to investigate spatial variability in groundwater flow and recharge processes. Piston-flow (PF) apparent ages ranged from 0 to 60 years, whereas exponential–piston flow model (EPM)-derived mean transit times (MTTs) ranged from 2 to 80–100 years across hydrogeological domains. Recharge-dominated systems showed strong seasonal groundwater-level responses despite the coexistence of young and broad groundwater-age distributions and highly variable hydrograph responses, reflecting mixed recharge and storage influences. Structurally controlled systems showed rapid hydraulic responses despite prolonged groundwater residence times, suggesting pressure transmission independent of groundwater transport times. Residence-time-dominated systems were characterized by older groundwater and subdued hydrograph responses associated with prolonged storage. Groundwater-level response rate showed a weak and statistically non-significant relationship with MTT (Pearson's r = − 0.307, p = 0.460), demonstrating hydraulic–age decoupling and indicating that recharge assessments based solely on groundwater-level fluctuations may substantially misrepresent groundwater recharge processes in structurally complex multilayer aquifer systems.

title: Evaluating the long-term efficacy of subsurface cutoff walls as a barrier against seawater intrusion in unconfined island aquifers under various climatic-stress scenarios
Seasonal fluctuation of spring outflows in contrasting lithological and geomorphological environments of the western mid-hill region, Nepal
Groundwater potential zoning in the Grande River Basin: A semi-arid region of Northeast Brazil
abstract: Abstract Seasonal water scarcity in western Bahia, Brazil, has led to increased dependence on groundwater resources; however, basin-scale hydrogeological measurements remain insufficient for preliminary assessments. This study presents a geographic information system-based groundwater potential map for the Grande River Hydrographic Basin (GRHB), where groundwater potential is defined as a relative index reflecting conditions favorable for recharge and subsurface storage, rather than a direct measure of aquifer productivity. Ten hydrogeological and terrain proxy layers, derived from existing datasets and remote sensing, were standardized and integrated using an analytic hierarchy process weighting scheme and a weighted linear combination. The resulting index was classified into five groundwater potential categories. The very high- and high-potential classes account for 48.08 and 25.41% of the basin, respectively, while the moderate class accounts for 19.90%, and the low- and very low-potential classes together comprise 6.59%. Spatial association with available well locations was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and the area under the curve, which yielded a value of 0.821, indicating that wells are more frequently located in areas with higher index values. Additionally, a groundwater abstraction-pressure proxy, derived from wells with reported daily abstraction volumes, was used to identify potential stress areas where high favorability coincides with concentrated abstraction activities. These outputs serve as a first-order screening tool to guide field verification, monitoring, and targeted data acquisition across the basin.

Integrating geophysical and underwater robotic surveys with transport and geochemical modeling to assess the Solotvyno salt mine hazard in the Transcarpathia province of Ukraine
abstract: Abstract The Solotvyno salt mine in West Ukraine presents significant environmental and infrastructural risks due to uncontrolled salt dissolution following mine flooding, causing ground subsidence, sinkhole formation, and transboundary contamination of the Tisza River. This study employs an innovative multidisciplinary approach to characterize subsurface conditions and contamination pathways. The UX-1Neo autonomous underwater robotic platform conducted 14 dives in two flooded mine shafts, revealing intact main shaft structures but worrying blockages in horizontal passages, distinct haloclines at different depths (60 m in ventilation shaft 9, 140 m in shaft 10), and evidence of ongoing salt crystallization. Ground geophysical surveys such as electrical resistivity tomography, very low frequency radio-magnetotellurics and horizontal loop electromagnetics identified compromised protective clay layers (“pallag”) and potential air-filled voids, explaining accelerated dissolution and surface deformation. Hydrodynamic and contaminant transport modeling quantified salt fluxes (~ 2000 m 3 /day through “pallag” zones, ~ 13–15 m 3 /day from direct mine leakage) and confirmed dissolution rates of approximately 5.0–5.5 m 3 /day of rock salt, driven by both anthropogenic influences and natural gradients toward the Tisza River. NETPATH mixing models revealed variable contamination throughout the system, with the Black Moor area showing highest vulnerability (up to 27.4% mine water contribution) while the Tisza River maintains relatively good water quality despite measurable contamination (1.97% mine water). The suggested approach provides critical insights into risk assessment and remediation planning, representing a significant advancement in monitoring and managing complex environmental hazards associated with abandoned salt mines.

title: Ascertaining controls on spring discharge: Implications for the revival of drying springs in the Middle Hills region of Nepal
Groundwater occurrence and quality in a hyper-arid desert: Insights from high-resolution electrical resistivity surveys in Tharparkar, Pakistan
abstract: Abstract The Tharparkar District in Pakistan is among the world’s most water-scarce regions, characterized by its hyper-arid climatic conditions and the absence of perennial surface water resources. Understanding the occurrence of groundwater potential and its quality is therefore critical, particularly in remote regions where hydrogeological information remains limited. This study characterized groundwater resources using 576 high-resolution electrical resistivity survey (ERS) probes up to a depth of 300 m, conducted from 2017 to 2020. Complementary hydrochemical investigations included laboratory analysis of 168 groundwater samples collected from dug wells and 672 soil samples up to a depth of 0.60 m. Results demonstrated that the water table lies at depths of 2–15 m (26% of the area), 16–30 m (23%), and 31–90 m (51%). Interpretation of ERS data revealed that approximately 10% of the groundwater resources, covering the southern parts of Diplo, Islamkot, and Nagarparkar Talukas, are suitable for drinking at a depth of 25 m, with around 3% classified as fresh and 7% as slightly saline. Groundwater salinity increases with depth, as 51% of the area shows high salinity at depths of 26–50 m and very high salinity at depths of 51–200 m. Arsenic and fluoride concentrations exceed permissible limits in 10 and 28% of the groundwater samples, respectively. These findings provide robust geophysical and hydrochemical evidence to guide targeted groundwater development, water quality mitigation strategies and inform policy interventions, aimed at enhancing water security and safeguarding the health of communities living in severely water-stressed desert regions.

title: The spatiotemporal evolution and controlling factors of the groundwater environment: Insights from long-term monitoring of Tongzhou District, China
Integrated geochemical characterization and multicomponent modeling for reservoir temperature estimation in the Boğazlıyan Geothermal Field (Central Anatolia, Turkey)
